Sports.title: Man City rivals 'working on' deals to poach players after Premier League guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Man City rivals 'working on' deals to poach players after Premier League guilty verdict

Manchester City are in an uncertain position after an independent commission found them guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against them by the Premier League

View 2 Images Manchester City are appealing after being found guilty of charges (Image: Getty Images)

Premier League clubs are understood to be trying to take advantage of the current uncertainty surrounding Manchester City by making a play for some of their talented academy players.

‌



‌



It emerged last week that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges levied against them by the Premier League, with the damning verdict since being published in full. Heavy sanctions are likely to be imposed upon City if an appeal against the ruling fails which could range from relegation, a transfer ban and potentially even expulsion from the Premier League itself.

‌



While City's right to appeal means an undisputed outcome may still take some time to be reached, the impact of the verdict is already being felt.

‌



Speculation over City's players and what the future may hold is already rife given there is a possibility City may not be playing in the top-flight soon - and it now appears they may risk losing some of their top homegrown talent, too.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



BBC Sport report that Manchester City's rivals are looking to capitalise on the situation the club find themselves in by trying to entice some of their academy stars away.

That could be particularly damaging if City are handed a transfer embargo as part of any potential punishment following an appeal given the majority of their first-team stars would be expected to stay within the Premier League.

Despite the investigation into City, it's understood that the majority of their senior stars do not have relegation clauses written into their contracts. And while City could attempt to play hardball over transfers, they could struggle to foot such a mammoth wage-bill without Premier League cash.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester City players, and some of their academy stars, are expected to attract attention from rivals (Image: Getty Images)

While other punishments have been touted, Gary Neville believes forcing the current owners to sell the club would be the right course of action to take.

Speaking on the latest instalment of Stick to Football, he said: "Points deductions, fines, transfer bans, removing the titles - not giving them to others, just removing the titles - it's significant punishments. The only punishment that would be fair would be have huge consequences - the biggest consequence - would be removing the owners.

"That is the only consequence if I was Manchester City that I would be worried about."

Sports.title: Man Utd flop Rasmus Hojlund SHOVES Portugal manager after Cristiano Ronaldo trolling act
Sports.content:
Man Utd flop Rasmus Hojlund SHOVES Portugal manager after Cristiano Ronaldo trolling act

Rasmus Hojlund performed Cristiano Ronaldo's trademark Siu celebration after scoring Denmark's second goal in their 4-2 Nations League defeat to Portugal in Copenhagen

View 2 Images Rasmus Hojlund had a bizarre encounter with Jorge Jesus after Denmark's defeat (Image: UEFA TV)

Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund was involved in a heated exchange with Portugal manager Jorge Jesus after copying Cristiano Ronaldo’s celebration. The Dane appeared to shove the 72-year-old after the former Benfica boss smacked him on the chest during a bizarre interaction.

‌



‌



Hojlund netted Denmark's second goal on Thursday night, wheeling off before performing Ronaldo's trademark 'Siu' celebration. The manner of the celebration comes amid another bitter dispute involving Red Devils hero Ronaldo after the 41-year-old walked out on international duty.

‌



Ronaldo had been an unused substitute in the 2-1 win over Norway, but he took matters into his own hands, leaving the camp, igniting a rift with Jesus in the early stages of a four-year deal in the hot seat.

‌



It isn't the first occasion that Hojlund has copied Ronaldo's celebration against his country. He scored the decisive goal in 2025 before racing away to perform it.

Portuguese media deliver damning Cristiano Ronaldo verdict as players refuse to discuss him READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

His remarks at the time reveal a degree of allegiance to the former United and Real Madrid icon, suggesting his celebration may well have been a statement directed at Jesus and a show of support for Ronaldo.

‌



Speaking in 2025, Hojlund said: "It's for my idol. It wasn't to mock him or anything. He's had such a huge impact on me and my football career.

"Maybe it's a bit ambivalent but to score against him and Portugal, it's huge. I remember him scoring from a free-kick in 2011, when I went to watch the match, and, since then, I've been a huge Cristiano fan."

Ronaldo was equally gracious in his response, making clear he had taken no offence: "For me, it's not a problem. I know it wasn't an act of disrespect. I'm smart enough to realise that.

‌



View 2 Images Cristiano Ronaldo played no part for Portugal against Denmark (Image: Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images)

"Not only him, all over the world, several athletes celebrate me. For me, it's an honour, but I hope he can see my celebration tomorrow [Sunday]."

Jesus, who only took over from Roberto Martinez in the summer after penning a four-year deal, finds himself under mounting pressure to manage the simmering tensions surrounding Ronaldo.

‌



The veteran forward was left out of the starting line-up in the 2-1 victory over Norway and remained on the bench throughout, a situation that ultimately prompted his announcement about departing the camp early.

The 41-year-old said on social media: "After the press conference of the national team and following a conversation with the president of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

"In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave."

Sports.title: Kevin Blake's Arc day tips: Three fancies on star-studded undercard
Sports.content:
Expert racing pundit Kevin Blake will be in Paris for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe and picks out three fancies on the undercard, all live on Sky Sports Racing.

Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe weekend at ParisLongchamp, live on Sky Sports Racing, is without doubt one of the crown jewels in the world of horse racing.

The feature race at 3.05pm on Sunday is one of the most prestigious races in the sport and the supporting card is dripping with Group 1 races.

With unusually dry weather having prevailed in recent weeks, the racing looks likely to take place on what we would call good ground if not a little firmer.

Sunday's renewal of the Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp Longines (1:47) is perhaps one of the weaker ones in recent years, but one factor that always persists in it is the importance of the draw. A low draw is a significant advantage and for that reason I am favouring the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained SHIRI, who is drawn in stall four.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player William Haggas spoke to Luke Elder ahead of Maltese Cross' run in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe

The daughter of Mehmas has proven to be very progressive in sprints this season, but she has really taken off in her last two starts when dropped back to five furlongs, winning a Listed race at Deauville in great style and finishing just Naana's Shadow too good for her in a Group 3 over this course and distance last time. She can be expected to come forward again and with the draw having been so kind to her, she looks to have a very good chance to run well.

The Prix de l'Opera Longines (3:50) has attracted a very interesting field that features a strong numerical cast of three-year-olds, but the standard is set by the established star in the Christophe Ferland-trained Aventure. However, I think the prize might be taken by an emerging star in the shape of the John and Thady Gosden-trained MISS SCOTT.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maltese Cross bids to back up his Grand Prix de Paris and Great Voltigeur wins in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe

The daughter of Night Of Thunder has been asked to take baby steps in her career thus far, but has responded by finding run-to-run improvement that culminated in her running out the impressive winner of the Snow Fairy Fillies' Stakes at the Curragh last time.

Returning to this slightly longer trip will play to her strengths and she most certainly looks capable of finding further improvement. While a career-best effort will be required for her to trouble an on-song Aventure, it wouldn't be a surprise if she shook her up.

The Qatar Prix de la Foret (4:25) is a sharper test than most appreciate, with the actual distance run over being slightly shorter than the advertised seven furlongs and a fair portion of the distance is run on a downhill bend. With the ground being firmer than it often is for this meeting, speed will be tested more so than stamina and for that reason the one I am favouring is the Fozzy Stack-trained THESECRETADVERSARY.

The son of St Mark's Basilica is unbeaten in his three starts at trips shorter than a mile this season including the Jersey Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Prix Jean Prat at Deauville. While his copybook has been blotted by three defeats in Group 1 races over a mile among those wins, don't let that distract from his effectiveness over these shorter trips. This course and distance promises to suit him ideally and he looks to have an excellent chance.

Sports.title: Mezcala fancied to scoop Challenge Cup prize
Sports.content:
After putting their collective support behind Daryz for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, the Weekend Winners panel turned their attention to Ascot's Challenge Cup.

A maximum field of 18 runners have assembled for the heritage handicap contest over seven furlongs, with Thunder Call the early market favourite for the William Haggas team.

Moonfall is in opposition for the Billy Loughnane and George Boughey combination, alongside Royal Ascot winner Mezcala.

Watch the race from Ascot - live on Sky Sports Racing - at 3.35pm on Saturday.

Sam Boswell...

"It lives up to its name, this Challenge Cup, because it's not easy! I thought Thunder Call was mightily short at 11/4, I respect his chances but didn't want to playing [at the price]. I thought I'd take a bit of a swing here. It's interesting that in these types of races Richard Spencer has gone through the season and done pretty well in them. He's gone a bit quiet recently but he's got two here, Hawksbill and Two Tribes - who I was most interested in.

"He's kicking around the 20/1 mark but this horse's form at Ascot is there for all to see. He was second in the International off one pound lower and that is the piece of form that stands out for me. He's just a really good horse and he's got Toby Moore booked, who will take a handy seven off - which will be really key to his chances. The less said about Ayr the better but [in the International] he had Extremely Zain behind in fourth, who has come out and won again since at York in good fashion.

"It could be a case of a race too many for him but I thought Toby Moore's booking was eye-catching and I'd hope he can run into the places."

Declan Rix...

"It's "once more unto the breach dear friends" with Mezcala. I just hope that Port Master runs because I don't see loads of pace in the race and it could get a little bit messy. We shouldn't forget they rail off the straight track to keep it fresh for Champions Day [at this meeting] and even though they do that and it's a smaller field than usual, they can split in two - so we'll see.

Image: Mezcala returns to Ascot this weekend

If he comes back to this form from the Buckingham Palace Stakes he's got a wonderful chance. The race set up nicely for him down the rail, he got plenty of cover and he did all of his best work late. He maybe got a little bit lucky that the runner-up was idling a touch but if he comes back to this form, he's going to go close. He ran at the Leger meeting and under the circumstances he ran really well. George Bass needs to get this guy covered up."

Kate Tracey...

"I'm also keeping the faith with Mezcala here and hoping that all goes well for him. That Doncaster run last time - I thought it was fair enough. Low draws came to the fore that day and he was in 14 with the running style also not helping. I did also feel that he was perhaps found wanting off that mark of 98 and he's been generously given 1lb back now!

"He's still above his Royal Ascot-winning mark but back to this track and trip and with his old pal George Bass on, I like him at 15/2."

Watch Weekend Winners in full on the At The Races YouTube channel.

Sports.title: Man City lodge appeal against guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission finding them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City insist in their statement they are "innocent" and have described the judgement against them as "opinion" and claimed it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Man City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rob Dorsett reports that two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs would be 'amazed' if 15 clubs would vote to expel Manchester City

The Premier League club had until Friday to appeal and confirmed they had done so in a statement just before midday.

In a statement on Friday, the club said: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

"The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

The statement from Man City again erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

City are a member of the Premier League and have signed up to the rules regarding disciplinary process.

How is the independent commission chosen? The three-person panel is chosen from members of the Judicial Panel that has been established by the Premier League.

The members of the Judicial Panel, comprising a number of legal, financial and other experts, are selected by its independent chair.

The chair also selects which members of the Judicial Panel sit on commissions, which are independent of the Premier League.

Appeal boards are also appointed by the chair of the Judicial Panel and must have three members.

One of those individuals should have held judicial office, and would be the chair of the appeal board.

The three-person tribunal took almost two years to write the judgement. The Premier League investigation started eight years ago and City were charged three-and-a-half years ago.

Later on Friday, the Premier League confirmed City's appeal had been lodged.

The statement added: "The club lodged the appeal to the Chair of the Judicial Panel.

"The independent Appeal Board hearing will remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted."

Analysis: How long will the appeal take?

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol:

"The appeal went in on Thursday at 7pm and so, according to the Premier League's rules, the appeal has to be done and dusted in 12 weeks from then, which takes us into the week before Christmas.

"The appeal can only last five days and those five days can only be in one block.

"The appeal panel, which has to be a different three-person panel from the original panel, would have 30 days to make up their minds and deliver their judgement. That would take you into the third week of January.

"Now that is the speeded-up timeline which has been introduced into the Premier League's rules this season.

"Now, Man City could argue that this speeded-up timeline should not apply in this case because this case has been going on for years and this new rule has only been introduced this season. That is something to look out for."

Details of Man City's appeal strategy explained

Latest from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas:

Manchester City are likely to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, Sky Sports News understands.

City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the independent commission, which "concluded it was an explanation that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".

However, it is understood City are expected to continue contesting this argument.

Manchester City is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Newton Investment and Development LLC. Sheikh Mansour is also a member of the ruling family of Abu Dhabi and he is the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The separation of UAE state investment and those that are private from the Abu Dhabi royal family has long been a subject of debate and criticism.

What did the independent commission find?

Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.

Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.

Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven

The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.

City: Process was not impartial

Following the publication of the guilty verdict, a Manchester City statement released on Tuesday read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

As above, Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

Why Man City's appeal could drag into 2027

Latest from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol and Amar Mehta:

Manchester City's appeal could drag on into next year if they argue that the process should not be run according to Premier League rules which were introduced for this season.

City have filed their appeal and the new rules about appeals state that this part of the disciplinary process has to be concluded within 12 weeks and the appeal hearing can last no longer than five days.

City's lawyers could argue that they were charged in 2023 and a hearing was held in 2024 - when the rules about a speeded-up appeals process were not in the Premier League Handbook.

A legal expert told Sky Sports News Manchester City would have a strong case for arguing that the new rules should not apply in this case.

The new rules were introduced to ensure that clubs, where possible, were punished in the same season as relevant rule breaches.

Sports.title: Vasseur admits 'big issue' with Ferrari distractions
Sports.content:
Frederic Vasseur says the "noise" surrounding Ferrari is a "big issue" for the team, admitting their release of a statement earlier this week reiterating the Italian outfit's faith in him had become "mandatory".

Vasseur said after last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix that the team were "not working in perfect serenity" amid persistent and "frustrating" rumours around his position at the Scuderia.

The Italian media have speculated over Vasseur's future in recent weeks amid links that Christian Horner would consider joining the team.

"When you see the noise and all the rumours in the press all the week, I think as a team we need to work in serenity, and it was absolutely not the case," said Vasseur.

"I think the statement was mandatory to do something, or it would have been the same this weekend.

"But honestly, the big issue that we have today is the stability, the serenity in the team, the focus that we need to have, and not to have this kind of question all the day."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Williams team principal James Vowles backs Fred Vasseur in a press conference after speculation surrounding the future of his Ferrari counterpart.

Vasseur, who joined Ferrari as team principal from Sauber in 2023, has overseen their return to race-winning ways this year after a poor 2025 but their world championship challenge to Mercedes has faded in recent months amid a five-race run without a podium finish.

The 58-year-old, who signed a multi-year contract extension last season, called for a more "friendly media".

"When you take the role, the positive and the negative side of the job. I was expecting something like this," said Vasseur.

"What is sometimes a bit unfair is when you put someone under the bus, and I'm there also to defend my team, my guys.

"When we are winning, we are winning as a team, but when we are struggling, I'm there to defend all of them. I think it's the right attitude from everybody, from them to defend the team principal, from me to defend them when we are struggling.

"Honestly, I knew what I would get on that. I'm not surprised at all, but sometimes the attacks are a bit personal. It's not good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ahead of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Lewis Hamilton shares his confidence in Fred Vasseur despite 'negative' outside sources.

Vasseur: I can't complain about the organisation

Lewis Hamilton passionately defended Vasseur ahead of this weekend's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but pointed to Ferrari's structure in the team and whether it needed to be changed.

It was unclear whether Hamilton's comments were about the top end of Ferrari, including chairman John Elkann and chief executive Benedetto Vigna, or people below Vasseur.

Asked about Hamilton's comments and the Ferrari structure, Vasseur said: "The relationship that I have with my bosses, Benedetto and John, is a very good one.

"We are in daily contact, and I can't complain at all about the organisation. But for sure, you always want to get more, you always want to do more, you always want to recruit more too.

"But I think it's true for me and it's true for everybody on the grid, that you always want to do more because it's the DNA of what we are doing. But honestly, it has nothing to do with the organisation."

Sports.title: Bentley to fight Mosley Jr on November 7 live on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
Middleweight world champion Denzel Bentley has signed a multi-fight deal with Zuffa Boxing and will fight on November 7 at the Copper Box Arena, live on Sky Sports.

Battersea's Bentley takes on quality American middleweight Shane Mosley Jr on the loaded ZUFFA BOXING 12 bill headlined by Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke.

Tickets are available now via Ticketmaster.

Bentley is a world-class middleweight who became the WBO champion after his tough victory over Endry Saavedra at London's O2 arena in April.

In a hard-fought battle with Saavedra, Bentley came back to take out the dangerous Venezuelan with a strong seventh-round finish.

That saw him win the WBO Interim title which was later upgraded to full world championship.

Image: Bentley has proved himself a force a world level. (Erik Verduzco/Las Vegas Review-Journal via AP)

Bentley has had to battle his way through adversity. A former British champion, he lost his first world title fight when he challenged Zhanibek Alimkhanuly. He then bounced back from a surprise loss to Nathan Heaney, beating Danny Dignum, Derrick Osaze and Brad Pauls to set himself up for the Saavedra bout.

"That's an achievement ticked off, that's one of my goals. I can leave the sport knowing that I was a world champion. But now it's time to try and achieve more and raise my potential. I don't think many people tipped me to be a world champion when I first started," Bentley told Sky Sports.

"I didn't really know if I could even get a chance to compete for one rather than actually win one.

"It's the highest accolade in the sport so you have to do a lot to get there but I just bit down and went through the process and made it there."

Mosley Jr is the son of boxing legend Shane Mosley. He is also coming off an outstanding win in his last fight when he halted strong Ukrainian fighter Serhii Bohachuk in six rounds in Las Vegas.

The American has fought at the highest level, beating former world champion Daniel Jacobs and missing out on the WBC Interim title when he boxed Jesus Alejandro Ramos last year.

Additional information on the event will be announced in the coming weeks.

Bentley: I'm still champ

While Mosley Jr is not Bentley's mandatory challenger but is ranked No 6 with the WBO.

Bentley told Sky Sports News: "I'm very game. I like to have a fight. I've got a very good knockout ratio, you can expect knockouts. Most importantly I am still currently the WBO middleweight champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Shane Mosley Jr produced the performance of his career as he floored Serhii Bohachuk in the sixth round before forcing an impressive stoppage win.

"I know everything that's gone on online and all the rumours [that he could be stripped of belt]. My team has put in an appeal, that appeal has gone through. We are hoping that we can get through this appeal and we get to defend this WBO title against a game, ranked opponent too.

"The son of a legend, he's there with a chip on his shoulder, trying to prove everyone wrong who believes he can't be as successful as his dad. So he's very dangerous. He's got real motivation and he's going to come in there and put on a great fight."

McKenna a future target?

There will be intriguing possibilities for the Bentley-Mosley Jr victor. Aaron McKenna laid down a marker for the middleweight division when he beat Etinosa Oliha to win the IBF title.

Bentley can consider McKenna a future target, if he comes through his November 7 clash with Mosley Jr.

"I think me and Aaron, the winner of that will be the No 1 in the division," Bentley said.

"If we are the ones making a noise in this division, you can't help make the winner of that fight No 1, rather than looking at [Carlos] Adames or [Erislandy] Lara and looking at their past performances and what they've done in the past and using that to make them No 1.

"We can put the middleweight division back on the map."

Sports.title: Leclerc tops second practice in Malaysia but Red Bull impress
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc was fastest in second practice for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but Red Bull impressed during Friday's running.

Leclerc was 0.099s quicker than Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, with McLaren's Lando Norris only 0.137s behind in a tight session which suggests four teams will have a shot at pole come qualifying on Saturday at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event.

Max Verstappen was fourth but only 0.257s slower on the mediums, unusually deciding to not do a qualifying simulation on the softs.

Given Verstappen topped first practice and generally is quicker than Hadjar, he likely had the pace to also top second practice but chose to focus on long-run pace as tyre degradation was a major issue around the hot, high-speed Sepang International Circuit.

Red Bull's race simulations were also strong on Friday so Verstappen could have a big chance at a first pole position of 2026 and, with it, a first win of the season.

"I think we had a decent start. The track is tricky, it's really hot, a lot of degradation and so a lot of things to figure out. But it has been positive," said Verstappen, who won the last F1 race in Malaysia in 2017.

Image: Max Verstappen did not top second practice but had an impressive day (Red Bull Content Pool)

Lewis Hamilton was three tenths slower than his team-mate in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

Hamilton was investigated for blocking Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto when he veered across onto the racing line on a slow lap down to Turn Nine. Stewards issued the Hamilton with a warning and imposed a €10,000 (£8,503) fine on the team for not telling the Briton - whose car had a damaged mirror - over the radio that the Audi, on an out lap, was fast closing behind him.

Meanwhile Mercedes had one of their most difficult Fridays this year, despite introducing their biggest upgrade package to the car since May's Canadian Grand Prix.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton is under investigation from the stewards for allegedly impeding Gabriel Bortoleto

George Russell and Kimi Antonelli set their best lap times on the mediums after both had scruffy laps on the softs, but were not lighting up the sectors with quick times before their mistakes in the last sector.

Antonelli ran wide at the penultimate corner while Russell went deep at the final corner and was forced to take to the pit lane.

It was thought Mercedes would dominate this weekend with their upgrades, which include a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner but Red Bull appear to be the team to beat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Bernie Collins takes a look at Mercedes upgrades as they head into the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

"With these conditions, tyre deg is huge for everybody and the cars are operating in a very different window," said Russell, who is 66 points behind Antonelli in the Drivers' Championship.

"I think, as a team, we just haven't got the car quite where we need it to be. We need to make some set-up adjustments. We're a bit off the pace."

Elsewhere, it was confirmed on Friday that Hadjar has received a five-grid place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, Alpine's Franco Colapinto has a 10-grid place penalty for a new engine, on top of his five-grid place penalty for causing a collision last time out in Baku, and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad will start at the back for a complete power unit change.

Sports.title: Manchester City lodge appeal as FA warns of major implications for integrity of game: football news – live
Sports.content:
From 4h ago 06.47 EDT Manchester City appeal confirmed by Premier League Manchester City have lodged an appeal against the findings of an independent commission regarding breaches of Premier League financial rules, it has been confirmed. “The club lodged the appeal to the Chair of the Judicial Panel,’ said a Premier League statement. “The independent Appeal Board hearing will remain private and confidential until publication of the outcome is permitted.” A statement on Manchester City’s website, meanwhile, states: “Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter. “The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe. “The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. “We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.” Share Updated at 06.58 EDT

6m ago 10.54 EDT Juan in Salford gets in touch: “Everyone seems to think this is all over; are we not allowing for the possibility that City’s appeal is successful and all charges are dropped?” It’s entirely possible and the damage done is already heavy whatever the outcome. Share

12m ago 10.48 EDT Rick Harris gets in touch, offering a strong opinion: “I believe I am correct in saying that under the Football Governance Act 2025, every club operating a team in a specified competition is required to hold an operating licence issued by the Independent Football Regulator, and that all professional footballers have to be registered with the FA in order to be able to play in the various leagues and cup competitions. “In most walks of life if you were accused of serious professional misconduct your employer or professional regulatory body would suspend you at the very least pending the outcome of a court case, so in my opinion the IFR should immediately suspend Manchester City until the end of the present season and the PL should declare the 5 games already played to be null and void. Instead of a 38 game season we will have a 36 game one and City’s last Carabao Cup opponents will be reinstated in their place in the next round. “If City lose their appeal then the current owners should be declared unfit and improper persons and the club ejected from professional football in England. The IFR should then invite the formation of a 100% supporters owned club along the lines of Barcelona and that new entity should be invited to apply to an appropriate level of the football pyramid consistent with it’s financial resources and ability to engage players and coaching staff etc. “It is simply inconceivable that City can stay in the PL or complete this seasons fixtures following the guilty verdicts on almost all the charges brought against them.” Share

14m ago 10.47 EDT World Cup final winning goalscorer Ferran Torres has withdrawn from the ⁠national squad with an ankle issue and will be replaced ⁠by Carlos Espi. Coach Luis de la Fuente called up Espi in his place, rewarding the Real Madrid youngster after he scored five goals and set ‌up two more in Spain Under-21s’ 13-0 rout of San Marino ​on Thursday. Share

21m ago 10.39 EDT Bloomberg are running a story on Manchester City and Abu Dhabi. double quotation mark Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak met a senior UK government minister to discuss the UAE’s investments in Britain just days before the club’s guilty verdicts were announced. Al Mubarak asked to meet Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds on 14 September in his capacity as CEO of Mubadala Investment Company, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund, sources tell Bloomberg. The pair held a private meeting in Downing Street on that date, the people said. Al Mubarak talked about current and future UAE investment in Britain, they said. Share

25m ago 10.36 EDT As part of his England press conference, Jordan Pickford talked of his role as backup goalie. Another Brighton man, Jason Steele, is the exemplar of that from the summer. Pickford said: ““It is not often I do that. The manager told me the reasons why. It was good for me to see where I’m at. It’s about me being a good team-mate with good energy around the place and train well and have that leadership role. I think I’ve done it really well over the last two games. “It’s not normal for me, but first and foremost, the manager asks to be the best team-mate. I love playing but if I’m watching, I just want the best for England and that’s to win and I think I dealt with it really well. It was different, but we have also been together in a cycle now for two years. “[James] Trafford started really well for Leeds. It’s been a good unit around us for the last two years. That’s what the manager said and you have to respect that decision.” Pickford is expected to regain the gloves in Croatia. View image in fullscreen England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford during a press conference in Rijeka. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA Share Updated at 10.41 EDT

44m ago 10.16 EDT How to run a sustainable club? Brighton are celebrating all three Premier League monthly awards for September! Fabian Hürzeler is manager of the month, Pascal Groß is player of the month, and Lewis Dunk – who else? – wins goal of the month. Share

54m ago 10.07 EDT John Brewin OK, it was this time last week that the City news leaked and then broke. What a ride it’s been since. More when we get it, and there’s always likely to be more. Share

1h ago 10.04 EDT That’s the lot from me: John Brewin is here to take the reins. Share

1h ago 09.37 EDT Neville makes a good point, I think, about the general perception that corruption and financial doping is something that occurs in other countries. Share

1h ago 09.35 EDT “I absolutely slammed my club after they put the Super League idea forward,” Neville adds. “City fans and players need to start adopting that tack. “If we look at other countries ... corruption and financial doping ... all those things ‘happen in other countries’ ... the Premier League is now being dragged through the mud, because the team who’s been the best team for 15 years appear to have won those titles inappropriately. That’s devastating. “The Premier League survived without Aston Villa, Nottingham Forest, Sheffield Wednesday ... they were bigger than Manchester City a few years ago … I don’t think it’s that important whether City get relegated. It’s a sideshow. “The achievements in that period, do they stand? And the owners … to own part of a football club is one of the greatest responsibilities you could have … the reality is, it has to be taken very seriously. Don’t get bogged down on fines, or whether City are in League One or League Two.” Share

2h ago 09.28 EDT Gary Neville is having a chat on telly now, about – you guessed it – Manchester City. “That period [of Manchester City success] is all in doubt ... who knows where it might go ... but it’s huge, it undermines the English game, it undermines the achievements of one of the greatest teams we’ve seen. “I think City players will come out fighting in the next few weeks ... that’s quite expected ... you defend your club to the hilt ... once this plays out. “If the guilty verdicts remain, it will be a period that is tainted for ever ... The achievements are tarnished.” View image in fullscreen Gary Neville kisses Paul Scholes after his Manchester United teammate scored the winning goal against Manchester City in 2010. Photograph: Lindsey Parnaby/EPA Share Updated at 09.29 EDT

2h ago 09.24 EDT The England goalie Pickford also said that at 32, he’s young for a goalkeeper. The question is about World Cup cycles, and whether or not he thinks in those terms. He mentions Gianluigi Buffon and Manuel Neuer, and obviously has no intention of hanging up his gloves any time soon. Share

2h ago 09.16 EDT Jordan Pickford was asked about how it felt to sit out the games against Spain and Czechia. He made all the right noises about being a good team player, and being supportive of James Trafford, even if he didn’t necessarily like being left out. Share Updated at 09.16 EDT

2h ago 09.07 EDT “We are here in a beautiful place, we are a group that likes to hang out together, so it feels almost like friends,” Tuchel said of the current camp. “We have been seven weeks together in the US, so we have a strong bond, and to have the possibility to be here, in this beautiful place … we train on a high level, we do what we love most, train football in this environment – what is not to love? It’s beautiful. “It’s a good time to recharge and also prepare for the match, because we expect a very difficult match tomorrow, against a big football nation, and a proud country, a country full of quality in the Croatian side. Very experienced players, also a good mix of young players, and also a new coach. You know how it is, everyone tries to impress the new coach, everything is ready to go and give everything … this is what waits for us. It feels a little bit like a cup game, like a cup semi-final or something … we will prepare carefully.” View image in fullscreen The former West Ham manager Slaven Bilic is back in charge of Croatia. Photograph: Manu Fernández/AP Share

2h ago 08.54 EDT Tuchel on Mateo Kovacic: :We had a special relationship, he was my player at Chelsea, we won the Champions League together, such a nice and humble and warm character – and on the pitch, full of character. It was pure pleasure to work with him. “Every time I see him I love to be close to him and hug him. It feels like a very very close relationship … even if we don’t text that much, and see each other even less … It was a pleasure to work with him … It’s a special bond, and he is a special player for me, always.” View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel and Mateo Kovacic in 2021, during their Chelsea days. Photograph: Oli Scarff/EPA Share Updated at 09.01 EDT

2h ago 08.51 EDT Tuchel on Modric: “Luka is a national hero. Legend of the game … he won the Ballon d’Or at the height of his career. He’s just a fantastic football player, an amazing person … the way he acts on the field, he’s a role model, and a true legend of the game.” Share

2h ago 08.49 EDT Tuchel is asked a question about the defensive changes in store for tomorrow in England’s lineup. “It seems Ezri Konsa is back, he did the full training today,” Tuchel says. “This gives us a lot of hope for tomorrow. Nico O’Reilly, our left-back, left camp. On the right side we have competition, Marc should be ready to go, ready to start. The coach will never tell you the lineup … Sometimes you forget that this team who played against Czechia never played together [before] … it was solid and professional … tomorrow we have to find solutions again and we’re up for it.” Share Updated at 08.50 EDT

2h ago 08.45 EDT Back to Manchester City. In theory, would Tuchel pick players outside the top flight for England [in the event that City are relegated as part of their punishment]? “There is always a possibility ... I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament. I would never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country, so you need to look at it case-by-case.” Share Updated at 09.09 EDT

2h ago 08.44 EDT What are Tuchel’s thoughts on Saturday’s game being behind closed doors (a few thousand Croatian children will be present, and around 100 England fans, it is said.) “First of all I’m happy for the children they have the opportunity to come and watch, that’s I think a big inspirement for them … a big occasion … a unique occasion … I’m glad that 100 [England] or 200 fans have a chance to be here, that means a lot to us, our most loyal fans have a chance to be behind the doors. “It’s never nice [with no crowd], it’s always a bit of a strange atmosphere then … we love the atmosphere in the stadium, a proper football crowd, and this is a part we have to take into consideration, we cannot fall asleep and switch off and be in holiday mode, it might feel a bit like pre-season, but it’s not pre-season, it’s a crucial match in the Nations League. It’s just another layer to be professional and to take care about. It is what it is and you have to deal with it.” View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel talks to media before England’s meeting with Croatia on Saturday. Photograph: Antonio Bronić/Reuters Share Updated at 09.53 EDT

2h ago 08.40 EDT Regarding team news before the Croatia game – asked if fatigue will play a part in his selection, Tuchel adds: “Not yet, I think not yet. We took care about fatigue in the last training sessions. It made a huge difference for us, having three days in between. So we could actually take care of players with a high output like Elliot Anderson, like Anthony Gordon, for example. “Today everyone was in training except Nico O’Reilly, who unfortunately had to leave camp, to get a treatment as soon as possible … with his discomfort it was just too painful, he could not come back on the pitch … that’s the only one who is not available ... everyone else started training, finished training today at a high level, we played 10 against 10, so everyone is pickable, and ready to go.” View image in fullscreen Nico O'Reilly has left the England camp due to injury. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Ed Sykes/Apl/Sportsphoto Share Updated at 09.00 EDT

2h ago 08.39 EDT Has Tuchel spoken to the City players in camp about the current scandal relating to financial breaches? Has it been discussed by everyone in camp? “I guess so. We had some time off between matches, and it’s a big subject … As you rightly say, everyone speaks about it, there is no other voice needed ... I am glad to not be that voice. No one needs my half-knowledge on the topic. “Of course the players talk about it, of course the Man City players, and we talk with them but only briefly. They are ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch, and in camp ... but of course it’s a big topic, it’s a big topic in camp.” Share Updated at 08.56 EDT

2h ago 08.32 EDT Cheers Tom. Yes, Tommy Tuchel is up imminently, to offer no comment on the Manchester City fun and games, before previewing Croatia v England. Share

3h ago 08.30 EDT Luke is back from lunch which means that Thomas Tuchel will be talking soon. My giddy aunt, I’m out of here. Share

3h ago 08.22 EDT More emails on City’s appeal. “If this evidence Manchester City is so ‘irrefutable’ – why wasn’t it considered as such during the main hearing? Other clubs should boycott their matches against them this season,” writes Matt Miller. Tom Atkins adds: “What did people expect? This is an organisation which has spent the last 15 years throwing money and lawyers at any attempt to limit their ambitions or hold them to account, they’re not exactly going to hold their hands up and say ‘it’s a fair cop’ now. Get them out, keep them out for a long time, and award Rob Holding the Premier League medal he deserves.” You had me until Rob Holding. Share

3h ago 08.17 EDT Savage steps up to take Peterborough job Peterborough United have confirmed the appointment of Robbie Savage as their new manager, with the Welshman leaving his role at Forest Green to take up the position. “Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager. A word I personally haven’t used about our football club for too long,” said chairman Darragh MacAnthony. “His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie. The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by.” Savage added: “What attracted me to the club is the size of the club, the philosophy, working with young players and making them better, but the style of football was key.” Full story: Robbie Savage steps up to take Peterborough job and ‘understands reservations’ Read more View image in fullscreen Robbie Savage says he ‘would rather win games 5-4 than 1-0’. Photograph: Craig Galloway/ProSports/Shutterstock Share

3h ago 08.06 EDT No “winning formula” for World Cup success, concludes Fifa technical report Fifa’s technical report on the 2026 World Cup has highlighted an increased number of tactical strategies at the tournament but concluded there was not necessarily a ‘winning formula’. The world governing body’s Technical Study Group (TSG) and Football Performance Insights Department (FPI) published a 500-page report on Friday, offering ‘unprecedented insights into how the best national teams and players on the planet are reshaping the modern game’. All 104 tournament matches were observed using advanced data and video analyses and 11 ‘key tactical and technical’ trends were identified. FPI lead Tom Gardner said: “The big change between 2022 and 2026 is the variety of different tactical styles that we saw, and how teams were able to execute those different strategies successfully. “The build-up in a back three was something that we observed as very important, but it wasn’t something that Spain did. “So we’re not here saying if you want to be a successful team, you have to build up in a back three. “It’s about saying this is what we’ve observed. This is where we see more and more teams headed, and this is where teams have been able to do it and do it well.” The key tactical innovations that were identified included building with a back three, wide player rotations, changing the point of attack, attacking transitions, structured high press, defensive blocks and counter pressing. The report said there were ‘contrasting routes to success’, adding: ‘From aggressive high presses to disciplined low blocks and rapid transitions, the analysis shows that there was no single winning formula. ‘Cabo Verde exemplified how compact defending, collective organisation and proactive goalkeeper involvement can enable teams to compete against technically superior opponents.’ Press Association Share

3h ago 08.00 EDT Ed Aarons and Miguel Dantas View image in fullscreen Rui Pinto (L) arrives to Lisbon Criminal Court in March 2019. Photograph: Rodrigo Antunes/EPA-EFE Rui Pinto is to appeal a decision to end the special protection programme that has safeguarded him since August 2020. Lawyers for the whistleblower say that he remains at risk and that ending his protection would leave him “more vulnerable than at any point since 2020”. They say the decision was taken without giving him an opportunity to be heard and have described the circumstances surrounding it as a “failure to respect the rule of law”. Pinto was notified on Wednesday that his protection is due to end on 10 October. His lawyers say they will lodge an administrative appeal with suspensive effect, meaning the decision will be suspended while it is challenged. In a request to Portugal’s Ministry of Justice, the lawyers asked the government to reconsider the decision, disclose the material on which the latest risk assessment was based, hear Pinto and ensure that his protection continues. “His situation is now critical,” said his lawyers in a statement. “The threats against him are not merely theoretical: last April, he was assaulted in Lisbon. His revelations implicated powerful individuals with substantial resources, and many of the resulting legal proceedings are still ongoing, as demonstrated by the decision issued just a few days ago by the Premier League’s independent commission concerning Manchester City. Abruptly deprived of his protected residence and placed in a situation of extreme precariousness, Rui Pinto will now be more vulnerable than at any point since 2020.” Pinto entered Portugal’s protection programme after cooperating with the country’s justice authorities. His revelations have subsequently been used by judicial, tax and sporting authorities across Europe, including the Premier League’s investigation into City’s alleged financial irregularities. Pinto’s lawyers argue that the authorities should take into account both his cooperation with the justice system and the continuing risks associated with his disclosures before ending his protection. “This decision, and the manner in which it was taken, regrettably fail to respect the rule of law and constitute an act of state terrorism. We cannot accept this,” they added. Share Updated at 08.34 EDT

3h ago 07.47 EDT “I, for one, can’t understand how all the other teams can play against Man City over the coming season with this hanging over proceedings,” writes Simon Staffans. “It’ll be so weird – will the points and goals count in the end? What if Isak plays against them at Anfield and comes off with a torn ACL, derailing Liverpool’s season in a match that perhaps should never have been played and definitely not been played with those players playing for Man City? It’s a kind of alternate reality almost. Bizarre, to say the least.” It’s a great point. City have a knockout cup game this month, how do you respect the result of that if you lose? Share

3h ago 07.39 EDT Hello, here for the next hour, as Luke said, keep your emails coming in. Share

3h ago 07.32 EDT I’ll be back at 1.30 for Thomas Tuchel’s media conference – Tom Bassam is stepping into the breach until then. Thanks for all the emails. You can vent to Tom here! Share Updated at 07.33 EDT

4h ago 07.30 EDT “Probably wishful thinking,” emails Nick, “but would the frivolity of an unsuccessful appeal factor into any decisions about sanctions, as per a red card? I’ll admit to being biased, but it’s hard to see how City are anything other than bang to rights here.” Share

4h ago 07.24 EDT In similar vein, Bob chips in with a beautifully precise one-word email, entitled ‘Man City appeal’: “Farcical.” Share

Sports.title: Andy Burnham urged by Lib Dems to reveal all meetings with owners of Manchester City
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham is facing calls from the Liberal Democrats to publish details of all his meetings with Manchester City’s owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), and declare all hospitality he has accepted at the Etihad Stadium.

The prime minister was widely criticised this week for saying he would be “really concerned” if ADUG were forced to sell City after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations, which led to Downing Street issuing two clarifications of his position on Thursday.

Burnham also praised ADUG’s investment in Manchester, having had close relations with the company, through which Sheikh Mansour bought City in 2008, during nine years as the mayor of Greater Manchester which ended when he returned to parliament this summer.

In a strongly-worded letter to Burnham the Lib Dems’ spokesperson for culture, media and sport, Anna Sabine, criticised his apparent defence of City as “extraordinary” and invoked Gianni Infantino’s aborted World Cup sell-off scheme in what she described as a difficult year for football.

“As you will know, an independent commission has found Manchester City guilty of 114 charges of breaching financial rules over a timeframe of nearly a decade, including the use of ‘sham contracts’ and schemes to disguise more than £830m of funding,” Sabine writes in a letter seen by the Guardian.

“Despite this, your response was to thank the club’s owners for their work and describe the findings as ‘contested’ and that it was ‘wrong to jump to a conclusion’. It is extraordinary that a prime minister would use his position to call into question the findings of the independent investigation, and risk undermining trust in the Premier League’s processes.

“This has been a difficult year for football’s reputation. Fifa’s conduct around the World Cup has already raised serious questions about integrity in the game we love. At a moment like this, fans expect their prime minister to stand up for the rules in place, not to appear to side with a club found guilty of breaking them.”

Sabine also told the Guardian that Burnham’s ties to ADUG should be scrutinised and is planning to write to Downing Street and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to demand details of their meetings.

“Football fans up and down the country deserve to know that the rules apply to everyone, however rich and powerful they are,” Sabine said. “When the prime minister leaps to the defence of a club’s owners within hours of a verdict, people are entitled to ask what their relationship is.

“Andy Burnham must come clean and publish details of every meeting and conversation he has had with City Football Group, Abu Dhabi United Group or UAE government representatives, going back to his time as mayor – and that includes any hospitality freebies received.”

Quick Guide How do I 

Burnham, an Everton fan, has been pictured attending City games at the Etihad Stadium in hospitality areas.

The extent of that hospitality is unclear because under GMCA regulations the public disclosure of gifts is available for current office holders without the submission of a freedom of information request.

Burnham has not been to a City game since he became prime minister but has attended two Everton matches at Hill Dickinson Stadium, where he was accommodated in the directors’ box despite having a season ticket in the South Stand.

City confirmed on Friday that they had appealed against an independent commission’s verdict. They repeated their assessment that the verdict “contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe”.

Sports.title: Robbie Savage steps up to take Peterborough job: ‘All I want is a chance’
Sports.content:
Robbie Savage has been confirmed as the new manager of League One strugglers Peterborough.

Savage has left his role at National League side Forest Green Rovers and signed a long-term contract at Posh, who are currently second from bottom and sacked Luke Williams last month. His appointment marks his first Football League role since retiring as a player in 2011, and Savage said he is relishing the opportunity to prove any doubters wrong.

“Everyone’s entitled to their opinion but all I want is a chance. I’ve done it all my life,” Savage said. “When I was released by Manchester United I was told I wasn’t good enough, when I moved to Leicester I wasn’t in the team and had to battle. Nobody’s given me anything in this world, I’ve earned it and I’ve worked hard for it.

“Judge me when we start playing football – that’s what I love. I’m passionate and emotional and I just want to watch this young team give me everything, play that explosive style of football.”

Savage started his managerial career at Macclesfield, whom he steered to promotion to National League North before moving to Forest Green in 2025. He is expected to meet the players for the first time on Sunday before taking charge for in Tuesday’s Football League Trophy tie against Ipswich Under-21s.

Quick Guide How do I 

The Peterborough chair, Darragh MacAnthony, said: “Excitement is the word I can use to describe the appointment of Robbie Savage as our new manager – a word I personally haven’t used about our football club for too long. His personality, character and mindset is something we need top to bottom. Nobody will work harder to get us up and running again than Robbie. The board were blown away by him in an extensive interview, and his hunger to fix our issues and get confidence back into our talented squad is what I am most excited by.”
