Sports.title: Bilic is back: bravery and belief underpin second coming as Croatia manager
Sports.content:
“I don’t believe in comebacks.” Slaven Bilic sat in the lobby of a hotel in Canary Wharf wearing a black Soundgarden T-shirt and dark denim, confidently discussing a wide variety of topics ranging from Sir Alex Ferguson’s autobiography to historical epics of Yugoslav cinematography and Nikola Tesla’s celibacy. He was living the good life in London, just before his third Premier League season as West Ham’s manager, and a rare interview for Croatian media was a chance for him to catch up with domestic intrigues.

“I’m now distanced by default, geographically,” he said, breathing a sigh of relief, before continuing to jump from subject to subject; a bit about a Metallica concert, then a bit about steaks at an Argentinian restaurant, followed by some off-record anecdotes. He was clearly enjoying himself and didn’t hesitate to show it; his time as Croatia’s manager seemed long gone, although he always left a bittersweet aftertaste when talking about them.

“I have nice memories and wouldn’t want to spoil them,” he said. “I don’t like coming back. It’s not the fear of failure, just the feeling that something has run its course.”

And yet, here we are now. Nine years after that interview – and 14 since his first spell as Croatia’s manager ended – Bilic is back at the helm and preparing to face England in Rijeka in the Nations League on Saturday. Between times there was the Saudi Pro League and Chinese Super League, as well as West Brom and Watford, and no work for 23 months from August 2024.

Age has added some sophistication to Bilic’s appearance, his styling resembling a patchwork of homages to great football managers of our time (the Klopp/Guardiola salt and pepper beard, the Bielsa glasses on a string, the Simeone all-black wardrobe), but he is still unmistakably himself: direct, eloquent and above all passionate, so different from his predecessor Zlatko Dalic’s restrained and humble, almost priest-like, persona.

In July, on Bilic’s first public appearance back in the job, it was as if someone had opened the windows and let in fresh air. The 58-year-old remains the man; he knows how to charm and capture attention.

No coach would find it easy to succeed Dalic, who made history with Croatia, leading them to second and third at World Cups, but Bilic was always the best choice: not only because he knows full well what he is dealing with but also because there is a lingering sense that he laid the foundation for that success.

The sense is that he started to plant what blossomed into Luka Modric’s and Dalic’s team; that he made Croatia dream big for the first time since his generation of 1998 as a player, a cornerstone being the famous 3-2 victory at Wembley in 2007, when Croatia won not because they needed to but because they could and felt fully confident in their strength.

Bilic is also probably the only one who could have convinced Modric to stick around for a while. Fittingly, the 41-year-old Modric scored the first goal of the second Bilic era, in a 2-1 win in Prague against Czechia last Saturday, and rushed to embrace his manager. “Luka is everything to us, he’s just incredible” Bilic said.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Luka Modric scored Croatia’s first goal since Slaven Bilic returned to the dugout. Photograph: Martin Divíšek/EPA

When it comes to his managerial work, Bilic needs to prove himself again. He is inevitably no longer the coach he was during his first reign and it remains to be seen how he can apply his experience. It is too early to tell after two games – the second a 4-1 away defeat by a vastly superior Spain, for which he rotated heavily – but there are clues.

Under Dalic the team often waited and relished their underdog role, then were deadly on the counter, despite not having many quick players and despite a creative midfield being their main strength. Bilic wants to dominate; he wants his players to press high, take more risks and for more players to arrive in the opposition area. He wants his centre-backs to step up with the ball rather than wait for Modric or Mateo Kovacic to drop back to the edge of the box and take possession. He wants his team to be brave, attacking and as passionate as he is.

Can he do it with a squad that, despite significant infusion of fresh blood over the years, is still dominated by veterans such as Modric, Kovacic and Ivan Perisic? He believes he can.

Bilic always believed. In 2012 he believed his Croatia could win the Euros (they went out in the group stage) and now he says he can match Dalic’s success. Maybe he really didn’t believe in comebacks nine years ago, but that didn’t stop him keeping faith in bigger things.

Sports.title: Nations League: Ronaldo-less Portugal prosper while Klopp gets first win as Germany coach
Sports.content:
Portugal maintained their perfect start to Nations League Group A4 as Jorge Jesus’s squad showed little signs of missing Cristiano Ronaldo with a 4-2 victory over Denmark in Copenhagen.

The 41-year-old Al-Nassr forward and five-time Ballon d’Or winner left the camp before the match amid reports of a falling out with Jesus, his former club manager, having been left on the bench throughout a victory in Norway.

João Cancelo gave Portugal a 13th-minute lead before Brentford midfielder Mikkel Damsgaard equalised.

Gonçalo Ramos swiftly put Portugal back in front after 25 minutes, with Napoli forward Rasmus Højlund levelling things up at 2-2 early in the second half following a swift counter.

Vitinha’s header, his first Portugal goal, and a late strike by João Félix made it three straight wins.

“A victory of the highest quality,” said Jesus. “This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard – and that cannot be overlooked. Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.”

New Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp got his first win with a 2-0 Group A2 victory over Serbia in Munich. Bayern Munich midfielder Tom Bischof fired in his first senior international goal and Liverpool forward Florian Wirtz then added a second in the 61st minute.

Germany produced a disciplined and intensive game, illustrating the high-pressure soccer Klopp wants to instill in the team. “That’s going in my archive. We’ll make a video out of it now,” Klopp said. “That’s how we want to play.”

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp (right) applauds fans alongside Tom Bischof, who scored his first international goal in the victory over Serbia. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

Speaking to public broadcaster ZDF, he added: “The mix of football and attitude was top level today. I told the boys that this has to be our benchmark.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wirtz said: “It was important to win again, just for the spirit in the team, and to send a signal out that we’re good football players and also a good football nation. Definitely a step in the right direction.”

In the same group, Tijjani Reijnders scored a late equaliser as the Netherlands fought back to draw 2-2 with Greece, who remain top. Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgos Masouras had the home side 2-0 up at the break.

Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk powered in a header from a corner on the hour. After Denzel Dumfries had seen his goal ruled out by VAR for offside, Reijnders lashed home a rebound in the 89th minute to secure a point.

In Group B3, Israel and Kosovo played out a goalless draw in Debrecen, Hungary. In Group D1, Malta and Gibraltar drew 1-1 while in Group D2, Azerbaijan were held to a goalless draw by Liechtenstein in Baku.

Sports.title: Shaw secures WCL draw against Real Madrid as Manchester City show spirit after week of turmoil
Sports.content:
Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City head coach, said the noise surrounding the guilty verdict dished out by the Premier League had zero impact on his women’s team’s performance after they played out a high-quality draw with Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League.

Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw’s ruthless finish earned City a point against an impressive Real Madrid side on a night when the hosts were surely glad for attentions to turn – however briefly – towards on-pitch matters after a week when the wider football club has dominated the headlines for the wrong reasons.

“Of course there is a lot of noise but the players are very calm – I haven’t seen or noticed anything that will take any percentage out of the players’ performance,” Jeglertz said.

The result – which was a fair reflection of an even but entertaining game – left both sides with two points from their opening two fixtures but City will know their league phase opponents should theoretically become less challenging from hereon after their opening draw at Bayern Munich. The Swedish coach added: “It is OK, it’s an OK start in the Champions League. It’s not ideal but it’s a good start and we know what is needed from us in the rest of the tournament.”

Quick Guide WCL roundup: PSG pummel Leuven Show The day after Paris FC played their first Women’s Champions League home game at Stade Jean-Bouin, across the road from Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, PSG’s women’s team entertained Leuven 20km away at the club’s suburban training centre. Rasheedat Ajibade put the hosts ahead from close range after nine minutes against the Belgian side. Naomie Feller (pictured) then scored a quick-fire double, before Sakina Karchaoui and Vitória Yaya completed PSG's 5-0 rout. In the early games, Modesta Uka scored Austria Vienna’s first goal in the WCL but Inter's captain, Ivana Andrés, levelled in the fourth minute of added time to earn a 1-1 draw. Inter dropping points left Barcelona, who thrashed Roma on Wednesday, as the only WCL team with six points after two games. In a match between two teams that had lost in the opening round, HB Køge crushed visiting Swiss team Servette 5-1 in Denmark. PA Photograph: Benoît Tessier/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Jeglertz had been at pains to insist that it has been “business as usual” for his team despite the damning guilty verdict released by the Premier League towards the men’s side. There was a strange mood around this stadium in the buildup to kick-off with opinions mixed.

Speaking to supporters on the bridge that connects this venue with the neighbouring Etihad Stadium, some appeared relaxed about the situation and unsure what it had to do with the women’s team, while others were clearly troubled and looking forward to watching some football as a form of escapism.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw fires home Manchester City’s equaliser early in the second half. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

An elderly City fan, who did not wish to be named, said pre-match: “We’ve been through rough times before, we’ll come through rough times again,” in a matter-of-fact manner. Another simply demonstrated what appears to be a growing dislike for reporters asking about the 115 charges when they said angrily “you’re from the media?” before using an expletive and promptly walking away.

A much politer, younger woman simply expressed her sadness and her hopes that it wouldn’t cause the players stress.

Once the match started, there were occasional references to the news from the stands; midway through the first half one home fan sang ‘Sheikh Mansour, my lord, Sheikh Mansour, oh lord, Sheikh Mansour’, to the tune of Kumbaya, although nobody else appeared to join in. There was also a small group of men carrying an inflatable banana in one corner defiantly chanting about ‘City going down with a billion in the bank’.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In general, though, the regular Women’s Super League match-going fans who are members of the supporters club seemed focused on their usual repertoire of fan chants to encourage the players, whether singing about the brilliance of Aoba Fujino and later chanting the name of Mary Fowler, who hit the crossbar with a header before the break.

By then Real Madrid were already ahead courtesy of Linda Caicedo’s clinical, low finish into the bottom corner after a lethal burst of pace. The visitors could have scored as early as the first minute, when a sloppy mistake by Carlotta Wamser allowed Felicia Schröder to shoot but her effort flew narrowly wide and bounced off the stanchion, rippling the net but from the wrong side. It was a sign of the Spanish team’s intent and they looked sharp throughout.

City’s play was significantly more urgent and incisive after the break and – after Yui Hasegawa spurned a volleyed chance when she was in space inside the box – it did not take long for the hosts to equalise. Shaw turned and clinically fired into the corner of the net with great technique after good pressing from City led to Hasegawa winning the ball in midfield and feeding Shaw in the area. It was the Jamaica striker’s fifth goal of the season in all competitions and her first of this Champions League campaign.

Suddenly the WSL champions were dominating the territory, although Caicedo did go close at the other end with a diagonal shot that bounced wide. The introductions of Beth Mead, Sam Coffey and Grace Clinton from City’s bench only seemed to further strengthen the hosts.

Hasegawa volleyed just wide again, this time from the second phase after a half-clear corner, in another let-off for Real Madrid, who had gone close themselves at the other end when Ayaka Yamashita did well to save from Caicedo. The home fans were on their feet to applaud Yamashita and chant her name when she later produced a quick reaction save to keep out Irune Dorado’s close-range effort and keep the score level.

Sports.title: Neco Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against 10-man Norway
Sports.content:
On a night when Erling Haaland moped around the pitch, dragging his hulking frame across the Cardiff turf, Wales registered a welcome victory over 10-man Norway and their first this year. Was this just one of those games where the game’s deadliest finisher was stuck on the fringes or was it a case of 115 things occupying his mind? Either way, this defeat proved a humbling experience. “You’re just a shit Kieffer Moore,” was the chant aimed at Haaland from the locals.

Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb’s well-worked opener in the first half and 17 seconds after the restart Torbjørn Heggem was sent off for fouling James as the Leeds winger streamed towards goal, resulting in a free-kick from which Neco Williams earned Craig Bellamy a timely win with an unerring strike. It is the first time the side have beaten opposition ranked higher than them under this head coach.

“It feels a bit like the first punch in the face in a long, long time,” said the Norway and Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard after his country lost successive games for the first time in four years. “Now we have to respond, stick together and fight back.”

For Bellamy, a first win since last November eased the mounting negativity after a bruising run of results, chiefly their World Cup playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March and a listless display in Denmark last Sunday. “I felt my own disappointment since Bosnia and I’ve felt the stick as well,” the Wales head coach said. “The summer wasn’t easy. These games weren’t easy. But I’ve seen it … I’ve seen managers before me get it. I’ve seen the abuse the previous manager [Rob Page] got. It’s been a really difficult couple of months but it’s ‘welcome to this’ if you want to step into this … this is it. I do think we could be kinder to each other.”

It was plain to see Bellamy had been hurting and he cited his daughter receiving abuse on social media. “I chose to live back down here because I wanted to be on the ground, I wanted to be called a wanker to my face,” he added.

View image in fullscreen Torbjørn Heggem sees red straight after half-time. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

“The World Cup [playoff defeat] moved, I just felt the shift … Look, I am a strong person, I think we all are, but it’s the people around me I’m conscious of. It’s just society. What are we? Eight prime ministers in the space of 11 years? It’s nuts ... We’re such a small country, why can’t we have each other’s backs? Why don’t we look after each other more? The others can go at us. We’re too quick [to criticise].”

View image in fullscreen Dan James brings Wales level in the first half. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Wales bounced off the canvas after Ødegaard’s cute ball released Bobb on goal to open the scoring on 11 minutes. Liam Cullen, now of third-tier Leicester, pinched the ball from Sander Berge after the Fulham ­midfielder was sluggish to claim Fredrik Aursnes’s pass and Wales raced away from the scene.

Cullen and Lewis Koumas burst forward and Sorba Thomas zipped a low cross into the box, where James beat David Møller Wolfe to the punch. Thomas, who by his own admission loves staying wide to get chalk on his boots, was a constant threat.

Norway were punished for being slow out of the blocks in the second half, Heggem hauling James down after the restart. James does everything at speed and Heggem knew he was in trouble. The Spanish referee Alejandro Hernández awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box and ­Williams dispatched a wonderful right-foot strike to Ørjan Nyland’s right, to the surprise of the former Aston Villa and Reading goalkeeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bobb played draught excluder behind a white wall of Norway shirts and Nyland stepped to his left. Nyland was out of position when he had to shuttle across his goalline when Williams thrashed the ball into the bottom corner.

Haaland had one of those games; he was on the periphery and recorded just 11 first-half touches, the fewest of any player, including the Borussia Dortmund full-back Julian Ryerson who was forced off through injury after 16 minutes. Ethan Ampadu easily won what, technically, will go down as a duel on halfway but in truth Haaland just stuck out a leg in the hope of claiming the ball. His first whiff of goal came a couple of minutes before the interval but Ryerson’s replacement, Marcus Pedersen, misread Haaland’s movement and the move collapsed.

The substitute Josh Sheehan spurned a golden chance to extend Wales’s advantage, sending a weak shot at Nyland after more fine craftsmanship from Thomas to release the Bolton midfielder on goal. Up the other end, Haaland ambled across the box in preparation for another Pedersen cross. When it arrived Haaland soared high but unmarked sent a header straight at Danny Ward. Then came a puff of the cheeks, a look to the turf. It has been that kind of week.

Sports.title: Man City launch appeal with defiant club relying on one make-or-break argument
Sports.content:
Manchester City have officially appealed against the seismic guilty verdict delivered by an independent commission on their 115 charges.

The Premier League announced on Tuesday that City have been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges against them.



5 City could face relegation from the Premier League after being found guilty of each of their financial breach charges Credit: AFP

It comes over three-and-a-half years after City were first charged with 115 alleged breaches in February 2023.

In an explosive verdict, the Premier League stated that the club had disguised funding of more than £900million via a series of commercial deals between 2009 and 2018.

During this period, City won eight trophies, including three Premier League titles.



The ruling by an independent panel found them guilty of inflating their revenue by around £900m through 'sham' contracts with sponsors, which were funded by the club's owners.

The club and sponsors have both slammed the Premier League's guilty verdict, with City chief executive Ferran Soriano insisting it is based on a 'conspiracy theory' while principal sponsor, Etihad Airways, have denied involvement in the inflated sponsorship deals.



Nevertheless, City face unprecedented sanctions unless they can overturn the verdict.

City announce appeal

Now, City have officially confirmed their appeal is underway.

A defiant club statement read: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.



"The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

New Premier League rules state that an appeal hearing must be held within 12 weeks of an appeal being lodged.



With the hearing only allowed to last five days, a decision will then be due within 30 days of it's conclusion.

FA Statement "The Independent Commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate. "As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

How will City argue their verdict?

City will argue that the so-called 'tagged' sponsorship payments (totalling £830m) came from the Abu Dhabi Government and not their owner ADUG (Abu Dhabi United Group).

This applies to state-controlled entities such as Etihad and Etisalat, yet the former has previously refuted Abu Dhabi Government funding as "false".

City can point to an internal report written for the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi in 2010, which was not intended for external publication, that concluded the Abu Dhabi Government did indeed cover the sponsorship of the club.



5 City owner Sheikh Mansour is fighting the case after his club were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules Credit: Getty

In their UEFA case, City denied the Etihad (or any other) sponsorship funds came from any other source other than a direct payment. Owner Sheikh Mansour provided a letter which read: "I have not authorised ADUG to make any payments to Etihad, Etisalat or any of their affiliates in relation to their sponsorship of MCFC."

In 2015, the 'Partnership for Open and Fair Skies' wrote to the United States departments of Commerce, Transportation and State, arguing Etihad gained a competitive advantage due to receiving huge sums from the Abu Dhabi Government. They allude to the internal report referenced above, which appears to confirm this.

Yet, Etihad's response was: "The assertion that the Abu Dhabi Government paid for Etihad's sponsorship of English Premier League football club Manchester City is equally false.



"In 2011 Etihad and Manchester City entered into a 10-year sponsorship agreement, which included naming rights for Manchester City's stadium. Etihad funded this sponsorship from its own liquidity. It is not uncommon for airlines to have sponsorships with sports teams and their venues."

Etihad's denial that the Abu Dhabi Government helped pay for their sponsorship goes against City's core argument, according to the verdict, that "AD Sponsors had from time to time applied for financial assistance from the AD Government towards their liability to pay the Recorded Sponsorship Fees."

Due to redacted names, multiple sponsors, and the phrase 'from time to time', City could make a case for other sponsors, but Etihad's on-record denial doesn't help the club's position, according to multiple legal sources spoken to.

5 The legitimacy of Manchester City's dominant era between 2009 and 2018 is on the line with the club's appeal underway Credit: Getty



It is also worth reiterating that the panel, having reviewed the evidence already provided, concluded any notion the Abu Dhabi Government, not ADUG, paid the tagged sums was "concocted well after the event."

Challenging the 'sham' accusation

Also central to City's appeal will be calling into question the 'sham' commercial agreements cited in the Premier League's verdict, which are alleged to have inflated their revenues.

By definition, a sham agreement needs cooperation and knowledge of all parties, and talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs revealed City will look to disprove this.

With City's shirt and stadium sponsors Etihad Airways publicly denying any knowledge of the commercial deals, this would give the club grounds to challenge the Premier League's accusation.



5 Manchester City's 61,000-capacity stadium is named after principal sponsor Etihad Airlines Credit: PA

"City semantically can say it isn't a sham agreement and if they succeed they can call into question the legal foundations of the verdict," Jacobs explained.

"In an appeal you can show bias, gross misconduct and error in the interpretation of the law. So City could go back and re-show the structure and say the Premier League and ultimately the panel haven't understood how the money funneled down.

"They can question whether the facts meet the definition of a sham deal."



When will City learn their punishment?

Applying the Premier League's rules, City's hearing could in theory conclude at the latest, on Christmas Day, and begin on December 21.

As that would not happen for obvious reasons, the implication is the appeal being heard from December 14.

It remains unclear whether sanctions will be announced before the appeal is heard, and whether they would ⁠take effect ​immediately.

5 Manchester City's players will now compete this season with a huge question mark over their heads Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



Should City be successful in their appeal against the Premier League's guilty verdict, that could then have a knock-on effect heading into a sanctions hearing, potentially dragging any verdict on longer.

Despite this, the Premier League intends to deliver a punishment verdict by the end of the season, with its clubs feeling the same.

talkSPORT understands that Premier League clubs plan to write to chief executive Richard Masters, stressing the importance of the City case, inclusive of appeals, being resolved this season.

Sports.title: Jarell Quansah wanted by European giants as failed Arsenal bid emerges
Sports.content:
Real Madrid have identified England international Jarell Quansah as a transfer target, according to reports in Germany.

Quansah, who plays for Bayer Leverkusen, has caught the attention of the La Liga giants after a string of impressive performances for the Bundesliga club.



4 Quansah has quickly become a key figure for Bayern Leverkusen after joining the club from Liverpool in 2025 Credit: AFP

German outlet BILD say the 15-time European Cup winners are currently scouting the 23-year-old.

The report also claims Quansah was the subject of a failed £55m bid from Arsenal this summer.

Talks between the Gunners and Leverkusen were widely reported at the time, before the Premier League champions ultimately landed Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa.



Real Madrid, now managed by Jose Mourinho, are expected to bolster their back line next summer with two new defensive incomings.

The signings of defensive trio Trent Alexander-Arnold, Dean Huijsen and Alvaro Carreras in 2025 have failed to convince.



Therefore ex-Liverpool ace Quansah could fit the bill for Mourinho as he continues his quest to edge Real back to the summit of European football.

The Warrington-born defender is currently on international duty with the Three Lions.



He played the full 90 minutes of England’s Nations League defeat to Spain last weekend, ahead of former Liverpool teammate Alexander-Arnold.

Quansah was an unused substitute in Tuesday's 2-0 win over Czechia in Prague.

Quansah's on fire

The defender has been in superb form for Leverkusen after joining the club in a record £30million switch in 2025.

Quansah has been deployed as both a centre-back and right-back, offering much-needed versatility to the Bundesliga outfit.



4 Jose Mourinho has identified the England defender as he looks to bolster his defensive options Credit: AFP

4 Quansah has clocked up seven caps for England and featured in Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad Credit: Getty

But his stay in Germany could be a short-lived one with Real Madrid appearing to step up their pursuit.

Quansah already shares a good relationship with Madrid duo Alexander-Arnold and Jude Bellingham from their time together with England.



And that could work favourably for Madrid in future negotiations for the star.

Liverpool's trump card

Despite Los Blancos holding a genuine interest, Liverpool remain in the driving seat should Quansah leave Leverkusen.

The Reds inserted a £59.5m buy-back clause for their academy star as part of Quansah’s Leverkusen deal.

4 Quansah's last act at Liverpool came in lifting the club's 20th top-flight title Credit: Getty



The Merseyside club have until June 2027 to activate the clause.

Liverpool could be in the market for a centre-back next summer with Virgil van Dijk’s contract set to expire.

Quansah came through the Liverpool academy and made his senior debut in a 2-1 win over Newcastle in August 2023.

He went on to make 58 appearances for the Reds, scoring three times.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo urged to join Man City despite 115 charges and possible Portugal ban
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo must join Manchester City - he would be the league's top scorer... in the fourth tier of English football.

That's the view of talkSPORT presenter Angelina Kelly, who believes Ronaldo and City are a match made in heaven in light of the club's guilty verdict for financial breaches.



5 Ronaldo's time on the international scene could be over, but a new chapter in England has been tipped to happen Credit: Getty

Both Ronaldo and City have dominated the news in recent days, with City awaiting Premier League punishment, which ranges from points deduction to possible top-flight expulsion.

They announced their appeal against the independent panel's seismic verdict on Friday.

As for the five-time Ballon d'Or winner, he walked away from Portugal's training camp having been left on the bench in last weekend's 2-1 win over Norway.



It was the first time since 2008 that the Manchester United and Real Madrid legend had been an unused substitute on the international scene.

Ronaldo is claimed to have been lied to by ex-Al Nassr boss Jorge Jesus about being introduced in Oslo, resulting in him issuing a bombshell statement on social media.



Will Cristiano Ronaldo ever play for Portugal again?

While the 41-year-old has not commented on his Portugal future - unlike his sister who has hinted he has retired from international football - Ronaldo could be banned from pulling on the famous jersey again.

Tied down in Saudi Arabia until the end of the 2026/27 campaign, it remains to be seen whether he will continue his career beyond next summer.



And he faces a possible six-month banishment from Portugal duty if he is found to have 'abandoned' the national team.

The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary code reads: "Any player who, having been regularly called up, unjustifiably abandons or fails to appear for training, a match, or any activity of the national teams or related to the sporting representation of the FPF or Portugal, will be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months."

Could Ronaldo join Man City?

And for Kelly, she has insisted that a Ronaldo and City link-up is now written in the stars - five years after he almost made the move to the Etihad before being lured back to Old Trafford.

5 City could face relegation from the Premier League after being found guilty of each of their financial breach charges Credit: AFP



5 A move to City would offer Ronaldo the chance to achieve his target of scoring 1,000 goals Credit: Getty

Speaking on Fiery Fridays as part of talkSPORT's Daily podcast, Kelly declared that Ronaldo, who in 2024 refused to rule out joining the Citizens in the future, will not be happy that City's verdict has dominated headlines this week.

As the Manchester United fan put it, 'If you can't beat them, join them!'

She said: "I feel sorry for Cristiano Ronaldo, he's walked out of Portugal's camp after crunch talks with their new manager."



Before adding: "So here is why I feel sorry for poor Ronaldo, because literally any other international break, this would be the biggest story in town, everyone would be talking about it.

"Instead, all anyone wants to talk about is Manchester City's guilty verdict.

"This is his big walkout moment, and even his best mate, Piers Morgan, is more interested in City, so, what's a girl to do?

5 No player in football history has registered as many international caps [234] or goals [146] as Ronaldo Credit: AFP



"If you can't beat them, I say join them Cristiano!

"And I think he should look to sign for Manchester City, because let's face it, depending what happens, Erling Haaland won't hang around if Manchester City get handed out points deductions for the next five years.

"So, Ronaldo should just get in there and take the opportunity, score a few more goals after January to help City finish 19th.

"Then he can be the top scorer in League Two next season, the crowds and standards of football will be better than the Saudi Pro League, in my opinion.

"And he will definitely reach the promised land of the 1,000 career goals, this is just wins across the board for him.



"And seeing as we're all now experts on Manchester City's sponsorship deals, the one thing that we've learned this week is that it's been hard for them to keep up with the red cartel's incomings, without using Abu Dhabi's own businesses as partners.

5 A move to the Etihad would tarnish Ronaldo's legacy at Manchester United Credit: Getty

"So how do you change that? Get the most famous man in the world to play for your team and watch the commercial deals absolutely sky rocket.

"And it's another way to wind up Manchester United fans, so as I say, this is win upon win for everyone, get Cristiano Ronaldo in a sky blue shirt."



Legendary talkSPORT broadcaster Adrian Durham was left stunned, as he remarked: "We are going to have to call the fire brigade because that is the hottest take I think I have ever heard in my life.

"But do you know what's really weird about that? I think you've got a great point, all the time I was listening, I was thinking, 'Please don't agree,' but actually, it makes total and utter sense."

talkSPORT's chief football correspondent Alex Crook then suggested that Ronaldo should be managed by Pep Guardiola if City are relegated to League Two.

He stated: "Pep Guardiola has come out publicly and said that he stands by Manchester City, Guardiola already picks his job, Bayern, Barceloa, Manchester City, the riches teams in all three leagues.



"If he really cares that much about Manchester City and if he is really that good, let him be the manager who takes over in League Two, let him see if he can do it at Accrington Stanley on a Tuesday night, he wouldn't have the gumption."

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson admits he was terrified by Old Trafford return after brain hemorrhage
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson admits he was terrified by Old Trafford return after brain hemorrhage

Sir Alex Ferguson has revealed he was ‘terrified’ about returning to Old Trafford following a brain haemorrhage.

The legendary Manchester United boss underwent emergency surgery after suffering a bleed on the brain in 2018.



3 Sir Alex made a heroic return to Old Trafford just months after life-saving surgery Credit: Getty

The ordeal saw him placed in intensive care and with just a 20 per cent chance of survival.

Ferguson went on to make a miraculous recovery but later feared losing his memory and his speech.

Just a few months on from his surgery, Ferguson made his return to Old Trafford to watch his beloved Red Devils take on Wolves.



Ahead of the release of his new book titled ‘Games of my Life’, the 84-year-old opened up on his emotions prior to his return to the director’s box.

Fergie's fear

“I was terrified,” Ferguson told the BBC on Friday.

“I wish I could say I was comfortable. I wasn’t. I wasn’t comfortable.



“I didn’t know what the reaction was. You go there and they make that announcement with the manager, and then of course the loud applause, it was heart-rending you know.

“My wife was with me and she was nearly crying. She sat down and said ‘ah that’s fantastic. That’s amazing.



“One of the things was the generosity of the support, and recognising my time there.”

Ferguson remains the most decorated manager in football history having masterminded a whopping 49 trophies during spells in charge of Aberdeen and Manchester United.

3 Ferguson won a record 13 Premier League titles at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

He took over at Old Trafford in 1986 and went on to manage the Red Devils for 26 seasons, accumulating 1,000 league matches in the dugout.



Ferguson led United to 13 Premier League titles, five FA Cups and two Champions League triumphs.

Although the legendary Scot has endured a difficult period with his health, he revealed that he is now in a much better place.

“I’m feeling quite good, yeah, despite small injuries,” he added.

“It was a long recovery. I wasn’t allowed to travel or drink or anything like that.

“I always remember my grandson coming in to see me, and I lost my voice, I couldn’t speak.



3 The 84-year-old says he is feeling better after a difficult period Credit: Getty

“And then they brought in a therapist and she started doing things like, write down names of birds, names of animals, names of rivers… but that way my voice came back.”

Asked about the emotional impact of his illness and recovery he said: “When I can’t talk, I must be frightened.

“That was a frightening moment that.”

Sports.title: Man City scandal could block Pep Guardiola from ever managing England
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola will never manage England - neither party will want to work together in the future.

That's the opinion of Spanish journalist Guillem Balague, who has commented on the possible implications of Manchester City being found guilty of all charges relating to Premier League financial breaches.



3 talkSPORT reported in May how Guardiola would welcome the chance to succeed Tuchel in the future Credit: Getty

The Citizens, who are planning to appeal the decision, now wait to see what punishment they face, with sanctions to potentially come into effect this season.

One major finding from the Premier League's 40-page document, was that City had been found guilty of inflating their revenue by around £900million from 2009-2018 through 'sham' contracts with sponsors, which were funded by the club's owners.

Guardiola was appointed at the Etihad in the last two years of the period in question, before remaining at the club until the end of the 2025/26 campaign.



Only legendary Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson has won more than his six Premier League titles, with the ex-Barcelona boss regarded as one of the all-time greats.

Could Pep Guardiola still manage England?

Such has been Guardiola's dominance in England, with the 55-year-old declaring that living in the country feels like home, he has consistently been linked with taking charge of the national team.



talkSPORT reported in May how he was keen on one day being in the Three Lions dugout, with the FA 'dreaming' of bringing in Guardiola when it comes to eventually replacing Thomas Tuchel.

But Balague, who wrote 'Pep Guardiola: Another Way of Winning: The Biography', insists that possibility could be over as a result of City's verdict - despite there being no evidence Guardiola knew of the club's historical breaches.



Claiming neither Guardiola nor England would now be willing to work with one another, Balague said on Drive: "Do you know that, for two months, Pep Guardiola made the England FA wait to see if he wanted to be the England national manager?

"And instead of that he stayed at Manchester City, renewed his contract and then they went for Tuchel. In my mind, he was always going to be a candidate post-Tuchel.

"Right now, I don't think the FA will want to bring somebody in that divides the world - or England anyway - in the way that Pep Guardiola will do from now on.

3 Guardiola''s Premier League legacy is being questioned by fans following City's guilty verdict Credit: Getty



"There's no doubt that this is going to happen whatever the consequences of the investigation and the cases, but I don't think he will want to be the England national manager either.

"Because he probably feels that there is far too many people interested in his legacy. But in his eyes, it was a really good job."

Has Pep Guardiola tarnished his legacy?

While rival fans of City's may argue that Guardiola's trophy-laden spell has been tainted in light of the verdict, Sports Breakfast co-hosts Alan Brazil and Ray Parlour beg to differ.

Asked whether he would accept Guardiola as England manager, Arsenal icon Parlour remarked: "I would, yeah, all day long.



"Because I can see us winning the World Cup with someone like Pep."

Interjecting, former Man United and Tottenham forward Brazil stated: "What's he got to do with business associates in Abu Dhabi, who are suddenly saying, 'I'll sponsor the club,' allegedly... what's he got to do [with the saga]?

3 City's possible punishments could be points reduction and fines, or even potential relegation and having their titles stripped

"If he's asked what players he wants, he can describe them, say, 'I'd love to have him,' he probably doesn't know their salaries and stuff like that."

Agreeing, Parlour then said: "He doesn't know how they fund it, absolutely, 'This is what my wish list is, if you can get them great, if you can't, you can't, simple as that, and then I'll work with the players.'



"You've still got to work with the players every day, you can spend a load of money, and that still doesn't guarantee you to be successful, does it?"

Ex-Scotland international Brazil then declared: "I'm not slagging the England manager [Tuchel], but I think Pep, he'd be a gem."

Having the final say on the matter, Parlour insisted: "You wouldn't be able to turn him down would you?"

Sports.title: Portugal star hails Jorge Jesus and ‘step forward in attack’ after Cristiano Ronaldo leaves
Sports.content:
Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo era may finally be over.

Well, that's if Vitinha's latest admission is anything to go by.

3 Vitinha's goal against Denmark was his first for Portugal Credit: Getty

Vitinha was one of four goalscorers for Portugal as they ran out 4-2 victors over Denmark in Nations League action on Thursday.



Also amongst the goals was Goncalo Ramos, who now firms as the 41-year-old's long-term replacement at the top of Portugal's attack.

It was a dominant display from the Selecao, who finished with 11 shots on target compared to Denmark's tally of just three.

Most notably, the win came a day after Ronaldo abruptly walked out on the national team amid reports he grew frustrated with a lack of minutes under new manager Jorge Jesus.

But if Ronaldo thought his strop would prompt several of his teammates to launch a passionate defence of his qualities, he better think again as Vitinha instead heaped praise on Jesus' tactical acumen when speaking to TVI Noticias.



What did Vitinha say about Portugal's performance against Denmark?

And, rather tellingly, the Paris Saint-Germain ace claimed Portugal 'took a step forward' in their attacking play with Ronaldo nowhere in sight.

"It's all thanks to the manager's work," Vitinha said.

"The truth is, we played an excellent game, and there's no hiding that.



"Winning here is extremely important, in a very difficult place to play, and two years ago, when we lost here, we learned that lesson. Don't be fooled by the result, because it was a very difficult game.

"Furthermore, it was the best performance we've had so far. We are growing, and the truth is, the more we work with the manager, the more we assimilate his ideas.



3 Jesus was appointed as Portugal boss on a four-year deal, so it's very much his ship to steer Credit: AFP

"Today we took a step forward in attack."

Portugal's win over Denmark also extended their perfect record under Jesus from three games.

And Vitinha is desperate to make it four from four when they return to Porto's Dragao Stadium on Sunday for a clash with Norway.

The midfielder also heaped praise on his teammates for the way they blocked out the noise generated by the Ronaldo sideshow.



"We tried to focus on the game and I think that's what we did," Vitinha said.

"We responded incredibly. Congratulations to the whole group."

3 Against Norway, Ronaldo was an unused substitute for the first time in 18 years Credit: Getty

Jesus, who vowed to 'explain everything' regarding the Ronaldo saga following Sunday's game against Norway, was equally delighted with his side's display in Denmark.

Crucially, the 72-year-old now feels like he has the entire group 'under control.'



What did Jorge Jesus say about Portugal's players?

"I have a group that believes... believes in my ideas, believes in the coach's ideas," Jesus said.

"Because they have so much individual quality, things go more easily.

"If you think this means having a group under control, then I have a group under control. Because they go hand-in-hand with me, with my ideas.

"The things that happen don't separate the group, they haven't separated us and they won't separate us."



Jesus and his side now turn their attention to Sunday's clash with Norway, but once the full-time whistle goes, all eyes will turn to Ronaldo who, like the national team boss, insists he'll tell all about the sideshow.

Sports.title: It could get even worse for Pep! Calls in Spain for Barcelona to be stripped of La Liga titles over payments to refs' chief... days after guilty verdict put his Man City legacy at risk
Sports.content:
A rough old week in the gilded life of Pep Guardiola has taken another turn for the worse.

First, the bombshell of Manchester City's guilty verdict compounded by details of their brazen disregard for Premier League rules as they built him a team to dominate.

Then, the Negreira scandal reared up again in Spain with 50,000 pages of evidence compiled by Real Madrid landing at UEFA on Thursday accusing arch-rivals Barcelona of making illicit payments to an influential referees' chief.

Maybe the timing is a pure coincidence. Maybe pure Madridian mischief.

Either way, Guardiola, the finest coach of his generation, finds his legacy under scrutiny like never before with demands raging for two of his three clubs to be stripped of the glittering array of titles he won.

The allegations in Spain are that Barcelona paid more than £7million in a series of payments over 17 years from 2001 to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira when he was vice president of Spain's technical committee of referees.

Pep Guardiola is finding his legendary managerial legacy under scrutiny like never before

Barcelona have repeatedly denied any wrongdoing, claiming the money was paid for scouting and technical reports provided by a company belonging to 81-year-old Negreira since the story broke in 2023.

At the time, Barcelona president Joan Laporta said: 'Let it be clear Barca have never bought referees and Barca never had the intention of buying referees, absolutely never.'

La Liga claimed they were unable to investigate because of the time elapsed since the alleged offences were so far in the past.

UEFA did launch an investigation although it appeared to be going cold until the matter resurfaced this year as Florentino Perez ran for re-election as president of Real Madrid with promises to get to the bottom of what he called 'the biggest scandal in history'.

On Thursday, UEFA issued a statement to confirm a 'substantial amount of documents' had landed at the door of its ethics and disciplinary inspectors and will be assessed.

Madrid-based sports papers Marca and AS splashed it across their front pages on Friday. Their Catalan equivalents gave the story less prominence.

Barcelona's response has been to point out that the proceedings have been ongoing since 2023 and had never been closed, and that they had complied with all requests to assist authorities.

The gist of the argument from Barca all along has been that nobody has offered any proof of sporting influence.

Real Madrid have accused Barcelona of making illicit payments to an influential referees' chief Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira during an era when Guardiola was at the helm

Madrid-based sports papers Marca and AS have splashed the latest controversy on their front pages

The allegations cover a period ending in 2018 when Barcelona-born former referee Negreira stepped down from the committee responsible for appointing match officials among other things.

Guardiola was head coach of Barca for four seasons in the heart of this era, from 2008 to 2012, during which he created a team generally accepted to be among the best to ever play the game.

With a youthful Lionel Messi sparkling at its heart, they won the Spanish title in three of Guardiola's four seasons and in 2011 swept the board winning every trophy they could, from La Liga and Copa del Rey to the Champions League, the Spanish Super Cup, UEFA's Super Cup and FIFA's Club World Cup.

The Negreira scandal relates specifically to Spanish domestic football but any lingering accusations that Barcelona tried to influence officials during this era will however chime with fans of English clubs.

At Chelsea, they will not forget the second leg of the Champions League semi-final at Stamford Bridge refereed by Tom Henning Ovrebo in 2009.

With the Blues ahead in the tie and well on top, Ovrebo resisted strong claims for what Chelsea boss Guus Hiddink later described as 'three clear penalties' and when Andres Iniesta equalised in stoppage time to send Barca into the final on away goals, Didier Drogba led the furious protests screaming 'disgrace'.

Chelsea defender Jose Bosingwa told Portuguese TV he thought the Norwegian referee had been 'bought'. Hiddink called it 'an injustice'.

Manchester United were beaten by Guardiola's Barcelona in the final in Rome, as they were again two years later at Wembley.

Robin van Persie's controversial red card at the Nou Camp in 2011 is an example that Real Madrid may have used against Barcelona

At Arsenal, they will recall Robin van Persie's red card at the Nou Camp in the last 16 tie in 2011, when Italian referee Massimo Busacca gave the Dutch striker a second yellow for taking a shot at goal one second after the whistle had gone.

'It is a joke,' fumed van Persie at the time. 'Frankly, embarrassing,' seethed Arsene Wenger.

There are many examples and it appears Real Madrid could have catalogued them all in their 50,000-page dossier.

Jose Mourinho, brought back by Perez for a second spell at the Bernabeu, will require no encouragement to fan the flames of the scandal.

Directly up against Guardiola's Barcelona for three years in his first spell at Real and for two more years as rivals in Manchester he thrives in a thickening plot, adept at the art of casting doubt.

After losing to Atletico last month, he seized his opportunity to lambast the appointment of the referee for the derby by the committee which no longer involves Negreira but will remain tarnished by association as long as these accusations continue to swirl.

Sports.title: Unai Emery fears the 'damage' caused to football if clubs break rules as he becomes the first Premier League boss to comment on bombshell Man City guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Unai Emery fears the 'damage' caused to football if clubs break rules as he becomes the first Premier League boss to comment on bombshell Man City guilty verdict

Unai Emery fears the ‘damage’ that football would suffer if clubs break its financial rules.

Manchester City were found by a Premier League independent panel to have illegally pumped in more than £900million to swerve financial rules, thanks largely to their ownership group topping up commercial partnerships to the tune of £830.69m. The club have appealed against the verdict.

Now Aston Villa boss Emery has become the first Premier League boss to comment on the matter.

Asked by Spanish publication Diario de Sevilla what might be the effect on the English top flight, Emery said: ‘It is an issue that has been publicly known about for a long time. We all have our restrictions: we have to sell players to comply with Financial Fair Play, and we have to work out how to structure contracts for new signings.

‘The owners generally have considerable financial resources, but Financial Fair Play is intended to ensure financial balance, so that you spend what you generate and there is no artificial inflation.

Unai Emery is the first Premier League boss to comment on Manchester City's guilty verdict

City are set to appeal their guilty verdict of breaching 'all charges related to serious breaches' of the Premier League's financial regulations

‘If other clubs had been artificially inflated and that were now coming to light, there would obviously be some damage. That is something for the courts and the relevant authorities to decide.

‘I feel sorry because of the way that team played. Under Guardiola, there were times when they were simply unmatched.’

Daily Mail Sport reported on Thursday that City would attempt to prove their innocence by arguing that the government of Abu Dhabi – rather than the club’s owners – part-funded ‘sham’ sponsorship deals.

Villa co-owners Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens are billionaires but the club are currently on the naughty step with UEFA for breaching financial regulations.

Clubs’ spending power is linked to revenue and despite their owners’ wealth, Villa do not have the same flexibility as global brands like Liverpool or Manchester United.

Villa are in Marbella, Spain, for a three-day training camp and were due to face Emery’s old club Sevilla in a friendly on Friday.

Sports.title: UAE threat to Britain over Man City case: Diplomatic ties are 'under significant strain'... as it's claimed club chief met cabinet minister in Downing Street the week before guilty verdict
Sports.content:
UAE threat to Britain over Man City case: Diplomatic ties are 'under significant strain'... as it's claimed club chief met cabinet minister in Downing Street the week before guilty verdict

The outcome of the Premier League's probe into Manchester City is understood to have put 'significant strain' on the diplomatic relationship between the UK and the United Arab Emirates, with billions of pounds of investment at stake.

Bloomberg UK reports that 'frustration on both sides' has escalated due to the fallout surrounding the case. City are owned by a private company run by Sheikh Mansour, a member of Abu Dhabi's royal family and the vice president of the UAE.

The outlet also reports that City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak met Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds in Downing Street to discuss UAE investment in Britain the week before the guilty verdict emerged.

In a bombshell judgment, City were found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 charges levelled against them by the Premier League, with the League saying this week that 'sham' sponsorship deals had been inflated by around £900million.

City today confirmed they have appealed against the verdict - with potential punishments if they do not succeed including a points deduction, heavy fines or even expulsion from the Premier League.

The Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters stated that the club had 'systematically broken' the rules for nearly a decade and called the decision by the Independent Commission who heard the case 'the most significant in Premier League history'.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Thursday, it is understood that City argue that the disputed money came from the Abu Dhabi government-owned sponsors, rather than the club’s owners – and was therefore not against the Premier League rules.

City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak (left) with owner Sheikh Mansour

City were proved over their dealings between 2011 and 2018, when they won three league titles

But, according to Bloomberg, Emirati officials have warned the UK government that the severity of the ruling could undermine their appetite for future grand-scale UK commitments. They add that UK government officials are equally frustrated by the conduct of some of their UAE counterparts with regard to the City controversy.

Over recent years the UAE has spent more than £30billion in major UK sectors, including defense, life sciences and technology. An investment summit is pencilled in for this month. Mubadala Investment Company, one of Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth funds, is owned by Mansour and its chief executive is City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak - who reportedly met Business Secretary Mr Reynolds in this capacity the week before the guilty verdict emerged.

Bloomberg report that on September 14 the pair held a private meeting in Downing Street, at which Mubarak talked about UAE investment in Britain.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham this week hailed the impact of City's owners and thanked them for their wider investment in Manchester.

'I would be really concerned to lose them,' said Burnham. ‘They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester.’

'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.'

'I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad (Stadium) and the campus around it but also into the city.'

On Thursday, Downing Street sought to clarify his comments. 'As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules,' a spokesperson said.

'He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.'

Sports.title: 'All the players are talking about it': Thomas Tuchel admits Man City guilty verdict is a 'big subject' in the England camp - and suggests he WOULD still pick their stars if they are kicked out of the Premier League
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has admitted the furore surrounding Manchester City is a 'big subject' in the England camp - with all the players in the squad talking about it. England are in Rijeka preparing for Saturday's Nations League clash with Croatia, a week after news first emerged that City had been found guilty of the vast majority of charges of financial impropriety brought against them by the Premier League. 'We had some time off between the matches and it is a big subject,' said Tuchel. 'Everyone speaks about it, so there is no other voice needed. I am glad to be not that voice. No one needs my half knowledge on the topic. 'Of course, the players talk about it. City players talk about it. We talk with them but only briefly. They are ready to go tomorrow. But of course, it's a big topic in the camp.' Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi are the two City representatives in this England squad, with Nico O'Reilly having withdrawn this week and returning to the club for an assessment on an injury. The left-back played the full game for manager Thomas Tuchel's side in the 3-2 defeat by Spain but missed Tuesday's 2-0 win against the Czech Republic, with Newcastle's Lewis Hall stepping in. Thomas Tuchel speaking in Croatia ahead of Saturday's gam Tuchel also suggested he would continue to consider picking City stars in the event that the club are kicked out of the Premier League as punishment, should their appeal fail. 'I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, occasion, the tournament,' he said. 'I will never rule out that because they don't play in the top flight in their country. We need to look at it case by case.' On Friday morning City confirmed they had launched an appeal against the verdict of the independent commission, saying: 'The club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe. 'The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions relating to this case. 'We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.'
