“My Lord, in this case, the letter is saying that J.B. Daudu wants to conduct the proceedings. But C. Ogbozor has been conducting the defence, and the record of this court is very clear,” the prosecution lawyer said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He also said the letter listed several lawyers, including a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) who could stand in for Mr Daudu in his absence.

He cited a Supreme Court case which held that a case should not wait for a particular lawyer, and argued that, in this instance, the lawyer the case was waiting for was not even the person handling it.

Despite his concerns, Mr Atolagbe said the prosecution would consent to the adjournment.

“It will be difficult for us to ask the court to proceed because we don’t want any party to raise any issue of fair hearing, but this is really sad,” he said.

He urged the court to adjourn the case until 23 October suggested by Mr Daudu.

Second defendant Omodachi Okolobia’s lawyer, Paul Erokoro, also SAN, did not oppose the request.

But he noted that the defence did complain when the prosecution sought several adjournments and used years to call witnesses.

Interjecting, Mr Atolagbe said Mr Erokoro had no right to comment on the issue since he did not author the letter requesting an adjournment.

This sparked off a back-and-forth between the two lawyers, forcing the judge, Peter Lifu, to intervene.

Mr Lifu said there was no need for further arguments because none of the parties opposed the request for adjournment.

He, however, noted that an adjournment should be based on the convenience of the court.

He adjourned the case until 6 November, which the lawyers also agreed to.

Corruption trial with chequered history

The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) first arraigned Mr Suswam and his then-Commissioner for Finance, Mr Okolobia, in November 2015 on 11 charges of conspiracy and money laundering, including criminal breach of trust.

The charges accused them of diverting N3.1 billion from the proceeds of the sale of Benue State Government shares managed through the Benue Investment and Property Company Limited.

According to the EFCC, the funds were channelled through Elixir Securities Limited and Elixir Investment Partners Limited between August and October 2014. Both defendants have consistently denied the allegations.

The has case faced repeated delays over the years. It moved between three judges, including the original trial judge, Ahmed Mohammed, who intitially withdrew from the matter, citing a Sahara Reporters publication accusing him of bias. The case was later assigned to Judge Okon Abang, before the Court of Appeal ordered that it be returned to Mr Mohammed.

Following Judge Mohammed’s elevation to the Court of Appeal in 2023, the case was reassigned to Judge Lifu, before whom the defendants were re-arraigned in March 2024.

The prosecution closed its case after calling nine witnesses and tendering documentary evidence before Mr Mohammed.

The defendants then filed a no-case submission, arguing that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against them.

However, in July 2025, Judge Lifu dismissed the application and held that the prosecution had established sufficient evidence requiring the defendants to enter their defence.

Mr Suswam later testified as the sole defence witness. Mr Okolobia neither testified nor called any witness for his defence.

The defendants closed their defence on 24 November 2025 after Mr Suswam testified.

Judge Lifu then fixed 20 January for the adoption of final written addresses and directed the prosecution and defence to exchange their written arguments within the prescribed timeline.

However, the case did not proceed to final arguments on the scheduled date.

It was adjourned several times before it was rescheduled for 29 May.

The matter was again shifted and, on 1 July, the judge adjourned it to 16 July.

On 16 July, the case was again fixed for today (Friday), when proceedings stalled again due to defence lawyer, Mr Daudu’s absence.

Mr Suswam served as the member of the House of Representatives representing Katsina-Ala/Ukum/Logo before becoming governor in 2007. He was governor between 2007 and 2015, during which he allegedly committed the offences for which he is being prosecuted.

He lost the election to the Senate to represent Benue North-East after completing his second term as governor in 2015.

But while standing trial in the last 11 years, 61-year-old Mr Suswam, won the senatorial election to represent the Benue North-East Sena in the Nigerian Senate for one term, between 2019 and 2023.

In March 2024, Mr Suswam declared intention to contest for the position of the chairmanship of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), the platform on which he has won all his previous elections. His bid to lead the PDP was unsuccessful.

World.title: Ekiti to cut transport fare by 50%, rolls out 15 CNG buses
World.content:
The Ekiti State Government has begun efforts to cut transport fares by 50 per cent across the state by deploying Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) buses to cushion the effect of transportation costs on residents.

The state governor, Biodun Oyebanji, said the deployment of the buses, which coincided with the nation’s Independence Day and the 30th anniversary of the state’s creation, marks a major step in the government’s move to reduce transport costs for the people, in line with President Bola Tinubu’s directives.

He added that the state has begun cutting transport fares by 59 per cent through the roll-out of 15 CNG buses donated by the federal government as part of efforts to promote affordable and accessible public transportation.

He said the state would expand the fleet to serve residents better.

Mr Oyebanji, accompanied by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, at the official flag-off of the vehicles at the Ekiti State Transportation Agency premises in Ado Ekiti, said the government would continue to explore ways to reduce the burden on citizens.

Speaking with journalists shortly after inspecting the fleet, the governor thanked President Tinubu for the intervention, noting that the buses would significantly reduce the burden of transportation on the people.

He added that the initiative demonstrates the commitment of both the state and federal government to improving the welfare of the people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He added that the CNG buses would provide a more affordable means of transportation for residents across the state, urging the drivers’ union to ensure the gains are passed on to commuters.

Mr Oyebanji, who also inspected ongoing projects in different parts of the state after inspecting the CNG buses, hailed President Tinubu’s economic policies, which he said provide more resources to the state to carry out our programme and projects that have a direct impact on the people.

“No matter how visionary a leader is, if there are no resources to work with, it will just stay in the realm of a vision. But the President has been helping and supporting us not only in Ekiti State but in all the states in the country to translate our vision into action and impact for the people.

READ ALSO: Ekiti Govt distributes 100 operational vehicles to security agencies

“The President charged all state governors that by 1 October, we should find a way of reducing transportation cost because most of the implications we are witnessing, transportation contributes a lot to it, and what we have done today is just the pilot: 15 CNG buses, which are going to be distributed to the unions, and the agency will manage it.

“My appeal is to the Unions; they should allow the gains to translate to the commuters because this will reduce transportation cost by 50 per cent,” he said.

Speaking on the deployment of the buses, the Director-General of the Ekiti State Transportation Agency, Tajudeen Akingbolu, said routes had been mapped out for the CNG buses to operate from Ado Ekiti to Lagos, Ibadan, Onitsha and Abuja, adding that the initiative would provide residents with more affordable and reliable interstate transportation while reducing the burden of high transport fares.

World.title: Lagos Coastal Highway crash kills one, injures three
World.content:
One person was killed and three others injured on Friday after a Lexus SUV crashed along the Lagos Coastal Road, inward Eko Hotel.

According to a statement on Friday by the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) spokesperson, Adebayo Taofiq, the grey Lexus 350, with registration number LSD 554 KV, lost control, hit a roadside pole and overturned.

Mr Taofiq stated that officials from the agency came to the scene after receiving information about the crash.

He said good Samaritans helped to bring the three injured victims out of the vehicle before they were taken to Duck-Yard Hospital in the military zone for treatment.

Security personnel from Victoria Island also assisted at the scene, while LASTMA officials removed the wrecked vehicle from the road.

The crash comes weeks after the federal government warned motorists against violating safety rules on the Lagos section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Road.

READ ALSO: Explosion as vehicle crashes into gas shop in Abuja

The Federal Controller of Works in Lagos, Olufemi Dare, had said some motorists were driving at about 120 km/h on the road, despite the 30 km/h speed limit.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

A similar fatal crash occurred on the coastal road in August when a speeding trailer reportedly lost control and hit a Toyota mini truck. One person was killed and two others were injured.

LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, commiserated with the family of the deceased and urged motorists to avoid excessive speed and reckless driving.

The agency also asked motorists and other road users to report crashes, broken-down vehicles and obstructions through its toll-free line, 3367.

World.title: Oyo govt impounds 20 cows in operations against open grazing, crop destruction
World.content:
The Oyo State Government has impounded 20 cows in two separate operations in Ibadan following complaints of open grazing, cattle rearing in residential areas and destruction of farm crops.

The operations, carried out by the Oyo State Rule of Law Enforcement Authority (OYRLEA) in collaboration with security operatives, occurred within 24 hours at Batake Village along the Ibadan-Eruwa Road and Idi-Iroko in the Moniya area of Ibadan.

According to a statement issued by OYRLEA on Thursday, nine cows were impounded at Batake Village on Wednesday after Adewolu Farms petitioned the authority over the alleged repeated invasion of its farmland by cattle.

The farm, according to the authority, grows cassava, maize, yam and cashew. The authority said its officials and security personnel arrived at the village at dawn following the complaint and found cattle being kept at the location.

“Upon sighting the team, the herders attempted to move the herd away, but nine cows were successfully impounded.”

In a separate operation carried out by the authority at Idi-Iroko, Moniya, 11 cows were impounded over alleged open grazing and rearing of cattle within a residential area.

The latest enforcement comes amid a series of operations by the authority against open grazing and cattle rearing in parts of Oyo State.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In September, OYRLEA impounded 10 cows in the Arola area of Apete, Ibadan, following a petition from residents who complained about cattle rearing in a densely populated neighbourhood and open grazing. The authority said its team found evidence supporting the complaints.

Also, in July, the authority also impounded 19 cows in Iseyin after a farmer complained that grazing cattle repeatedly destroyed farmlands.

The authority said its latest operations were part of its enforcement of the Oyo State Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law, 2019.

“OYRLEA reaffirmed its commitment to enforcing the Oyo State Open Rearing and Grazing Regulation Law, 2019, to protect residents, farmers and lawful economic activities.”

World.title: Katsina approves solar equipment for public facilities, targets 70MW
World.content:
The Katsina State Executive Council has approved the procurement and installation of solar power and battery storage systems at 11 public facilities.

The approval was among decisions taken at the council’s meeting on Wednesday.

The meeting was chaired by Governor Dikko Radda, according to a statement by his spokesperson, Ibrahim Mohammed.

Briefing journalists after the meeting, the governor’s adviser on power and energy, Hafiz Ahmed, said the equipment would support a solar programme with a combined capacity of 20 megawatts.

He said an assessment found that the facilities accounted for 93.4 per cent of the state government’s electricity expenditure.

Facilities mentioned in the statement include Umaru Musa Yar’Adua University, Hassan Usman Katsina Polytechnic, General Amadi Rimi Hospital, Turai Yar’Adua Maternity Hospital, the House of Assembly and the state High Court.

It also listed three waterworks and a booster station.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ahmed projected savings of about N7 billion from reduced spending on grid electricity and diesel generators. However, the statement did not specify the period covered by that estimate.

He said the investment could be recovered through savings on electricity and diesel costs in approximately three and a half years.

The statement did not disclose the cost of the latest equipment approval, the contractor or the completion deadline.

A solar programme covering 11 public facilities had previously been announced in August 2025 as part of a N19.9 billion renewable energy approval.

That announcement provided for 20.1MW of solar capacity with battery storage at the facilities, alongside an additional 10MW of solar power at Lambar Rimi.

The latest statement did not explain whether the newly approved equipment was included in the earlier contract.

Mr Ahmed also said the state had achieved more than 30MW of generation capacity and was targeting 70MW by 2031 under an Integrated Resource Plan developed with Power Africa.

The Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Surajo Abukur, announced the approval of a N10,000 monthly allowance for 2,500 young people.

Payments to the stated number of beneficiaries would amount to N25 million monthly. The statement did not disclose the selection criteria, commencement date or duration of the scheme.

Mr Abukur said the council also approved an inter-ward football tournament to encourage young people’s participation in organised sports.

On education, the Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Yusuf Jibia, said contracts were approved for external works at the special model secondary schools in Jikamshi and Dumurkul to prepare them for opening.

The council also adopted recommendations on teachers’ English language proficiency, school leadership, recruitment and deployment.

The Commissioner for Health, Musa Adamu, said approvals covered renovation and additional buildings at the general hospitals in Jibia, Batsari and Ingawa.

Other health projects include upgrading the Primary Health Care Centre in Bindawa to a maternal and child hospital and renovating doctors’ quarters at General Hospital, Katsina.

The council approved the purchase of an asphalt paver for the Katsina State Roads Maintenance Agency and motorcycles for the state’s 34 local government areas. The statement did not specify the number of motorcycles.

It also approved a review of the additional contract sum for construction work at Katsina House in Abuja, citing an expanded scope of work. Neither the previous nor the revised amount was disclosed.

World.title: 15 farmers killed by terrorists in Borno laid to rest
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Suspected members of Boko Haram/ISWAP terrorists have reportedly killed 15 farmers around Ala and Musune wards of Marte Local Government Area of Borno State.

Our correspondent gathered that the victims mostly slaughtered were ambushed on their farmlands on Wednesday evening, but due to lack of telecommunication, information on the incident was delayed.

According to sources, only 15 bodies out of the 18 persons who went to their farmlands were recovered and buried on Thursday according to Islamic rites, with three others still missing.

The Public Relations Officer of the Borno state police command, ASP Nahum Daso who confirmed the incident to Journalists on Friday, said efforts are ongoing to recover the remaining bodies.

“Yes, there was an attack in Marte. 15 people were killed while others are still missing. Efforts are ongoing to determine their whereabouts,” he said.

The PPRO said details of the incident were still sketchy, adding that the police will update members of the public as soon as data gathering is complete.

Meanwhile, human rights organisation Amnesty International has condemned the attack while describing the killing as horrific.

In a statement on Friday, the organisation said the killing constitutes a grave violation of international humanitarian law.

“Amnesty International strongly condemns the horrific of at least 15 people killing on Thursday, 1 October 2026, in Marte Local Government Area of Borno State, Northeast Nigeria,” the statement reads.

“The victims, who were local residents venturing into the surrounding bush to gather firewood to earn a living or cook for their families, were ambushed and targeted by suspected Boko Haram group,” it added.

It further noted that the targeting of civilians by non-state actors constitutes a grave violation of international humanitarian law.

“Amnesty International calls on the Nigerian authorities to take immediate, transparent, and human-rights-compliant measures to protect vulnerable communities living in the region,” the statement said.

World.title: Imo abduction: Oyo govt condemns kidnapping of Oyo corps members
World.content:
Oyo State Government has expressed deep concern over the abduction of some corps members of Oyo State origin in Imo, describing the incident as distressing and reprehensible.

This is contained in a statement issued in Ibadan on Friday by the state Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade.

The state government, which condemned the abduction in strong terms, says its heart is with the affected young Nigerians and their families.

According to the statement, the government is in close communication with relevant security agencies, the Imo Government, and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) leadership to ensure a coordinated and urgent response.

“We are fully committed to securing the safe release of our children and will stop at nothing to ensure that they are reunited with their families without harm,” the statement read.

It stated that Gov. Seyi Makinde has directed that all necessary resources be deployed to this effect.

The governor, the statement said, has emphasised that the safety and well-being of every indigene of the state, within and outside its borders, remains a top priority.

The government urged families of the abducted corps members to remain calm, assuring them that the state is actively engaged on all fronts to secure their release.

It also called on security agencies to intensify efforts to rescue the victims and bring the perpetrators to justice. (NAN)

World.title: Ogun NNPP guber candidate, Rotham withdraws suit against Yayi
World.content:
…..says Ogun West agenda bigger than personal ambition

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Akinbola Hammed Rotham, has withdrawn a suit challenging the eligibility of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, to contest the governorship election.

Rotham said his decision to withdraw Suit No. FHC/AB/CS/135/2026 was taken in the interest of the Ogun West agenda and the broader development of Ogun State.

Speaking at a press conference in Abeokuta, Rotham said continuing with the case would not necessarily serve the collective aspiration of the people of Ogun West Senatorial district, which, according to him, has waited for about 50 years to produce a governor of the state.

“My decision to withdraw Suit No. FHC/AB/CS/135/2026, challenging the eligibility of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, was taken strictly in the best interest of the Ogun West agenda and the future of Ogun State,” he said.

Rotham described Yayi as his brother and fellow contestant, stressing that their political rivalry should not undermine the unity needed to advance Ogun West’s interests.

“Senator Yayi and I are both sons of Ogun West and contestants in the 2027 Ogun State governorship election. I strongly believe that the collective aspiration of Ogun West to produce a governor of Ogun State, after 50 years of waiting, is greater than any individual ambition,” he said.

According to him, “the Ogun West agenda must come before personal political interests.”

He also called for a shift away from what he described as divisive arguments surrounding place of birth, parental origin and indigeneship in political contests.

Rotham said: “I also believe that our democracy must mature beyond unnecessary sentiments and controversies over where an individual was born, where his parents came from, or questions of indigeneship being used as political weapons.

“Developmental democracy should focus on competence, capacity, character, accountability and the ability to deliver good governance, rather than divisive sentiments.”

The NNPP candidate said he had reflected on the implications of continuing with the legal action before deciding to withdraw it.

“Having reflected deeply on the matter, I concluded that continuing Suit No. FHC/AB/CS/135/2026 would not necessarily serve the larger interest of Ogun West or contribute positively to the development of our democratic culture.

“Therefore, I decided to halt the process in the interest of peace, unity and developmental democracy,” he said.

Rotham said the withdrawal should not be interpreted as an abandonment of his political ambition, adding that he remained committed to contesting the 2027 governorship election.

“My decision is also consistent with the philosophy of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP). Other political parties are not our enemies; they are sister political parties,” he said.

“As an opposition party, our responsibility is not simply to oppose for the sake of opposition, but to engage constructively whenever such cooperation can advance the interests of our people and our country.”

He also acknowledged the leadership of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the leadership and founding vision of the NNPP under Dr Boniface Aniebonam Okechukwu.

Rotham said he was particularly mindful of the fact that Senator Yayi belongs to the political family of the President.

“Since Senator Yayi belongs to the political family of Mr. President, I do not want unnecessary political distractions to come from us in the NNPP, particularly when such distractions could undermine the broader interest of Ogun State and Ogun West,” he said.

He subsequently extended what he described as “a hand of brotherhood, friendship and constructive engagement” to Yayi.

“Let us compete fairly. Let us respect one another. Let us put Ogun State first,” Rotham said.

Rotham reiterated his commitment to the 2027 governorship contest and said he would continue to advocate for what he described as a better Ogun State.

He said the withdrawal of the suit should be viewed within the broader context of unity and collective political aspirations in Ogun West.

“This is not about one man. It is about our people. It is not about personal ambition. It is about collective destiny. It is not about division. It is about unity and progress,” he said.

Rotham added that he looked forward to meeting Yayi and engaging with him as “a brother and fellow contestant,” and expressed readiness to work with stakeholders committed to Ogun State’s development.

World.title: Court remands alleged fake JAMB registrar in Kuje prison
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered a remand of Arinze Nwogba in Kuje Correctional Centre for allegedly impersonating Prof. Segun Aina, Registrar of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB).

Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a short ruling, held that Nwogba would be in custody pending the ruling on his bail application which was moved by his lawyer, Christian Ejike.

Justice Ibrahim then fixed Oct. 7 at noon for a ruling on the application and adjourned the matter until Oct. 19 for commencement of his trial.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the Inspector-General (I-G) of Police had, in the charge marked: FHC/ABJ/CR/612/2026, sued Nwogba as sole defendant.

The I-G, in the charge dated Sept. 18 and filed Sept. 21 by Samuel Mallum, preferred six counts against the defendant.

In one of the counts, Nwogba, who resides at No. 16, Emeka Egbe by Roban Stores, Abakaliki in Ebonyi, and others now at large, were alleged to have, sometime in the year 2026, fraudulently impersonated the JAMB Registrar, Prof. Aina.

The defendant was alleged to have registered his picture on WhatsApp profile and Truecaller on telephone number: 08139433155 with the intent to gain financial advantage for himself.

The offence is said to be contrary to and punishable under Section 22(3)(a)(b) & (4) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc) Act, 2015 Amended 2024.

When the case was called, the police lawyer, Nonso Eleodimuo, informed the court that the matter was scheduled for Nwogba’s arraignment.

The defence lawyer did not oppose the application.

After the charge was read to him, Nwogba pleaded not guilty to all six counts and the prosecuting counsel sought a trial date.

Responding, Ejike did not raise objection to Eleodimuo’s application for a date for trial but he told the court that he had a motion for bail filed on Sept. 23.

The lawyer said the prosecution had been served and responded to their application for bail.

Eleodimuo, who acknowledged the receipt of the bail application, said a counter affidavit, dated Oct. 2, had also been filed and served on the defence.

After moving the application, Ejike prayed the court to admit Nwogba to bail on liberal terms.

The Prosecution Counsel in his response, urged the court to dismiss Nwogba’s application for bail.

In a counter affidavit deposed to by Gregory Woje, a clerk at the Directorate of Legal Services, Force Headquarters in Abuja, stated that majority of the paragraphs in Nwogba’s affidavit in support of his bail application were false.

Woje averred that the defendant’s affidavit was speculative and were facts within the knowledge of the defendant, which are extraneous to the case.

The officer told the court that if granted bail, there was likelihood of Nwogba evading justice.

He added that the defendant would not appear in court to stand trial for the case against him.

“That assuming the court is minded to grant bail, it is for the court to do so considering the punishment upon conviction and upon terms that will ensure the defendant/applicant attend his trial,” he said.

Woje stated that bail conditions are at the discretion of the court and not for the defendant to decide.

The officer said the I-G was ready “to prosecute the case expeditiously as all the exhibits and witnesses are ready for the trial.”

“That if the defendant/applicant is granted bail and abscond from trial, it will be a clog on the whole proceedings before this court.

“That the complainant/redpondent will be prejudiced if the application of the applicant is granted,” he said.

Justice Ibrahim after listening to the parties’ arguments, adjourned until Oct. 7 for ruling on the bail and fixed Oct. 19 for trial.

The prosecution, in the brief facts of the case, said a petition was written and submitted to the I-G by the board registrar concerning the activities of some suspected criminal gangs who fraudulently registered and are using the telephone number 08139433155 and using the name and pictures of Prof. Aina without his knowledge and authority.

The police alleged that these individuals were using the identity of the JAMB registrar to deceive unsuspecting members of the public.

It said they equally went on LinkedIn and published the said number where they directed unsuspecting innocent citizens to contact them only through WhatsApp using the number.

“The investigating team decided to engage the fraudsters directly using the WhatsApp number he advertised on LinkedIn.

“The fraudsters who already used the image of JAMB registrar as profile pictures both on WhatsApp and Truecaller in order to deceive innocent Nigerians informed his victims that he wants to offer them a contract and he has obtained necessary approvals from the Minister of Education.”

According to the document, in his text message on WhatsApp, he stated, “Federal Ministry of Education Abuja has approved the supply of 200 units of HP laptops to us as a part of our digitization programs.”

It alleged that the acclaimed JAMB registrar also sent the contact of his personal assistant as (07017626031) who he described as Dr Stephen Igwe and who would be representing him to make all the arrangements for the award of the contract.

“He equally directed that his PA will send an account number where he directed the sum of N900,000 to be paid for handshake.

“He equally ordered the payment of another three (3) million naira into the account for the Permanent Secretary and Minister of Education.

“He equally sent an Access Bank account number 1572799985 with account name: EDEH CHIMEZIE BENEDICT.

“He requested for an initial deposit of nine hundred thousand naira (N900,000) to be used to bribe the members of staff at the minister’s office,” the prosecution alleged, among others.

It said Nwogba whose operational name was Dr. Stephen Igwe, was subsequently arrested in Abakaliki in Ebonyi.

“He confessed that the account details belong to his late nephew who died in April 2026 and was buried on July 31st, 2026.

“He admitted that he actually forwarded the details of the account to his cousin, one NNABUIFE NWEKPA ‘M’ of Onitsha, Anambra State, to use for the fraudulent activity.

“The said NNABUIFE NWEKPA (the acclaimed fake JAMB Registrar) is now on the run and currently at large.

“Serious efforts are being intensified to arrest the fleeing suspect,” the police said. (NAN)

World.title: Man City verdict a ‘big topic’ for England players, says Tuchel
World.content:
England’s German head coach Thomas Tuchel attends a press conference at Wembley Stadium, north west London, on September 18, 2026, ahead of their Nations League fixture against Spain. (Photo by Brook Mitchell / AFP) / NOT FOR MARKETING OR ADVERTISING USE / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE

Thomas Tuchel said that Manchester City were the talk of the England camp after the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, but insisted that the case would not affect his selection for Saturday’s match in Croatia.

The findings by an independent commission, announced earlier this week, have sent shockwaves through English football.

City, the dominant Premier League force over the past 15 years, face severe sanctions, which could include expulsion from the top division.

Marc Guehi and Elliott Anderson are the only two City players remaining in Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League match in Rijeka after Nico O’Reilly was forced to withdraw due to injury.

“We had some time off and some time between the matches, and it’s a big subject,” Tuchel told his pre-match press conference on Friday.

“Of course the players talk about it, and City players talk about it, and we talk to them, but only briefly.

“They’re ready to go for tomorrow, that’s what they show on the pitch and that’s what they show in camp, but of course it’s a big topic.”

City deny wrongdoing and on Friday lodged an appeal against the ruling.

But unless they can overturn the decision of the commission, they are likely to face at least a points deduction, which would threaten their place in the Premier League.

Tuchel was asked if the club’s players would still be in his mind for selection should they be playing regularly in the lower divisions.

“There’s always a possibility,” he said. “I think I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament, and I will never rule out that they don’t play in the top flight in their country.

“So we need to look at this from case by case.”

England’s clash with Croatia, which will take place behind closed doors, is their third of four Nations League games in the current international window.

The Three Lions were beaten 3-2 by world champions Spain on home soil last weekend, but bounced back to beat the Czech Republic 2-0 on Tuesday.

AFP

World.title: FIFA blocks Argentina’s plan to retire Messi’s iconic No. 10
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

FIFA has blocked Argentina’s plan to permanently retire Lionel Messi’s iconic No. 10 shirt after the Inter Miami forward decided to end his international career.

According to Goal, the Argentine Football Association wanted to retire the number as a tribute to Messi after more than two decades with the national team; however, FIFA regulations prevent teams from permanently retiring numbers within the required squad range at major international tournaments.

Messi, 39, announced on August 31 that he was retiring from international football. He is expected to make his farewell appearance before the Argentine public on October 6 when Argentina face Benin in a friendly at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Messi has made 207 appearances for Argentina and scored 125 goals during his international career, wearing the iconic No. 10 shirt for much of his time with the national team.

However, FIFA rules require teams at international final tournaments to assign squad numbers from 1 to 26, meaning Argentina cannot permanently remove the No. 10 from its squad numbers.

Liberia encountered a similar situation after retiring the No. 14 shirt in honour of former striker and president George Weah. FIFA regulations subsequently required the number to be used during the country’s 2026 World Cup qualifying campaign.

Argentina can leave the No. 10 shirt vacant for some friendly matches, but it must be assigned during major international tournaments.

Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni has yet to announce who will inherit Messi’s famous shirt.

“We are not obliged to assign it for the upcoming matches, so we will give it to no one until after Leo’s farewell match. We just have not yet decided who,” Scaloni said, according to Goal.

However, ESPN Argentina reporter Federico Bueno reported that Nico Paz is the leading candidate if Scaloni extends his contract as Argentina coach.

“If Scaloni extends his contract as Argentina head coach, then Nico Paz will be the new number 10. That has been decided internally,” Bueno said, according to Goal.

Paz, 22, has made 11 appearances for Argentina and scored once. The attacking midfielder previously played for Real Madrid before joining Italian club Como permanently.

The No. 10 shirt has been associated with some of Argentina’s greatest footballers, including Diego Maradona, before Messi inherited the iconic number.

World.title: Olu Jacobs laid to rest in Lagos
World.content:
Veteran actor Olu Jacobs has been buried in Lagos following a funeral service held on Friday.

The funeral service took place at the Freedom Centre in Lekki, where family members, colleagues, friends, dignitaries and several stars of the Nigerian film industry gathered to honour the late actor.

Jacobs died in September at the age of 82 after a career spanning several decades and earning him recognition as one of Nigeria’s most respected actors.

Among those who attended the funeral were Lagos State Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat and former Ogun State Governor Ibikunle Amosun.

Nollywood personalities at the ceremony included Shaffy Bello, Keppy Ekpeyong, Stan Nze, Morayo Afolabi-Brown, Ireti Doyle, Lala Akindoju, Kate Henshaw, OC Ukeje, Patrick Doyle, Stephanie Okereke and Ernest Obi.

The funeral followed a night of tributes and a service of songs held on Wednesday to celebrate Jacobs and his contributions to the Nigerian entertainment industry.

Born in 1942 to parents from Egba Alake, Jacobs spent his early years in Kano, where he attended Holy Trinity School.

His passion for the performing arts developed after he watched a Hubert Ogunde concert party performance at the Colonial Hotel in Kano. He subsequently moved to England, where he trained as an actor at The Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London.

Jacobs began building his stage career in the 1970s. In 1972, he played The Boy in ‘A Taste of Honey’ at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield.

He later appeared in a number of British television productions, including ‘The Goodies,’ ‘Till Death Us Do Part’ and ‘Barlow at Large.’

In 1978, he portrayed President Mageeba in Michael Codron’s presentation of Sir Tom Stoppard’s play ‘Night and Day’.

After returning to Nigeria in 1990, Jacobs featured in the NTA detective series ‘The Third Eye’ before becoming a prominent figure in the country’s emerging Nollywood industry.

He went on to act in hundreds of films and established himself as one of the most acclaimed performers in Nigerian cinema.

His career earned him several honours, including the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2021 Africa International Film Festival (AFRIFF) and an Icon Award from the Audio-Visual Rights Society of Nigeria (AVRS) in 2022.

At the 2023 AMVCA, Jacobs received the Industry Merit Award in recognition of his outstanding contribution to acting.

World.title: Adebayo urges IGP to rescue abducted corps members
World.content:
Adewole Adebayo

By John Alechenu, Abuja

ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Prince Adewole Adebayo, has called on the Inspector-General of Police and other security agencies to urgently rescue National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members abducted in Imo State.

The corps members, graduates of tertiary institutions in Oyo State, were reportedly travelling from Ibadan to the NYSC orientation camp in Bende, Abia State, when they were ambushed at about 6:30 a.m. on October 1 along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway, around Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area of Imo State.

Ten of the victims were reportedly rescued at the scene by security operatives, while others remained in captivity.

Adebayo condemned the incident in a statement issued on Friday by the Head of Media and Communications of the Adewole Adebayo-Bugaje Presidential Campaign, Comrade Mark Adebayo.

He described the attack as unacceptable and called for immediate deployment of security resources to secure the release of the remaining corps members.

“This cowardly attack on young citizens serving their fatherland is an unacceptable assault on the nation’s future,” he said.

Adebayo urged the Inspector-General of Police, the military high command and the Imo State Commissioner of Police to deploy all available rapid-response assets to secure the victims’ release.

He said security agencies must act with urgency because of the vulnerability of the abducted corps members.

“We cannot fold our arms while the youth of this nation, who have committed themselves to national integration and service, are hunted down like game on public highways.

“Our security agencies must act with absolute urgency. This is a race against time, and no stone must be left unturned until every single corps member is brought back alive,” he said.

The SDP candidate also appealed to the governors of Anambra, Abia and Imo states to prioritise efforts to rescue the abducted corps members.

He urged the governors to suspend political disagreements and deploy available state security resources in support of the rescue operation.

“I am calling on the Governors of Anambra, Abia, and Imo states to drop everything they are doing right now. Shut down governance if you must, suspend political bickerings, and concentrate 100 per cent of your state security resources on rescuing these young Nigerians,” Adebayo said.

He stressed that the security and welfare of citizens should remain the primary responsibility of government.

“The primary purpose of government is the security and welfare of the people. Right now, your children are in the den of kidnappers; nothing else should matter until they are safely recovered,” he stated.

World.title: Nigeria at 66: Our Problems Stem From Failure of Values, Principles, Says Dan Kanu
World.content:
*Faults 3-day warning strike by civil servants

Chuks Okocha in Abuja

Chairman of the New Deal Organization, Prince Daniel Kanu, has blamed Nigeria’s persistent challenges on the failure of good values and principles across society, saying the country’s problems cannot be solved through politics, strikes and constant finger-pointing.

Kanu said Nigerians must look beyond government for solutions and accept their own responsibility for rebuilding the country, especially by putting national interest above ethnic, religious and political considerations.

In an Independence Day message signed by him, Kanu described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s 66th anniversary address as sincere and progressive, urging Nigerians to support legitimate institutions and leadership while playing their part in fixing the country.

“Nigeria is where it is today because Nigerians have failed themselves at virtually every level—both those in government and those outside government. We must learn to tell ourselves the truth and stop indulging in self-deception,” he said.

Kanu also questioned the three-day warning strike announced by the Joint National Public Service Negotiating Council, JNPSNC, over demands it said the government had failed to meet by September 30, 2026.

“It is rather ironic that some of the people who should be working within the system to help fix our systemic problems are going on strike to compel someone else to fix problems that are, in part, within their own areas of responsibility,” he said.

He said Nigeria’s development was being undermined by the absence of values, including integrity, honesty, competence, accountability, compassion and respect for rules.

“The solution to Nigeria’s problems therefore depends on the deliberate inculcation and practice of values and principles such as integrity, honesty, respect, competence, compassion, empathy, accountability, and customer service,” Kanu said.

While acknowledging the hardship facing Nigerians, particularly the less privileged, Kanu said the country’s problems did not begin with the present administration and would not be solved by politics or industrial action.

He urged Nigerians to take responsibility for building the country, quoting former United States President John F. Kennedy: “Ask not what your country can do for you—ask what you can do for your country.”

Kanu said Nigeria’s abundant natural and human resources would remain insufficient without responsible citizens and institutions, urging Nigerians to put the country first and rally around the Constitution in the interest of present and future generations. ‎

World.title: Maryam Abacha: Court Orders Takeover of Disputed Victoria Island Property
World.content:
Restrains firm from selling, transferring property pending suit

Wale Igbintade

The Federal High Court in Lagos has appointed a Receiver/Manager to take possession and control of a disputed property at No. 68 Molade Okoya Thomas Street, off Ajose Adeogun Street, Victoria Island, Lagos, in a suit filed by Mrs Maryam Sani Abacha against Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited.

Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa, in an interim order issued on September 29, 2026, restrained Levitikal Realties, its directors, agents, representatives, servants and persons acting through it from selling, transferring, assigning, mortgaging, leasing, charging, alienating or otherwise encumbering the property pending the hearing and determination of the applicant’s Motion on Notice for interlocutory injunction.

The order was made in Suit No. FHC/LAG/CS/1245/2026, in which Abacha is the Plaintiff/Applicant and Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited is the Defendant/Respondent.

The property is covered by a Certificate of Occupancy dated July 4, 1988, and registered as No. 32 at Page 32 in Volume 1988B of the Lands Registry Office, Lagos State.

The court’s intervention followed an ex-parte application filed by Abacha on September 10, 2026, through her counsel, Adedayo Adesina, SAN.

In addition to restraining the defendant from dealing with the property, Justice Lewis-Allagoa barred it from taking any step or carrying out any act calculated to interfere with, overreach, dissipate, assign, transfer, sell, alienate, encumber or otherwise prejudice the subject matter of the originating summons.

In a significant aspect of the order, the judge appointed the Deputy Chief Registrar of the Federal High Court, or any officer of the court serving as Official Receiver, as Receiver/Manager to take possession, custody and control of the disputed property pending the hearing and final determination of the Motion on Notice.

Alternatively, the court approved the appointment of the property management company of Bola Adebule & Company, Estate Surveyors & Valuers, or any other fit and reputable property management firm registered with the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Agency, LASRERA, to take possession and control of the property.

Justice Lewis-Allagoa further restrained Levitikal Realties from representing or holding itself out to any third party as the owner of the property with the capacity to sell, transfer, mortgage, lease, alienate or otherwise encumber it.

The order arose against the backdrop of a Notice of Dispute and Request for Mediation and/or Arbitration dated September 7, 2026, concerning the property.

The dispute reportedly originated from a joint venture arrangement for the development of a high-rise property on the site.

According to the account contained in the court processes, the landowner subsequently terminated the joint venture agreement over alleged fundamental breaches by the developer, Levitikal Realties & Construction Limited.

The court processes further indicate that the dispute has generated parallel legal and alternative dispute-resolution proceedings, including the Federal High Court action and arbitration proceedings.

Levitikal Group identifies Samuel Mawuyon Ajose as its Chairman and Chief Executive Officer and describes the group as having interests including construction and real estate.

Ajose also publicly described himself in January 2026 as the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Levitikal Group while declaring his interest in the 2027 Lagos governorship race.

The property has also previously attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC.

Media reports in August 2026 said EFCC operatives had marked the Victoria Island development with a warning directing persons to keep off amid an alleged investigation.

Those reports, however, did not establish a final finding of wrongdoing against any party.

Against that background, the latest Federal High Court order places further restrictions on dealings involving the property while the substantive dispute remains pending.

Justice Lewis-Allagoa also authorised Abacha to publish the court’s orders in national newspapers and online media circulating in Nigeria to notify members of the public, prospective purchasers, lenders, investors and other interested parties of the pending proceedings and her interest in the property.

The judge further directed the Nigeria Police Force, including the Inspector General of Police, the Assistant Inspector General of Police, Zone 2, and the Commissioner of Police, Lagos State, as well as the EFCC and other relevant law-enforcement agencies, to provide adequate security and assistance to the applicant and the Deputy Sheriff of the Federal High Court for the implementation and enforcement of the orders.

The court reached its decision after considering the affidavit filed in support of the application, sworn to by Sadiq Mohammed Abacha, as well as the submissions of Adesina, SAN, on behalf of the applicant.

The matter has been adjourned until November 9, 2026.

World.title: Fertility Specialist, Musician Daramola Marks 40, Keeps Dreams Alive
World.content:
Founder and Medical Director of Greenleaf Fertility Clinic and Wellness Centre, Ikorodu, Dr. Adeleke Daramola Luke, has marked his 40th birthday, celebrating a career highlighted by over 300 successful live births through in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) alongside an active pursuit in the Nigerian music industry.

Widely known as ‘Dr. Global’ on social media, Daramola has built his medical career around reproductive medicine and assisted conception, helping couples achieve parenthood after years of fertility challenges.

Born into the royal family of Oba Adewumi Daramola, the Onigbemo of Igbemo-Ekiti, Dr. Daramola earned his medical degree from the University of Lagos.

He subsequently undertook specialized postgraduate training in reproductive medicine across Germany and the United Kingdom before returning to Nigeria to establish his medical practice.

Alongside his medical practice, Daramola has maintained a longstanding passion for music.

In 2015, he emerged as a runner-up in an MTN music talent competition, where he performed on stage alongside established Nigerian artists including Humblesmith and Harrysong.

He has continued to write and record music, with his latest artistic venture being a collaboration with Afro-fusion artiste, Qdot.

Those close to his work described his dual path as a reflection of his drive to build a career on his own terms.

In a tribute, scientific consultant and long-time friend, Dr. Adetokunbo Soyoye, said Adeleke’s rare blend of medicine and creative arts is a testament to what happens when vision meets relentless drive.

​”Adeleke is a goal-getter, completely unashamed about pursuing his dreams,” he said.

World.title: Ogun PDP Deputy Gov Candidate, Sowunmi-Kolapo, Installed as Muslim Council Grand Matron
World.content:
Ĥ.Urges Ogun indigenes to shun money politics, protect their heritage

The Ogun State Muslim Council has installed the Peoples Democratic Party’s deputy governorship candidate for the 2027 election, Hajia Lateefat ‘Yemi Sowunmi-Kolapo, as its Grand Matron (Egba Zone).

Sowunmi-Kolapo, who is the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and Ameerah of Ogun State, was installed and decorated at the Ake Palace, Abeokuta, on Thursday, October 1, 2026.

The ceremony, which attracted Muslim leaders, political stakeholders, traditional figures and other members of the community, was held under the theme, “Socio-Economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security.”

The installation has assumed political significance, coming ahead of the 2027 governorship election, with Sowunmi-Kolapo using the occasion to call for increased civic participation among Muslims and urging voters to reject electoral violence, vote-buying and political apathy.

She also urged Muslims across the state to take an active role in determining the political leadership of the country.

Speaking in an interview after her installation, the new Grand Matron described the honour as a demonstration of confidence and support from the Muslim community.

She said, “It’s a great honour for me because when people appreciate you and they show it, you can only be thankful to God and them.

“I thank the Ogun State Muslim Council for this great honour. As we were told, the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland is expected to be decorated OMC Grand Matron (Egba Zone). Our late revered mother, late Chief Khadijah Adebisi Edionseri, was the Iya Sunnah of Egbaland and OMC Grand Matron.”

“Stepping into her shoes is a big deal for me. I pray Almighty Allah guides my steps and makes the journey fruitful,” the deputy governorship candidate added.

She also expressed appreciation to members of the Muslim community for the support she had received, from the beginning of her political journey, and throughout the process leading to her installation.

“To the Muslim community, I can only say thank you to them because the shower of love and support that I got from them from the beginning of this journey is unprecedented and I don’t take it for granted,” she said.

She, however, used the occasion to broaden her message from religious leadership to civic and political participation, urging Muslims to recognise the importance of political power in protecting their interests and heritage.

The new Grand Matron said the Muslim community must not remain passive in matters concerning its future.

“An elder statesman was telling me something when I went to visit him. He said religious leaders should not sit back and think that they will hand over everything they seek to them on a platter of gold.

“If you don’t struggle for power, some oppressors will use the same power to destroy you, which is why we say our power is in our votes.”

The PDP candidate urged Muslim parents, leaders and community stakeholders to educate their children and wards on responsible democratic participation.

She said electoral participation should be peaceful and driven by citizens’ choices rather than inducements.

Earlier at the ceremony, the OMC, Egba Zone, used the occasion to draw attention to the connection between socio-economic conditions, education, security and global stability.

Earlier at the ceremony, the OMC, Egba Zone, used the occasion to draw attention to the connection between socio-economic conditions, education, security and global stability.

The guest lecturer, Sheikh Sulaimon Faruq Onikijipa, OON, who spoke on the theme, “Socio-Economic Stability: A Fortress for Global Security,” urged governments to give greater priority to security, education and the economic wellbeing of citizens.

Onikijipa said a stable society could not be achieved when citizens were denied access to quality education, security and the basic socio-economic conditions necessary for dignified living.

Also speaking at the ceremony, Senator Prof. Iyabo Obasanjo commended the Ogun State Muslim Community for honouring Sowunmi-Kolapo and giving her the blessing to serve as the PDP deputy governorship candidate.

Obasanjo described the new Grand Matron as humble, faithful and kind, while acknowledging her contributions to the Muslim community.

World.title: Group Backs NAICOM’s Regulatory Role, Retracts Call for CEO’s Removal
World.content:
The Coalition for Good Governance in Nigeria (CGGN) has reaffirmed the importance of NAICOM’s regulatory role in Nigeria’s insurance sector and retracted its earlier call for the removal of the commission’s Commissioner for Insurance and Chief Executive Officer, Mr Olusegun Ayo Omosehin.

In a statement dated September 29, 2026 and signed by Salisu Mohammed, the group withdrew its earlier demand for Omosehin’s resignation or suspension, admitting that the allegations on which the demand was based were inaccurate, incomplete and unsupported by verifiable evidence.

The coalition also retracted its characterisation of NAICOM’s regulatory actions during the recapitalisation exercise as unlawful.

“Upon rigorous internal review, further engagement with relevant documents, and careful consideration of additional facts that have since come to light, the coalition has determined that the assertions contained in that earlier statement were inaccurate, incomplete, and not supported by verifiable evidence,” CGGN said.

“We therefore withdraw the statement in its entirety.”

The group withdrew claims that NAICOM made unlawful demands, forced insurers to transfer capital into Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) escrow accounts or collected funds for consultants who were never engaged.

It also abandoned its earlier assertion that Omosehin’s continued stay in office constituted a “clear and present danger” to the insurance sector or an affront to accountability.

According to the coalition, its earlier description of NAICOM’s regulatory actions as unlawful or lacking legal foundation was based on incomplete information and a misunderstanding of the applicable legal and regulatory framework.

“The characterisation of NAICOM’s regulatory actions during the ongoing recapitalisation exercise as unlawful or lacking legal foundation was erroneous,” it said.

CGGN expressed regret over any distress, reputational harm or public anxiety its earlier statement may have caused Omosehin, NAICOM’s management and staff, insurance operators, policyholders and the general public.

It also offered an unreserved apology for publishing claims that subsequent scrutiny had shown to be incorrect.

“Good governance requires not only the courage to speak when concerns arise, but also the integrity to correct the record when those concerns are shown to be misplaced,” the coalition said.

The group formally withdrew its demand for Omosehin’s immediate resignation or suspension, as well as its suggestion that the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy should take disciplinary action against him on the basis of the earlier petition.

“We therefore retract, without reservation, every demand for the immediate resignation or suspension of the Commissioner for Insurance,” CGGN stated.

“We further withdraw any suggestion that the Honourable Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy should take disciplinary action against him on the basis of the earlier petition narrative.”

The coalition, however, said the retraction did not diminish its interest in the orderly and lawful conduct of the recapitalisation exercise.

It reaffirmed its commitment to transparency, accountability and the strengthening of Nigeria’s financial services sector, while recognising the importance of an independent and professional insurance regulator.

CGGN urged stakeholders to allow the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Federal Ministry of Finance and NAICOM to discharge their statutory responsibilities without distraction from unsubstantiated public campaigns.

It said the retraction was issued in the public interest and in the spirit of fairness and accuracy that should guide civic advocacy.

World.title: Fuel Subsidy Removal, FX Policy Aimed At Addressing Longstanding Structural Challenges in Nigeria’s Economy, Says Group
World.content:
Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

A support group, the Atiku Bagudu Grassroots Network for Tinubu 2027, has explained that the removal of fuel subsidy, foreign exchange reforms and ongoing fiscal and tax reforms were difficult decisions but necessary measures which were aimed at addressing longstanding structural challenges in the Nigerian economy.

The group named the Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Senator Atiku Bagudu, as its patron and also endorsed President Bola Tinubu for a second term, declaring its intention to mobilise 19 million votes from the 19 northern states for his re-election.

The group gave the assurance after a meeting in Abuja attended by delegates representing the 19 northern states.

At the meeting, members reviewed the administration’s policies and programmes and discussed strategies for grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

It added that its decision to support Tinubu’s re-election was based on the administration’s efforts to reposition the economy, strengthen infrastructure and implement reforms aimed at creating a more sustainable fiscal foundation for the country.

Its convener, Hon. Ali Oriri, in a statement issued Friday, said the network would build a strong grassroots structure across the north to mobilise support for Tinubu and secure the group’s target of 19 million votes.

He said the 19 million-vote target would be achievable with effective coordination and sustained mobilisation across the region.

The convener stressed that the group would take its campaign to communities across the north, engaging traditional, religious, youth and community leaders as part of its grassroots mobilisation strategy.

Oriri urged members of the network in the 19 northern states to strengthen their structures and commence sustained engagement with voters ahead of the 2027 election.

He added that the group would also continue to explain what it described as the benefits and long-term objectives of the administration’s reforms to citizens at the grassroots.

He explained: “The removal of fuel subsidy, foreign exchange reforms and ongoing fiscal and tax reforms were difficult decisions but necessary measures which were aimed at addressing longstanding structural challenges in the Nigerian economy.

The group also cited ongoing investments in roads, rail, power, housing, agriculture and other sectors as reasons for seeking continuity under Tinubu.

It was of the opinion that continuity was important to allow the reforms to mature and translate into broader economic opportunities and improved living conditions for Nigerians.

World.title: Muiz Banire at 60: Honouring A Legacy of Leadership and Impact
World.content:
Family, friends, professional colleagues, public sector leaders, and well-wishers across the nation are preparing to celebrate distinguished legal luminary, public servant, and community leader, Dr. Muiz Adeyemi Banire, as he officially marks his milestone 60th birthday.

The diamond jubilee stands as a celebration not only of six decades of life, but of a lifetime defined by unwavering integrity, purposeful leadership, legal excellence and selfless service to humanity.

​Over the past decades, Dr. Banire has distinguished himself as a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), a seasoned academic, a former cabinet officer in Lagos State, and an influential national figure. His diamond jubilee provides a moment to reflect on his contributions to constitutional law, governance, institutional reform, and youth empowerment.

Beyond his professional achievements, his legacy is firmly anchored in his passion for legal advocacy, principled public service, and mentoring the next generation of Nigerian professionals.

​In a tribute, Chief Executive Officer of Lorache Consulting, Dr. Ayo Adeyemi, congratulated Dr. Banire on reaching the milestone. Dr. Adeyemi highlighted that turning 60 is a testament to a leader’s enduring impact on society, the lives touched through mentorship, and an uncompromising commitment to national development. He wished the celebrant many more years of health, wisdom, and continued service to the nation.

​To honour Banire’s legacy, the organizers have announced the Lagos Leadership Ignite Summit 2026. Designed as an educational and inspirational conference, the virtual summit is themed ‘Lead From Within, Impact Beyond’ and will take place on October 3 and 4, 2026, from 12:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The two-day event aims to turn this milestone into an interactive platform for leadership development, ethical governance, career growth, entrepreneurship and sustainable community advancement.

​The summit will feature Dr. Frank Mba, DIG (rtd.), as Keynote Speaker, alongside a panel of expert speakers including: Grace Oluwalola, Human Development Specialist,

​Azuh Arinze, renowned author, publisher and Media Executive, Oyebola Okusanya, Corporate Governance and Management Professional, Kingsley Madu, Strategic Innovation Consultant, Omotade Makinwa, Legal Practitioner and Youth Advocate;

​Ayo Owodunni, MBET, Executive Coach and Leadership Consultant; Lady Adedoja Allen, Entrepreneur and Community Leader

​Serving as the Programme Coordinator.

Dr. Ayo Adeyemi expressed appreciation to the keynote speaker, panellists, planning committee, and media partners for assembling the initiative.

​”On behalf of the organizing committee, partners, and supporters, I extend our warmest congratulations to Dr. Muiz Adeyemi Banire, on his 60th birthday,” said Dr. Adeyemi. “We celebrate his journey, his immense contributions to legal jurisprudence, and his dedication to public good. May the years ahead bring him greater health, peace, and avenues to impact lives. We are deeply grateful to every speaker, volunteer and partner working to make this summit a reality.”

​The Lagos Leadership Ignite Summit 2026 reflects Banire’s belief that effective leadership begins with internal character and becomes meaningful through its benefit to others. Members of the public, young professionals, legal practitioners, and emerging leaders are invited to join the virtual sessions to celebrate a legal icon while gaining insights for personal and professional growth.

World.title: Akande: Govt Must Move Beyond Policies, Create Jobs, Respite Care for People with Disabilities
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

Founder and Director of Patrick’s Speech and Language Centre; and Pure Souls Learning Foundation, Dotun Akande, Thursday called for policy changes that will provide social support, respite care, education and employment opportunities for people with autism and intellectual disabilities.

Akande made the call at the Patrick’s Speech and Language Centre’s 20th anniversary RISE Summit, in Lagos, themed, ‘From Cradle to Contribution’.

She stressed the need for government to move beyond policies and ensure their effective implementation to promote inclusion of people with neurodevelopmental and intellectual disabilities.

She said the centre was shifting its focus from early intervention for children to preparing young adults and adults with disabilities for meaningful participation in society.

According to her, the theme of the anniversary, reflects the centre’s vision of ensuring that children who have benefited from its interventions eventually become active contributors to their communities.

She stated: “Many of them are part of the community. Some of them are still not part of the community because, one, parents are hiding; two, they don’t have financial support; and three, the government is not helping.”

The founder noted that despite progress in early intervention, with many children now accessing mainstream education and more organisations emerging in the neurodiversity and intellectual disability space, significant challenges remained, particularly for adults.

“We have done well with early intervention. Many children are now in mainstream schools. Many organisations have sprung up since we started to do things in the field of neurodiversity and intellectual disability. So now we are moving to the next stage, which is our children are now assuming 20. We are now looking at adults,” she said.

She urged the government to develop policies that would provide respite centres across the country, enabling parents and caregivers to temporarily place their children in safe, supportive environments when they need to travel or attend to other responsibilities.

The director explained that such centres could be operated through partnerships between government and private organisations, with appropriate systems put in place to ensure that parents remained responsible for their children.

“Our quest now is to have a policy where they can partner with private organisations. We have ways of knowing the people and ways in which we make them come back to pick their children,” she stated.

Beyond respite care, she also called for government support through housing assistance, subsidies and educational support for families raising children with disabilities.

“Authorities should review existing disability-related legislation and focus on implementation. The existence of laws alone would not guarantee inclusion.

“We have a lot of special people’s laws. Are they being practised? We need to look at it. Are they being implemented? Implementation is one of the challenges we have in this country,” Akande stressed.

She further called for legislation requiring private organisations to employ people with intellectual disabilities, arguing that employment should be based on individuals’ abilities rather than assumptions about their limitations.

She said people with intellectual disabilities could perform a range of roles depending on their capabilities, including administrative support, mailing and other workplace responsibilities.

In her keynote titled, ‘Building Strong Foundations’, Rear Admiral Itunu Hotonu (rtd) called for greater understanding, acceptance and family support for autistic children, stressing that families must move beyond stigma and misconceptions to recognise the individual needs and abilities of children on the autism spectrum.

She shared her experience as the grandmother of an autistic child, explaining that her personal journey, which began with her grandson’s diagnosis, eventually led to doctoral research on the experiences of families with level one autistic children in mainstream private schools in Lagos.

She said the initial diagnosis plunged her family into a wilderness marked by disbelief, confusion, fear and concerns about stigma, noting that her greatest challenge was not autism itself but the gap between what the family thought it knew about the condition and the reality they encountered.

According to her, the experience compelled her to question long-held assumptions about autism and disability and to embark on a process of unlearning misconceptions that had shaped her understanding of autistic people.

“I wanted to understand that wilderness. I wanted to look past the medical charts, the medical language, and explore the actual human experience of families like mine with level one autistic children,” she said.

Other speakers at the conference stressed the need for parents with children on the neuro divergent spectrum to reach out for help and speak about their journey.

“Stigma is keeping families away. We might call the children neuro divergent, but they are differently able. Don’t keep quiet. Tell your story and own your truth,” she said.

World.title: Spring allergies: Where pollen levels are highest in SA
World.content:
Tree pollen levels remain high in several parts of South Africa. Image: Pexels

Tree pollen remains the main concern for people with allergies across several parts of South Africa, with high counts continuing at inland monitoring sites.

The latest pollen report shows high or significant tree pollen in several areas, while grass and weed pollen remained consistently low across the sampled sites.

Here is what the latest pollen readings show in each area.

Cape Town

Pollen concentrations dropped sharply in Cape Town, with no peaks recorded at the monitoring site.



Trees detected included cypress, waxberry, pine, plane, yellowwood, gum and oak.

Weed pollen included the daisy family, goosefoot, erica and protea, while mould levels remained low.

Johannesburg

Johannesburg recorded another round of tree pollen peaks.

The monitoring site detected birch, false olive, bushwillow, sweetgum, pine, plane, oak, karee and elm.

Mugwort was among the weeds detected, while mould levels remained low.

Pretoria

Pretoria continued to record high tree pollen levels.



The site detected a wide range of trees, including birch, Australian pine, cypress, bushwillow, jacaranda, gum, olive, pine, yellowwood, poplar, oak, karee and elm.

Weed pollen remained low.

Mould levels were generally low, but the site recorded moderate peaks of Cladosporium, an allergenic mould.

Bloemfontein

Significant tree pollen concentrations continued in Bloemfontein, with plane the dominant tree detected.

Other trees included birch, false olive, hackberry, cypress, mulberry, waxberry, gum, olive, pine, bushwillow, yellowwood, poplar and karee.

Weed pollen and mould levels remained low.

Durban

Durban recorded significant tree pollen.

The monitoring site detected several trees, including palm, Australian pine, hackberry, birch, bushwillow, cypress, ebony, ash, mulberry, gum, pine, yellowwood, poplar and elm.

Weed pollen remained low.

The report’s overall summary noted mould peaks in Durban, although the detailed results for the city described mould levels as low.

Gqeberha

Pollen and mould levels remained low in Gqeberha.

Trees detected included acacia, Australian pine, gum, cedar, pine, cypress, olive and plane, while yellowwood was the dominant tree.

Weed pollen included sedges and mezereum.

George

The report uses two-year averages for George.

These averages show low pollen and mould concentrations.

Trees included mesquite, pecan, cypress and yellowwood, while the weeds included spurges and goosefoot.

Potchefstroom

Potchefstroom recorded high tree pollen counts, with mulberry the dominant tree at the monitoring site.

Other trees included birch, hackberry, bushwillow, cypress, ash, pine, plane, oak, karee and willow.

Weed pollen and mould levels remained low.

Kimberley

The latest report does not provide current pollen readings for Kimberley because the pollen readers were away.

Instead, it uses six-year average counts. These historical figures show that tree pollen tends to remain low in the semi-arid region at this time of year.

Trees that may occur include mulberry, pine, oak, karee, hackberry and sumac.

Where do you live, and what are pollen levels like in your area?

World.title: 70% of children born between 2018 and 2021 rely on a social grant
World.content:
Most children in South Africa rely on a social grant. Image: Pexels

In a classroom of 35 children, at least 24 will benefit from a grant.

This means most South African parents earn less than R5 900 a month.

And raises questions about how much support these children will need later in life.



Most South African Children Get a Grant

According to the South African Social Security Agency’s (SASSA) half-year report, most South African children rely on grants.

On average, 64% of the country’s children rely on a grant.

However, the report shows that for those born between 2018 and 2021, this jumps to 70%.



These 5- to 8-year-olds get more than R22 billion in support every year.

The next age group to reach 70% are 12-year-olds.

The government spends just over R5.8 billion a year supporting this age group.



The age group with the fewest beneficiaries are children under 1 year old. Only 32% get a grant in this age group.

But as children grow, so does the number of those getting grants. Children in Grade R (5-year-olds) have the highest concentration of grant beneficiaries: 71% are on a grant.

Yet only 1 school-going age category falls below the 64% average.



That’s 17-year-olds.

Only 63% of the country’s 17-year-olds get a grant. Most of these get a child support grant.

But this age group has the most foster care grant beneficiaries.



The foster care grant is awarded to foster parents with court-ordered custody of a child.

This may happen in instances where the child has been removed from the home or when both parents are deceased.

Age Birth Year % Relying on a Grant Annual Spend 5 Years 2021 71% R5.73 billion 6 Years 2020 70% R5.68 billion 7 Years 2019 70% R5.53 billion 8 Years 2018 70% R5.33 billion 12 Years 2014 70% R5.81 billion

The Impact on the Country

Understanding how many of South Africa’s children benefit from a grant can provide insight into the country’s economic future.



To be eligible for a child support grant, parents must earn less than R5 900 a month.

Married parents can’t exceed a household income of R11 900 a month.

The data suggests households with fewer resources have the most children.



In fact, the report reveals most households have more than 1 child receiving a child support grant.

There are 7 million child support grant beneficiaries, but 12.3 million children who benefit from this grant.

It also means the government will spend at least R251 billion over the next 10 years supporting the age groups with the highest percentage of grant beneficiaries.

World.title: What exactly will be stored in your new South African digital ID?
World.content:
Home Affairs has revealed what its new digital ID Wallet could contain. Image: file / canva

South Africa has given its very first look at a working digital ID, with Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber demonstrating the system through the MyMzansi Digital ID smartphone app.

The demonstration on 1 October 2026 showed what the digital ID would=d look like, while some of the features discussed by Schreiber are still part of the government’s proposed framework.

So what could eventually be stored in your new digital ID?



A new way to store documents and personal details

The digital ID profile demonstrated by Schreiber displayed his photograph, name and date of birth.

He said the photograph came directly from the Home Affairs population register, linking the digital credential to the official information held by the department.

The system is intended to be more than a photograph of a physical ID card. Schreiber described it as a remote verification tool linked to a person’s biometrics.

The proposed Wallet feature on the digital ID is intended to store a person’s Home Affairs credentials.

Schreiber said this would include another copy of their ID, as well as documents such as their birth certificate and marriage certificate.

These features form part of the department’s proposed digital ID framework, rather than documents that South Africans can currently access through a public digital ID system.



The broader plan is for the Wallet to eventually bring together multiple Home Affairs documents in one place.

What information will you be able to share from your digital ID?

The demonstration showed that a digital ID could be used to share specific information with an authorised official.

The information fields included name, surname, date of birth, sex, nationality, identity number, place of birth, photograph and issuing country.

A user receives a notification when an official requests their information and can accept or reject the request. The system also allows users to choose which information they share.

Schreiber demonstrated this using an immigration official requesting information about his nationality.

The proposed digital ID system also includes biometric security measures, including a facial biometric template and cryptographic signature.

It is also intended to be linked to a specific smartphone or other device through device binding.

Privacy has been a major concern raised around the digital ID plans. Schreiber said the system was not intended to give government unrestricted access to people’s information and stressed the role of user consent.

What is confirmed, and what isn’t?

While a working digital ID profile, identity verification, QR-code information sharing, notifications when information is requested, and the ability to accept or reject requests have already been confirmed for the new digital ID, there are still things that have not been set in stone.

The full digital Wallet containing documents such as birth and marriage certificates, wider government-service integration and the final rules governing how the system operates have only been proposed.

The full digital ID rollout is also only expected after 2030, so South Africans cannot yet 

In the meantime, the Smart ID card remains the immediate replacement for the green ID book, with production of green books ending on 31 March 2027 and the old documents becoming invalid from 31 March 2028.
