MARRAKECH — This guide is for people who live in Marrakech or are staying for weeks, not for a two-night tourist sprint. It covers the confirmed events, exhibitions and performances worth crossing the city for, with practical notes on venues, prices and how to plan around them. The focus is things to do in Marrakech October 2026.

The cultural calendar picks up in October after the summer lull. The first half of the month belongs to photography and aviation, the middle to theatre and design, and the last ten days bring poetry, music and folk traditions. One fixed-date public holiday falls in the month: Aïd Al Wahda (Unity Day) on Saturday 31 October.

1 to 10 October: Water, Photography, Air Show and a Women’s Race

Thursday 1 October to Friday 30 October Énergies Créatives Musée Mohammed VI pour la Civilisation de l’Eau au Maroc, Palmeraie · Price from the venue A month-long exhibition about water, the resource that has shaped Marrakech for centuries. It is a good reason to visit the water museum in the Palmeraie, which many residents never get around to seeing. Check opening hours directly with the museum before you go.

Sunday 4 October, from 08:30 La Kéchoise 2026 Place de la Koutoubia, Medina · Registration at lakechoise.com A women-only 7 km race, now in its sixth edition, starting from the Koutoubia, one of the most visible public spaces in the city. It brings a sporting energy to the Medina early on a Sunday morning. Register at lakechoise.com.

Wednesday 7 October to Saturday 10 October, schedules vary Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech, 6th edition Meydene, M Avenue, Palais Bahia, Musée Yves Saint Laurent, Musée de l’Art Culinaire Marocain, Sofitel Marrakech, Mövenpick · Festival-wide price not stated; some exhibitions may be free The principal visual-arts event of the month, themed “Deux siècles de lumière”. It spreads across several venues, from M Avenue to the Bahia Palace, with exhibitions, screenings, talks, master classes and portfolio reviews. Pick up a programme at Meydene or check the festival’s official channels for the daily schedule.

Wednesday 7 October to Saturday 10 October Marrakech Air Show 2026, 8th edition Marrakech Air Base, airport area · Public-access ticketing not stated A major aerospace and aviation exhibition that draws industry professionals from across Morocco and beyond. Public access may be restricted, so verify ticketing and entry requirements before heading to the air base. It is a significant event for anyone working in aviation, defence or related sectors.

Wednesday 7 October Miss Mermaid Institut français de Marrakech, Gueliz · Price from the venue A film screening followed by a discussion with Pauline Brunner and Marion Verlé. It is a French-language cultural evening in Gueliz, useful for francophone residents and anyone working on their French. Check the Institut français Marrakech for booking details.

Mid-October: Campus Fair, Theatre and Design

Wednesday 14 October, from 14:00 Campus Fair Institut français de Marrakech, Gueliz · Price and registration from the venue A higher-education orientation event for students and families. Foreign residents with school-age children may find it useful for understanding study pathways in Morocco and abroad. Registration details are not in the public listing, so contact the Institut français directly.

Thursday 15 October to Sunday 15 November Élisabeth Busson: L’art du toucher La Mamounia, Hivernage · Price from the venue A contemporary art exhibition in one of Marrakech’s most storied hotels. It is a good excuse to see the Mamounia’s gardens and interiors while taking in new work. Verify entry arrangements with La Mamounia, as access policies for non-guests can vary.

Thursday 15 October, 19:00 Iqtibas by Sarah M. Institut français de Marrakech, Gueliz · Price from the venue A multidisciplinary performance combining theatre, dance and music. It is the kind of small-stage production that gives Gueliz its cultural rhythm. Check the Institut français for ticket prices and booking.

Friday 16 October to Sunday 18 October, daily times not stated Creative & Design Summit by Les Impériales Marrakech, exact venue not stated · Price and registration from the organiser A professional summit for the creative, design and communication industries. It is aimed at people working in those sectors rather than the general public. Registration details are not in the public listing, so contact Les Impériales directly.

21 to 25 October: Poetry, OUM and Folklore Days

Wednesday 21 October, 19:00 Nuit de la poésie Institut français de Marrakech, Gueliz · Free, fully booked A poetry evening at the Institut français de Marrakech. The listing shows it as fully booked, so check the Institut français for any returned places.

Thursday 22 October, 20:00 to 22:30 OUM — “Dialddar” Maison Denise Masson, Medina · Price from the venue A headline Moroccan concert by OUM, whose work blends contemporary music with North African and international influences. Maison Denise Masson is a distinctive setting for live music in the Medina. Verify ticket prices and booking with the venue or organiser.

Thursday 22 October to Sunday 25 October, daily times not stated Marrakech Folklore Days 2026, 8th edition M Avenue and Jemaa el-Fna, Gueliz and Medina · Price from the venue; some public performances may be free Four days of performances, parades, workshops and cultural exchange centred on living folk traditions. The Jemaa el-Fna component is likely to be the most accessible. Check the festival’s official channels for the daily programme and any ticketed events.

Late October: Holiday Weekend and Running All Month

Saturday 31 October, all day Aïd Al Wahda — public holiday Citywide · National public holiday Morocco marks Unity Day on 31 October. It falls on a Saturday in 2026, so it adds no extra weekday closure.

Through Saturday 31 October Maroc, regards d’hier et d’aujourd’hui Maison de la Photographie, Medina · Price from the venue A photography exhibition tracing Morocco’s visual history from early documentary work to contemporary portraits and architecture. The Maison de la Photographie is one of the Medina’s most rewarding small museums. Check the museum for October entry prices.

Planning your Marrakech in October

One fixed-date public holiday falls in October 2026: Aïd Al Wahda (Unity Day) on Saturday 31 October, so there is no extra weekday closure. The next fixed national holiday is Green March Day on Friday 6 November.

Getting around at night is easiest by taxi or ride-hailing app. Agree a fare before getting into a petit taxi if the meter is not running. For events in the Medina, allow extra time to walk from the nearest vehicle access point to the venue.

Prices in Marrakech are quoted in Moroccan dirhams (MAD or DH). The exchange rate to the US dollar changes daily, so check the rate published by Bank Al-Maghrib, your bank or a reputable provider on the day you pay. Many venues do not publish ticket prices online, so call ahead or ask at the door.

For weekly listings, check the Institut français de Marrakech, La Tribune de Marrakech events page, and the official Visit Marrakech events calendar. These are the most reliable local sources for confirmed dates and venue changes.

More from The Rio Times: Morocco news and guides, the Rencontres de la Photographie, the cost of living in Marrakech.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the biggest events in Marrakech in October 2026?

The Rencontres de la Photographie de Marrakech runs 7 to 10 October, the Marrakech Air Show runs the same weekend, and the Marrakech Folklore Days run from 22 to 25 October.

Are there any public holidays in Morocco in October 2026?

One fixed-date Moroccan public holiday falls in October 2026: Aïd Al Wahda (Unity Day) on Saturday 31 October. The next one is Green March Day on Friday 6 November.

When is La Kéchoise 2026 in Marrakech?

The sixth edition of La Kéchoise, a women-only 7 km race, starts at 08:30 on Sunday 4 October at the Place de la Koutoubia. Registration is through lakechoise.com.

How do I buy tickets for Marrakech events in October 2026?

Many venues do not publish ticket prices online. Contact the venue or organiser directly, and check the Institut français de Marrakech, La Tribune de Marrakech and Visit Marrakech for confirmed listings.

World.title: Costa Rica beats Nicaragua 3-0 as Bryan Ruiz wins debut on the bench
World.content:
Costa Rica finally had something to celebrate last night as La Sele defeated Nicaragua 3-0 in Managua, giving Bryan Ruiz a victory in his first match as interim head coach and ending a winless stretch that had lasted nearly a year. Orlando Sinclair and Carlos Mora scored three minutes apart early in the second half before Kenyel Michel added a third in stoppage time to seal a convincing scoreline at the Estadio Nacional de Nicaragua.

It was exactly the type of result Costa Rica needed after a miserable start to the Concacaf Nations League and the dismissal of Fernando Batista. The victory, however, came too late to rescue La Sele’s chances of reaching the quarterfinals. Costa Rica had already been eliminated from contention and entered Thursday’s match with a more immediate concern: avoiding relegation from League A.

For Ruiz, the first night on the bench offered at least a reason for optimism. The former Costa Rica captain was handed the national team on an interim basis after Batista’s departure and had only a few days to prepare for Nicaragua. The opening 45 minutes showed that the problems surrounding the national team have not disappeared overnight.

Costa Rica created chances but could not find the goal before halftime. Nicaragua goalkeeper Brandon Mayorga kept the visitors out, while the artificial surface in Managua made for a difficult night. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 56th minute as Sinclair found space inside the area and finished to put Costa Rica ahead. Three minutes later, Mora took advantage of a mistake in Nicaragua’s buildup and made it 2-0.

The quick double changed the match. Nicaragua pushed forward looking for a way back, but Costa Rica stayed organized and avoided the defensive mistakes that have hurt the team throughout the year. Michel then finished the night in the 95th minute with Costa Rica’s third goal.

Ruiz acknowledged afterward that it was not a perfect performance. The new coach said Costa Rica did not necessarily play great football, but he was pleased with what he saw from his team defensively and offensively. He also stressed the pressure surrounding the match because of the possibility of Costa Rica dropping into League B.

There was another familiar face back in goal. Keylor Navas returned to the starting lineup after missing Costa Rica’s first two Nations League matches. The veteran goalkeeper was not heavily tested but provided experience behind a team badly in need of some stability. Navas said afterward that Costa Rica still has plenty to improve but emphasized that winning was the priority after such a difficult period.

“For the few days we’ve had, you could see a good result,” Navas said after the match. The night was not entirely positive as Defender Jeyland Mitchell was forced out after only 18 minutes with an injury and was replaced by Juan Pablo Vargas. Navas also reported some discomfort in his knee, which he attributed to the playing surface, although he expressed hope that the problem was not serious.

Perhaps the biggest significance of the victory was simply seeing Costa Rica win again. Before last night, La Sele’s last victory had come on Oct. 13, 2025, when it defeated Nicaragua 4-1 during World Cup qualifying. Since then, the national team had gone through nearly a year of poor results, coaching changes and growing frustration among supporters.

One victory against Nicaragua will not erase those problems, but for Ruiz, whose history with the national team was built during some of Costa Rican football’s best years, his first night on the other side of the touchline ended about as well as he could have hoped. Costa Rica now has little time to enjoy it.

La Sele returns home to face Haiti on Sunday, Oct. 4, at 6 p.m. at the Ricardo Saprissa Stadium in San José in its final Nations League group match. The quarterfinals are no longer available, but avoiding relegation remains on the line. For a national team searching for direction, Thursday’s win in Managua was at least a start.

World.title: Costa Rica’s New Workplace Harassment Standard Takes Effect Today
World.content:
An international treaty on violence and harassment at work takes full legal effect in Costa Rica today. It applies to every workplace, from government ministries to small private businesses. The International Labour Organization’s Convention 190 widens what counts as harassment, stretches protection well beyond the office, and shifts the burden toward prevention rather than reaction after a complaint lands.

So what actually changes today? On paper, less than some headlines would suggest but in practice, potentially a great deal. The biggest shift is that a single incident can now be enough. Costa Rican courts long treated workplace harassment as a pattern of repeated conduct but the convention instead defines violence and harassment as unacceptable behavior or threats, whether they happen once or repeatedly, that aim at, cause or are likely to cause physical, psychological, sexual or economic harm.

The courts were already moving that way as the Supreme Court’s Second Chamber, which handles labor cases, dropped the requirement that harassment be repeated and accepted that one act can qualify. Cristhian Monge said employers can no longer assume a case requires repeated behavior. A single act, he said, may now carry legal weight depending on its nature and its effects.

The second change is where the rules apply. Protection now covers anything that happens during work, in connection with work, or as a result of it. That includes business trips, training sessions, work social events, rest areas and restrooms, housing provided by an employer, and the commute between home and work.

It also covers work-related messages sent through digital tools. A harassing WhatsApp message from a supervisor late at night falls inside the framework just as much as a comment made across a desk. The third change is who is protected. The convention reaches far beyond salaried staff in the public and private sectors. It also covers interns, apprentices, trainees, volunteers, job applicants and people whose employment has already ended, regardless of their contract status.

What the convention does not do matters just as much. It does not rewrite existing employment contracts, create new grounds for dismissal or replace current labor law, according to Daniel Valverde, a labor law partner at the firm Ecija. Valverde said its force is as an interpretive standard. The Ministry of Labor and Social Security and the courts can now use it as a reference when deciding specific cases.

Costa Rica still has no standalone law that comprehensively regulates workplace harassment in the public and private sectors. A bill to prevent and punish workplace harassment in both sectors was filed in the Legislative Assembly in August and remains under debate.

The Labor Ministry has confirmed the ratification but had not, as of yesterday, issued official guidelines on how the convention will work alongside existing national law. Sexual harassment is a separate matter. Law 7476, in force since 1995, already requires every employer to maintain an internal policy that prevents, discourages and punishes sexual harassment. Labor lawyers say that policy alone no longer covers the scope of the new standard.

Specialists disagree on how quickly employers face real consequences. José Edgardo Jiménez, a lawyer and accountant who advises small and medium-sized businesses, said that from today all employers should have harassment policies and procedures in place and documented.

According to Jiménez, a company found without them during a Labor Ministry inspection could be fined under Article 398 of the Labor Code. Those fines are calculated in base salaries and range from one to 23. A base salary is not anyone’s actual paycheck. It is a fixed reference amount, tied to the pay of an entry-level judicial clerk and updated each year, that Costa Rica uses to calculate fines and penalties.

Jiménez put one base salary at ₡462,200, which he said is the likely minimum for a first offense. Repeat offenders could face the maximum of 23, or roughly ₡10.6 million. Valverde, by contrast, said the convention’s taking effect does not by itself trigger an immediate regulatory change for each company. He and other specialists nonetheless advise employers to act now rather than wait for a case or an inspection.

If you run a business or manage staff, the advice from labor lawyers follows a similar path. Start by finding out what you already have, since many companies have codes of conduct that partly cover the issue. Update that language to reflect that one incident can count and adopt a general policy against violence and harassment rather than relying on a sexual harassment policy alone.

From there, the lawyers recommend assessing where risks exist in day-to-day operations, setting up clear and confidential complaint channels, and writing a straightforward protocol for investigating cases. They also advise protecting the people involved from retaliation, training managers and human resources staff, documenting every complaint and action taken, and telling employees plainly how the system works.

Labor Ministry inspectors already check whether companies have internal procedures for receiving and handling complaints, the lawyers noted. Óscar Corrales said the core message is prevention. Having a procedure to react to a complaint is not enough, he said; companies need to identify risks, train people, and review interactions that happen outside the office, including on digital platforms, during travel and at work events.

If you are an employee, the change is mainly in what can be raised and how seriously it may be weighed. A single serious incident, a message in a work chat or behavior at an off-site event can now form the basis of a complaint, either through your employer’s internal channel or before the Labor Ministry and the labor courts.

The convention arrives at full strength without a dedicated national harassment law or official ministry guidance in place. For now, the courts and the pending bill will do much of the work of deciding how far the new standard reaches.

World.title: Costa Rica Braces for Afternoon Storms as Tropical Wave No. 48 Arrives
World.content:
Tropical Wave No. 48 is expected to cross Costa Rica today bringing a greater chance of afternoon downpours and thunderstorms as already wet areas face an increased risk of flooding and landslides. The National Meteorological Institute (IMN) said a drop in atmospheric pressure across Central America is pulling the Intertropical Convergence Zone (the band near the equator where trade winds meet, creating clouds, storms and frequent heavy rain) closer to Costa Rica.

Combined with the tropical wave, that will increase atmospheric instability over the country and help fuel rainfall through Thursday and into the coming days. The day is expected to begin relatively calm and much of Costa Rica will see partly cloudy skies and warm, muggy conditions during the morning before the weather changes during the afternoon.

The IMN expects showers and thunderstorms to develop first around the mountains and higher elevations. Rain could then spread into lower parts of the Greater Metropolitan Area (GMA), the Northern areas and the Caribbean. In the Central Valley, San José, Alajuela, Cartago and Heredia are forecast to remain partly cloudy during the morning before scattered afternoon downpours and thunderstorms develop.

Cloudy conditions, isolated rain and patches of fog could linger into Thursday night. San José is expected to reach about 28°C (83°F), while Alajuela could climb to 31°C (88°F). Cartago will be cooler at around 25°C (77°F), with Heredia near 29°C (84°F). The North Pacific will also see a hot morning followed by scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon. Liberia could reach around 36°C (96°F), while Puntarenas is also forecast near 36°C. Nicoya could reach approximately 35°C (94°F).

In the Central and South Pacific, rainfall is expected mainly around mountainous areas during the afternoon, with variable cloud cover continuing into the evening. Quepos is forecast to reach about 33°C (91°F), while Golfito could reach 34°C (93°F). The Northern Zone and Caribbean could also see afternoon thunderstorms, particularly near the mountains, followed by scattered rain into the evening. Ciudad Quesada is forecast near 28°C (82°F), while Limón could reach around 30°C (85°F). Of particular concern are areas where the ground is already saturated after recent rainfall.

In its latest weather advisor from yesterday, the IMN reported soil saturation above 95% in parts of the Northern Zone and Northern Caribbean, as well as areas near the mountains of the Central and South Pacific. The institute warned that additional rainfall could increase the possibility of overflowing streams, drainage problems, localized flooding and landslides.

The IMN also said rainfall totals in some of the more affected areas could reach 20 to 50 millimeters, with localized totals of 60 to 80 millimeters. In other parts of the Central Valley, rainfall totals of 5 to 30 millimeters were possible. Anyone in that part of Costa Rica should use extra caution in areas prone to flooding and landslides, particularly during the afternoon and evening. The IMN also recommends seeking shelter during thunderstorms and remaining alert for strong wind gusts near storm cells.

The wetter pattern may continue beyond today. The IMN’s weekly outlook through October 4 calls for humid and unstable conditions, with the Central Pacific and mountainous parts of the Caribbean and Northern Zone carrying some of the greatest potential for moderate to heavy rain.

World.title: Former Petén Governor disputes denial of Guatemalan military aircraft entering Belizean airspace
World.content:
Former Petén Governor disputes denial of Guatemalan military aircraft entering Belizean airspace

By Zoila Palma: Former Peten Governor and Guatemalan Attorney Rudel Alvarez is disputing his Government’s reported denial of a Guatemalan army airplace in Belize’s airspace on September 24, 2026.

“I do believe that flight took place; the real-time flight tracking platform Flightradar recognized the flight. Zooming in on the map, it can be seen that at a certain point, the Air Force plane enters Belizean territorial waters, then exits and remains in a holding pattern for about 40 minutes, before turning off its transponder and returning to Guatemala,” Alvarez explained on Facebook.

In addition, Alvarez called out Guatemalan President Bernardo Arevalo who reportedly questioned the veracity of Flightradar and asserts that the Air Force never carried out that flight.

“The President has fallen into a trap that will only further damage his reputation.

The Army is deliberately lying to him; they did so three days ago when they told him that the Army never participated in the incursion in Huite, Zacapa, and now they say they did but don’t know how it happened. President Arevalo: Don’t trust the Army. Make urgent changes or they will continue to deceive you. The flight did exist and it has been scientifically proven,” Alvarez added.

But, Alvarez also said that Belize is making “a huge fuss about something simple.”

He further alleged that Belize remains “silent when illegal flights enter the heart of their territory every week with illicit cargo, sometimes even unloading it in their territorial waters.”

World.title: Child Protection and Justice Steering Committee calls for stronger safeguards for children at public events
World.content:
Child Protection and Justice Steering Committee calls for stronger safeguards for children at public events

By Zoila Palma: The Child Protection and Justice Steering Committee (CPJSC) is calling for stronger child safeguarding measures at public events following recent scenes involving children during this year’s Carnival celebrations.

In a statement issued on October 1, 2026, the Committee stressed that children should be able to participate in cultural, sporting, and community events in environments that are safe, age-appropriate, and respectful of their dignity and rights.

The CPJSC acknowledged Carnival as an important expression of Belizean culture, creativity, and community, but emphasized that adults have a responsibility to maintain appropriate boundaries when children are involved. The Committee noted that behavior that may be acceptable between consenting adults is not automatically appropriate when a child is involved, and called for greater attention to the safety and well-being of children at public celebrations.

The Committee is urging event organizers, public officials, parents, and caregivers to implement safeguards at all public events involving children. These include clear codes of conduct for adults interacting with minors, age-appropriate choreography and costumes, designated family spaces with adequate supervision, and trained child protection personnel who can respond promptly to concerns. The CPJSC also called for safeguarding expectations to be clearly communicated to performers, staff, participants, and families.

The CPJSC further urged media outlets, content creators, and members of the public to protect the identity and dignity of children when incidents raise safeguarding concerns.

It cautioned against publishing or resharing images and videos that could identify a child involved, noting that continued circulation can expose children to unwanted attention or further harm.

World.title: $160,000 a year, $33,000 in allowances and 20% gratuity for Procurement Director
World.content:
$160,000 a year, $33,000 in allowances and 20% gratuity for Procurement Director

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Public officers and Government CEOs are raising eyebrows over the leaked contract of Director of Procurement Rey Guerrero, and the Opposition is demanding answers.

Guerrero’s renewed contract carries a base salary of $160,000 a year, about twice the pay of a Government CEO. With a 20 percent gratuity and close to $33,000 in yearly allowances, the two year deal approaches $450,000.

The Procurement Unit has been promoted by Prime Minister John Briceño as a key fix following the high profile Mira and Marin procurement scandals. It is meant to centralize and reform how Government spends public money.

Opposition Leader Tracy Panton says procurement reform must begin with transparency. While the Opposition supports qualified professionals, she said every dollar must be justified by competence, performance and value for money.

Panton also pointed to what she called a double standard. She says that despite repeated written requests to the Office of the Prime Minister, the Office of the Leader of the Opposition receives not a single penny to carry out its constitutional oversight duties.

“Make it make sense,” she wrote.

Guerrero has not responded to requests for comment.

World.title: International News: Pacific Ocean reaches record-high temperatures as El Niño intensifies
World.content:
International News: Pacific Ocean reaches record-high temperatures as El Niño intensifies

By Zoila Palma: Sea surface temperatures in a key region of the Pacific Ocean have reached their highest level ever recorded, as a rapidly strengthening El Niño continues to develop.

Preliminary data from the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) showed the average temperature in the Niño 3.4 region reached 85.73°F (29.85°C) on September 29, surpassing the previous daily record of 85.68°F set in November 2015.

The Niño 3.4 region covers about 2.4 million square miles of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific and is closely monitored to measure the strength of El Niño.

NOAA cautioned that the September 29 reading remains preliminary and could change as additional observations from ships, buoys and other sources are incorporated. Data from buoys along a 1,000-mile stretch of the Pacific on September 30 recorded temperatures ranging from 83.8°F to 87.8°F.

Scientists say the record warmth is raising concerns about marine ecosystems, coral reefs and communities that depend on the ocean.

Ben Kirtman, dean of the University of Miami Rosenstiel School, described the situation as a combination of climate change and a rapidly strengthening El Niño, noting that temperatures in the region could continue rising into November. The current El Niño developed earlier than expected and is not expected to reach its peak until later in 2026.

The unusually warm Pacific waters could also affect marine species, weather patterns and coastal communities.

Scientists have reported changes in the distribution of marine species, while warming waters have already been linked to disruptions in marine food chains in parts of the Pacific.

World.title: Panton questions $450,000 contract for Procurement Director
World.content:
Panton questions $450,000 contract for Procurement Director

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Opposition Leader Tracy Panton is demanding an explanation from Government over the reported renewal of Rey Guerrero’s contract as Director of Procurement.

According to reports cited by Panton, the two year package is worth nearly $450,000. It reportedly includes an annual salary of $160,000, close to $33,000 in allowances and a 20 percent gratuity.

“If these reports are accurate, Belizeans deserve to know who approved these terms, what performance assessment supported the renewal, and what results justify the expenditure,” Panton wrote.

She said the Opposition supports qualified professionals and stronger public procurement, but every dollar must be justified by competence, performance and value for money.

Panton is calling on the Prime Minister and the Ministry of Finance to release the signed contract, provide the supporting performance assessment and account for the Procurement Unit’s results in securing savings, strengthening competitive tendering and preventing abuse.

“Make it make sense,” she wrote.

World.content:
Book 3 nights, get the 4th free at San Ignacio Resort Hotel

Whether you are planning a weekend escape, a family getaway or a chance to explore western Belize, now is the perfect time to book.

World.title: Hot Friday ahead with inland temperatures reaching 94 degrees
World.content:
Hot Friday ahead with inland temperatures reaching 94 degrees

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belizeans can expect another hot Friday with isolated showers and thunderstorms as relatively moist and somewhat unstable conditions continue across the country.

The National Meteorological Service says skies will be mostly sunny with a few cloudy spells today.

Showers and thunderstorms will generally remain isolated, although a few more are expected to develop over inland areas during the afternoon and evening.

Tonight and Saturday morning, cloudy intervals are expected with a few showers and isolated thunderstorms developing mainly along coastal areas.

Temperatures will remain hot, particularly inland, where the daytime high is expected to reach 94 degrees Fahrenheit.

Coastal areas can expect highs around 89 degrees, while temperatures in the hills will reach approximately 82 degrees.

Marine conditions will be choppy with waves between three and five feet. Winds will blow from the east to southeast at 10 to 15 knots.

On Saturday, cloudy skies are expected at times with a few showers and isolated thunderstorms during the morning and nighttime.

Activity will shift mainly inland during the afternoon and evening.

The tropics remain quiet, with no tropical cyclone formation expected over the region during the next 48 hours.

World.title: PSU objects to Troy Gabb as Acting PSC Chair, cites political commentary; appointment revives controversial DFC-era history
World.content:
PSU objects to Troy Gabb as Acting PSC Chair, cites political commentary; appointment revives controversial DFC-era history

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The Public Service Union of Belize (PSU) has formally objected to the appointment of Troy Gabb as Acting Chairperson of the Public Services Commission (PSC), saying his record as a political commentator and his past public positions raise concerns about confidence in the body responsible for appointments, promotions and discipline in the public service.

In a statement issued today, October 1, the PSU said Gabb, a weekly commentator on Love FM, has “repeatedly shown hostility toward trade unions,” opposed PSU positions on public policy and sharply criticized public officers. The Union further described him as widely perceived to be politically partisan. Those characterizations are the PSU’s stated position.

The Belize Gazette of July 23 confirms that Governor General Dame Froyla Tzalam appointed Gabb to act as Chairperson of the PSC effective July 20, 2026, while substantive Chairperson Diana Price-Murillo is on leave.

But Gabb is no stranger to controversy involving public institutions.

He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of the Development Finance Corporation (DFC) during a period that later became the subject of extensive Senate scrutiny and a Commission of Inquiry over questionable loans, securitization arrangements and other transactions at the state-owned lending institution.

During Senate hearings in 2004, Gabb was questioned about DFC’s large portfolio of non-performing loans. He acknowledged at the time that roughly 35% of DFC’s loan portfolio was non-performing, while senators questioned the institution’s due diligence surrounding major borrowers, including the Novelo’s Group.

Gabb was again called before the DFC Commission of Inquiry in 2007, where he faced questions concerning a number of major transactions, including the Novelo loans, DFC’s involvement in the Mahogany Heights deal, transactions involving companies associated with former DFC chairman Glenn Godfrey and a multimillion-dollar transaction involving the Belize Bank and Government.

One of the more personally controversial issues raised during those hearings concerned a San Pedro property Gabb acquired from DFC for $15,000. Contemporary reporting on the inquiry said commissioners placed its value at approximately $68,000, meaning the purchase price was roughly $53,000 below that valuation. Gabb was questioned about the transaction during his testimony.

The inquiry also heard testimony that, during Gabb’s tenure, certain DFC administration or legal fees were waived or varied in selected cases, with commissioners questioning what authority existed for the CEO to exercise that discretion.

Gabb defended his stewardship of the DFC and challenged aspects of the inquiry and forensic audit, arguing that adverse findings had been prepared without first allowing him an opportunity to respond and questioning the legality of the forensic auditor’s appointment.

Justice Herbert Lord’s subsequent report concluded more broadly that wrongdoing had occurred in the operations of the DFC during the period investigated. That finding concerned the institution and transactions examined by the Commission and should not, by itself, be read as a finding that Gabb personally committed a criminal offence.

Against that history, the PSU says it also opposes Gabb being reappointed as a member of the PSC when his current term expires in November 2026.

“Building a strong Public Service begins with confidence and trust in the Commission,” the Union said.

The PSU has written to Minister of the Public Service Henry Charles Usher outlining its concerns and has called for future PSC appointments to be persons with public-service knowledge, integrity and standing who command the respect of both public officers and the wider public.

The Union also extended best wishes to Price-Murillo and said it hopes for a speedy resolution of the circumstances surrounding her leave and her return to office.

World.title: Brace for delays in health services, JMDA warns amid pay dispute
World.content:
Doctors say if there is no ruling in their wage dispute with the Government by Friday, October 2, 2026, they cannot guarantee normalcy within the health sector across the island (Photo: Adobe Stock)

Jamaicans have been warned to brace for longer wait times and delays in the completion of procedures in the healthcare sector as junior doctors remain restive over the matter of overtime rates which has been before the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) for the past year.

In a press release on Friday, Jamaica Medical Doctors Association (JMDA) President Dr Jubilee Brown said the body “cannot guarantee normalcy from 8 am on Friday, October 2, 2026 to 8 am on Saturday, October 3, 2026.

“Only emergency services will be provided during this period,” the JMDA president said.

She added that the association has activated relevant protocols to minimise adverse outcomes during the period.

According to the JMDA, the Government owes the doctors $31 billion in retroactive overtime, but the Government’s calculation sits at $23 billion.

“We have been working at the same overtime rates since 2021. This is unacceptable. The JMDA calls upon the Industrial Disputes Tribunal to hand down its award without further delay,” Brown said.

World.title: No fallout
World.content:
The scene in Black River in the immediate aftermath of Hurricane Melissa last October. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

DESPITE concerns from some quarters over the slow spending of Hurricane Melissa donations, permanent secretary in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Sheila Sealy Monteith says the Jamaican Diaspora has not raised any complaints about how its contributions are being used.

Sealy Monteith told Parliament’s Internal and External Affairs Committee on Thursday that the ministry had “many opportunities” to receive feedback from the Diaspora but had not received any indication of concern. The assurance came against the backdrop of concerns about the pace at which millions of dollars donated following Hurricane

Melissa have been utilised. Category 5 Melissa left immense damage after slamming into Jamaica’ south-western coast on October 28, 2025 and swept across western and north-western parishes.

During the committee’s deliberations with the ministry, Opposition Member of Parliament Dr Kenneth Russell raised the Auditor General’s finding that only about 1.7 per cent of the donated funds had been used months after the contributions were made.

“Has the ministry, one, received any feedback from the members of the Diaspora and the donors about the slow use of their contributions? And secondly, is the ministry concerned about the reputational risks done to the country and the effect it will have on your ability to raise funds should a similar situation recur?”

Russell queried.

Sealy Monteith responded that the ministry had not seen evidence of a decline in confidence in Jamaica’s ability to handle international support.

“We have used the strength of our diplomacy to ensure that countries who wish to contribute are enabled to contribute, that we are able to record it. We are providing direction for them, and we pass them on to the relevant authorities.

We have not received any indication to date that there has been a loss of confidence in our abilities to use it,” she revealed.

The permanent secretary stressed that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade’s role is primarily to facilitate international assistance, rather than to determine how the funds are ultimately spent.

She said the ministry works with other government entities to ensure that countries and other contributors wishing to assist Jamaica are able to do so and are directed to the relevant authorities.

Sealy Monteith also suggested that the pace at which contributions are absorbed and deployed must be considered in the context of the capacity of the receiving authorities to use the support.

“I think people understand also that when support comes in, it requires the ability to be able to assimilate and to use, and that comes over time as well,” she said. “So, if you’re asking me whether there’s been a fallout of interest and solidarity, I have not seen that. We continue to be a preferred guest on many agendas, and Minister [Kamina Johnson Smith] had a schedule in New York last week that was head-turning because everybody wants Jamaica to be at the table, to sit on our committees, to be there,” she added

World.title: Kevin Smith spoke in  tongues, detective testifies
World.content:
SMITH… late pastor of Pathways International Restoration Kingdom Ministries

A detective constable testified on Thursday that Kevin Smith, the now deceased pastor of Pathways International Restoration Kingdom Ministries in Albion, St James, refused to speak to him on the night of October 17, 2021 when the clergyman was alleged to have killed a male member of his church and ordered another to cut the throat of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner, who was also a member of his flock.

The detective constable is the seventh witness to take the stand in the murder trial of Andre Ruddock,

who is accused of killing Gardner, allegedly on Pastor Smith’s command.

While Smith refused to engage the detective constable in conversation, it was a different story with

Ruddock, who was allegedly eager to speak about the shocking events that unfolded at the church on the night.

According to the investigator, both Smith and Ruddock were wearing nothing but briefs while they were handcuffed and seated on the ground, in the driveway, close to the entrance gate of the premises.

“I spoke to Kevin Smith but he didn’t speak to me. Instead, gate of the premises. “I spoke to Kevin Smith but he didn’t speak to me. Instead, he started talking in a loud voice, in a way I couldn’t understand. It was like when someone was talking in tongues in a church. I informed both Andre Ruddock and Kevin Smith that they would be taken into custody under reasonable suspicion of double murder and wounding with intent. I caused them to be taken to the Montego Bay Police Station lockup,” the detective said.

In relation to Ruddock, the detective explained that he was more cooperative than Smith. The cop testified that he spoke to Ruddock before his futile attempt to talk with Smith. He said that after completing a walkthrough of the church property where the bizarre events unfolded he went to Ruddock, lifted him from off the ground, and took him to an area of the premises where Smith could not hear their conversation.

“After completing the walkthrough and speaking to the detective inspector I came back to where Andre Ruddock was by the big gate. I introduced myself to him and took him up from where he was by the big gate and took him to the area I described as a bathroom right next to the fencing,” the detective constable testified.

“I wanted to speak to him outside of the presence of Kevin Smith. I allowed him to put on some clothes because he was in his underpants. He stated that he had clothes nearby,” he said.

He told the court that Ruddock confessed to killing Gardner by cutting her throat after receiving instructions to do so. When asked who gave the instructions, Ruddock did not say who, but looked in the direction where Pastor Smith was seated on the ground in the driveway of the church.

Prosecutor Latoya Bernard showed the detective numerous photographs of the bizarre scene. He will continue to identify more photographs today when the trial resumes.

World.title: Endeavours Reloaded
World.content:
From left: Sizzla, Tarrus Riley, Spragga Benz, Stephen Marley, Masicka, and I Wayne at the Endeavors Reloaded launch

They say third time’s the charm, but for internationally renowned dancehall icon Spragga Benz, two shots were all it took to perfect the musical vision he had been carrying with him. And on Wednesday night, at Jammin’ On The Oasis, that vision came alive in more ways than one.

The launch of Endeavors Reloaded felt more like a homecoming of artistes, producers, industry players, and friends to celebrate one of their own.

“Mi feel like mi deh inna mi house wid mi bredda and sister dem,” Spragga said, reflecting on the evening.

When he first released Endeavors last year the project did not quite resemble the album he had originally envisioned. Time, schedules, and the demands of an industry that rarely waits for anyone meant that some of the collaborations he wanted simply did not materialise.

Echo Minott, the late Cocoa Tea, Tarrus Riley, Agent Sasco, I Wayne, Sizzla, Bugle, and a host of other respected names were brought into the fold, giving Spragga the opportunity to finally make the album he had imagined.

“Everybody found a way to get dem verse to me or come to the studio and we did it. Nothing happen before the time; this was the right time,” he said.

Sizzla put the significance of the gathering into perspective.

“This is not just an album release, this is history,” he declared, pointing particularly to the presence of one of Cocoa Tea’s final recordings on the project.

In the final days of Cocoa Tea’s life, Spragga Benz was at the hospital with him when a television report about flying saucers sparked a conversation between the two. Cocoa Tea, ever ready to turn life into music, suggested they make a song about the unusual event.

They never made it to the studio together. But the song still came. Cocoa Tea sent voice notes with his vocals, urging Spragga to honour his promise with with the single

That Drone on Endeavors Reloaded.

I Wayne, meanwhile, chose not to explain his collaboration; instead, he embodied it, reaching for the words of the song titled Teach Dem, performing an a capella rendition.

But it was Tarrus Riley who perhaps offered the clearest explanation of why Endeavors Reloaded feels so deliberate.

“Spragga is a one-of-akind artiste, unique talent, voice, writing skills just everything,” he said, before drawing attention to the significance of the album’s title. For Riley, Endeavors speaks to Spragga’s willingness to make an intentional musical statement — to choose what he wants to say, how he wants to say it, and with whom he wants to say it.

That intentionality may well be the project’s defining characteristic; the relationships mattered.

Endeavors Reloaded is a record of friendship, respect, memory and the enduring brotherhood of Jamaican music.

World.title: TALL TASK!
World.content:
Honduras player Alenis Vargas (left) challenges Jamaica’s Tyreece Campbell during the Concacaf Nations League match on Monday.

JAMAICA will be looking to get back on track in the Concacaf Nations League when they face hosts El Salvador in San Salvador tonight at 9:00 pm Jamaica time.

The Reggae Boyz started their campaign with a 3-2 win against Guatemala at the National Stadium in Kingston last Friday. But three days later, they lost 1-0 to Honduras at the same venue.

Now, Jamaica face two away games in four days. After playing El Salvador, they travel to take on Honduras again on Monday.

Suriname lead Group B with six points from two games. Four teams — Guatemala, Honduras, Jamaica, and El Salvador — are tied on three points each, while Martinique sits at the bottom without a point.

Jamaica made five changes to their starting line-up against Honduras, but the team still struggled with energy levels.

Interim Head Coach Rudolph Speid says fatigue hurt the team early in that match.

“The people who started the last match, we repeated them,” Speid said in the press conference on Monday. “We were a bit lethargic, and that allowed Honduras to dominate the game in the first half, especially.”

The home loss puts extra pressure on the team as they head into two tough away matches.

“The loss to Honduras is a setback for us,” he said. “It means that we have to win our remaining games to qualify straight from this stage. So, it’s going to be tough, and we’re going away, which makes it even harder for us.”

Speid also mentioned defensive problems that need quick fixing before facing El Salvador.

“There’s a lot of things — almost everything that we need to improve on,” he said. “Our pressing wasn’t good against Honduras, but even when we dropped into a low block, Honduras still found ways through. Maybe we were just too wide apart, and we have to play much tighter.”

With games coming four days apart and travel involved, Speid hinted at making changes to keep the team fresh.

“We have a big squad, and it is possible that we might have to allow other players who have more energy to play,” he said. “We’ll have to rotate, and that’s something we’re going to look at.”

Tajay Grant, Jamone Lyle, Kyle Ming, and Ramone Howell have been added to boost the squad for this trip.

El Salvador also enter this match with three points from two games. They opened with a 3-1 win over Martinique before a 6-0 loss away to Guatemala on matchday two.

Playing at home at Estadio Cuscatlán, El Salvador will be eager to recover and take advantage of their home crowd.

Jamaica are undefeated in their last five meetings against El Salvador, with one win and four draws. The most recent match was a 1-1 draw in Kingston during World Cup qualifying in March 2022.

Winning away at Estadio Cuscatlán has proven difficult for the Boyz. Their last two trips to San Salvador in World Cup and Nations League qualifying ended in a 1-1 draw in November 2021 and a 2-0 loss in March 2019.

World.title: Kia moves towards sustainable mobility
World.content:
Kia Central & South America (CSA) unveiled its road map to 2030 and beyond at its 2026 Kia EV Day I CSA event in Quito, Ecuador.

The two-day event, which ran from September 16 to 18, provided a detailed look at the brand’s global and regional electrification strategy.

“Since the Kia brand relaunch was executed in 2021 we are on the journey of transformation. We introduced a new brand identity, a new logo, and a new vision for the future. But this transformation was never simply about changing how Kia looks. It was about fundamental improvement in the value we deliver to our customers. As technology and lifestyles evolve, customers increasingly expect convenience, connectivity, innovation, and mobility solutions that fit naturally into daily life. This transformation led us to set a clear ambition: From a traditional automotive manufacturer to be a sustainable mobility solutions provider,” Steve Lee, president, Kia CSA, told guests at the event.

According to Lee, there is no denying the transition to electrification for Kia CSA.

“Over the past year, Kia has achieved a 146% increase in electrified vehicle sales across our region, driven by growing consumer acceptance of hybrid and electric technologies and by an increasingly diverse product portfolio,” added Victor Valentin, vice-president of sales, Kia CSA.

Lee further explained that this pace is currently being driven by first adopters, and that mainstream buyers are not only still slowly moving toward EVs, but there are complex critical barriers within the Latin American & Caribbean markets. These include infrastructure and economic conditions, amongst others.

“Because every customer and market is different, there is no single path to electrification. That is why at 2026 Kia EV Day we are showcasing an electrified portfolio built around one simple principle, providing the right solution at the right stage of the electrification journey,” said Lee.

This strategy will see Kia have a model for the customer at whatever point of electrification they are at, or willing to move towards. These were all revealed on the first night of the event, with the Kia model line-up consisting of all-electric vehicles and hybrid electric vehicles.

Attendees watched as the brand’s new strategy unfolded in front of their very eyes. Kia showed off the all-electric range consisting of the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5, all on their Electric-Global Modular Platform. These were followed by hybrid versions of popular standard models, such as an all-new Niro HEV, the recently launched Seltos, and the familiar nameplates — Sportage, Sorento, and Carnival. Kia aims to further increase the model count to ten in each of the two categories.

“Today, our portfolio includes eight fully electric models and five full Hybrid models, including the recently launched 2026 Kia EV2,” said Ricardo Rosales, executive chairman, Kia Ecuador.

Lee went into further detail.

“This portfolio includes a complete hybrid line-up, providing a practical first step toward electrification for many customers; a full line-up of dedicated EVs, offering advanced technology, dynamic design, a reliable electric mobility experience, and innovative Platform Beyond Vehicle (PBV), that will unlock new possibilities by redefining how mobility can serve both individuals and businesses. Together, HEV, EV, and PBV support customers at every stage of their mobility journey,” he added.

For the second day of the 2026 Kia EV Day event, media, and guests were invited to explore the all-electric model line-up hands-on and, on the road, with a test drive loop around Quito and environs.

“Successful electrification requires comprehensive understanding of customers, adapting to each market, and making sustainable mobility relevant in everyday life. At Kia, we remain committed to supporting this evolution through innovation, customer- focused solutions for a smooth transition towards electrification. We believe the opportunity for electrified mobility in our region is substantial, and we are confident the best is yet to come,” said Lee.

World.title: JTA president-elect rushed to hospital following two- vehicle crash in Trelawny
World.content:
Scenes from a two-vehicle crash in Duncans, Trelawny, on Thursday afternoon that left President-elect of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association (JTA), Dr Maureen Mullings-Nelson, injured.

TRELAWNY, Jamaica — President-elect of the Jamaica Teachers’ Association (JTA), Dr Maureen Mullings-Nelson, was rushed to hospital on Thursday afternoon after sustaining multiple injuries in a two-vehicle crash on the Duncans main road in Trelawny.

The crash, which occurred about 3:30 pm, involved two Honda CR-V motor vehicles.

Mullings-Nelson was a passenger in one of the vehicles, which was travelling from Montego Bay, St James, towards Kingston after a JTA Central Executive meeting at the Sea Gardens Hotel.

The Jamaica Observer understands that Mullings-Nelson sustained multiple injuries and was taken to hospital for treatment.

The driver of the other Honda CR-V reportedly suffered minor injuries. It was not immediately clear whether the driver of the vehicle in which Mullings-Nelson was travelling was physically harmed.

The crash resulted in a lengthy traffic pile-up along the roadway as emergency personnel responded to the scene.

Members of the Jamaica Fire Brigade and the Jamaica Constabulary Force were among those who responded.

Further information on Mullings-Nelson’s condition were not immediately available.

World.title: ‘A me kill Taneka’: Detective testifies Ruddock confessed to Pathways killing
World.content:
Taneka Gardener was allegedly murdered on the orders of Kevin Smith at Kingdom Restoration Ministries in Albion St James.

A detective constable a few moments ago testified that murder accused Andre Ruddock confessed to him that he killed 39-year-old Taneka Gardner at the Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in Albion St James.

Gardner was killed on October 17, 2021, as part of what has been described as a human sacrifice ritual at the church.

Ruddock is alleged to have cut her throat on the instructions of his now-deceased pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, who allegedly told Gardner that her blood was unclean and therefore she had to die. The pastor allegedly asked her if she believed he could bring her back to life if she was killed. After she repeatedly said she believed, her throat was cut, allegedly by Ruddock after another man hesitated to carry out the pastor’s order to slash her throat.

Both Ruddock and Gardner were members of Smith’s flock.

The detective constable took the witness stand for the first time in the Home Circuit Court murder trial of Ruddock in downtown Kingston. He is the seventh witness to take the stand.

The detective explained that when he arrived at the scene around 11:00 pm he was pointed to two men in handcuffs who were sitting on the ground by a big gate leading to the church. One of the men was identified to the detective as Kevin Smith. The other man was identified to him as Andre Ruddock. The only sort of clothing both had on was underwear.

After receiving certain details regarding the incident, the cop led Ruddock away from the pastor and took him inside the building, where he allowed him to put on some clothes. He proceeded to caution him by telling him that he was not obliged to say anything unless he wished to do so, but that anything he said would be taken down in writing and could be used against him in a court of law.

According to him, Ruddock decided that he had something he wished to say and allegedly began to spill the beans.

“I took him away from where he was by the gate. I allowed him to put on some clothes because he was in underpants…He immediately started talking, saying, ‘a me kill Taneka, mi naa go tell you no lie and mi ago tell you everything weh happen’.

“I asked him how he killed Taneka, and he said, ‘mi cut har neck’. I asked him why he cut Taneka’s neck, and he said, ‘mi get instructions fi do it. I asked him who instructed him, and he didn’t respond, but he was looking in the direction of the big gate where I took him from,” the detective said.

The prosecution team, comprising Latoya Bernard and Carolyn Wright, will continue the examination-in-chief of the witness. In the meantime, Ruddock’s attorneys Anthony Williams and Venice Brown are listening attentively as they prepare to cross-examine the detective constable.

World.title: 17 countries join forces to oppose EU budget cuts
World.content:
"We therefore believe that the overall funding for Cohesion Policy and the CAP must be preserved in the next MFF," the seventeen countries wrote in the letter to Irish Taoiseach Micheal Martin seen by POLITICO.

The signatories include Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Greece, Hungary, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Romanian President Nicușor Dan coordinated the initiative and will host an informal meeting of those countries in the margins of the next European Council on Oct. 15 and 16.

The Multiannual Financial Framework, or MFF, finances everything from farmers’ subsidies to development aid, and is among the toughest negotiations in Brussels. In 2025, the European Commission proposed a budget of nearly €2 trillion for the 2028-2034 period and shifted hundreds of billions from agriculture and regional payouts, known as cohesion policy. to new priorities such as defense and competitiveness.

The so-called Friends of Cohesion group warned that further reductions to agricultural and cohesion "would only weaken it [budget] and risk undermining public support for the European project."

Ireland’s negotiating document, or negobox, will set the scene for discussions among the EU’s 27 leaders during the summit in Brussels in October.

World.title: G7 agrees major release of oil stocks following pressure from the US
World.content:
The statement did not specify that the releases would come from European reserves, but U.S. President Donald Trump said in a social media post that Europe had conceded to pressure.

"Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "The process will begin immediately."

The announcement comes after several rounds of emergency talks between European governments over how to respond to the U.S. pressure, with France proposing a release of 100 million barrels of European oil and diesel earlier Friday.

The G7 includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the U.K. and the U.S.

The announcement comes after POLITICO reported earlier this week that the U.S. administration was directly requesting that EU governments and the United Kingdom release new stocks of diesel and crude oil into the market to cushion a sharp rise in diesel prices that threatens the U.S. agricultural sector and has heaped pressure on Trump ahead of critical midterm elections next month.

While G7 countries participated in a release of 400 barrels of oil earlier this year led by the International Energy Agency, many of the barrels released never made it to market because they were unable to compete with cheaper U.S. crude that has recently flooded the bloc, according to a trader and an EU diplomat. But they were, officially, available, the people said.

Two other diplomats suggested Friday that the announcement was simply a reaffirmation of that March commitment.

World.title: Šefčovič: Verhandlung mit China noch ohne  Ergebnisse
World.content:
Über die Ergebnisse der Reise sprechen die EU-Staats- und Regierungschefs am 15. und 16. Oktober bei ihrem EU-Gipfel in Brüssel. Die EU droht damit, den Zugang chinesischer Unternehmen zum Binnenmarkt einzuschränken, sollten die Gespräche scheitern.

Die EU und China verhandeln seit Juni. Die Staats- und Regierungschefs der EU haben erklärt, sie wollten die große Menge chinesischer Importe und das hohe Handelsdefizit mit China, nicht länger hinnehmen.

„Ich glaube, unsere chinesischen Partner haben verstanden, dass dies direkte Auswirkungen auf die Zukunft bedeutender europäischer Unternehmen hat – buchstäblich Tausende von Arbeitsplätzen“, berichtete Šefčovič. „Und auch auf das soziale Gefüge und das Sozialmodell, das in Europa über viele, viele Jahrzehnte hinweg entwickelt wurde.“

Im Mittelpunkt der Gespräche steht das wachsende Handelsdefizit der Union mit China von einer Milliarde Euro pro Tag. Um dieses Defizit zu verringern, müssen die Importe aus China reduziert und/oder die EU-Exporte nach China gesteigert werden.

Šefčovič erklärte, er hoffe, aus Peking Ergebnisse zu drei Hauptthemen mitbringen zu können: plötzliche Exportanstiege Chinas in wichtigen Industriezweigen, Maßnahmen zur Steigerung europäischer Warenexporte nach China, Klarheit hinsichtlich chinesischer Exportbeschränkungen für Rohstoffe, insbesondere für Seltene Erden.

In Milwaukee traf sich Šefčovič mit dem chinesischen Vizeminister Li Chenggang. Der slowakische Kommissar erklärte, China habe Verständnis für die Bedenken Europas: „Alle von uns angesprochenen Themen liegen auf dem Tisch. Ich sage nicht, dass wir Zusicherungen haben, dass wir sie lösen werden, aber sie liegen auf dem Tisch.“

World.title: G7 to hold emergency talks over possible diesel release
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump speaks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney next to French President Emmanuel Macron at a working lunch with leaders of G7, on June 16, 2026 in Evian-les-bains, France. | Pool photo by Evelyn Hockstein via Getty Images

The meeting comes as Trump threatens to ban U.S. diesel exports.

BRUSSELS — The G7 club of rich countries is preparing to convene later today to explore whether to release further diesel reserves to bring down fuel prices.

Four people familiar with the matter confirmed the plan to POLITICO. The meeting will take place after the U.S. pressured European countries to act on their reserves or face an export ban.

The meeting of the Group of Seven, which includes France, Germany, Italy, the U.K., the U.S., Canada and Japan, will come on Friday afternoon amid growing concern over rising diesel costs that have triggered a pressure campaign by Washington.

World.title: Frankreich erwägt Freigabe von Öl- und Dieselreserven nach US-Druck
World.content:
Berlin hingegen zögerte laut den Informanten, überhaupt Barrel freizugeben. „Deutschland und andere Länder wollen nicht instrumentalisiert werden; sie möchten ihre Vorräte nur aus echten Gründen der Versorgungssicherheit freigeben“, sagte einer von ihnen POLITICO unter der Bedingung der Anonymität, um – wie auch andere in diesem Artikel – offen sprechen zu können. Deutschland und Frankreich verfügen laut offiziellen EU-Statistiken über die größten Reserven an Öl und Erdölprodukten in Europa.

„Frankreich ist sehr daran interessiert, sich zu beteiligen und der Bitte nachzukommen … es ist klar, dass die EU etwas unternehmen wird, sofern sie sich auf etwas einigen kann“, sagte die zweite Person. Sie fügten hinzu, dass unklar sei, ob die Freigabe gemeinsam von der EU koordiniert oder auf bilateraler Basis erfolgen werde, angesichts des „chaotischen“ Vorgehens der USA, die unterschiedliche Anfragen an verschiedene Länder gerichtet hätten. „Das ist eine typische Anfrage der USA – sie nutzen nicht die üblichen offiziellen Kanäle.“

Ein Sprecher des französischen Wirtschaftsministers Roland Lescure wies den Vorschlag als „Gerüchte“ zurück und lehnte eine weitere Stellungnahme ab. In einer Erklärung teilte der Élysée-Palast mit, dass Emmanuel Macron „so bald wie möglich“ ein Treffen der G7-Staats- und Regierungschefs einberufen werde, „um die erforderlichen Maßnahmen zu koordinieren, die dazu beitragen sollen, den Preisdruck zu mildern und die Versorgung mit Rohöl und Raffinerieprodukten in den G7-Ländern sowie weltweit sicherzustellen“.

Macron führte am Donnerstagabend ein Telefongespräch mit US-Präsident Donald Trump, um „die weltweite Energiesituation zu erörtern“ und „die weltweite Verfügbarkeit von Raffinerieprodukten sicherzustellen“, teilte der Élysée-Palast mit.

Britische Regierungsvertreter erwarten die Einberufung eines G7-Treffens bereits am Freitag, doch seien unmittelbare Ergebnisse unwahrscheinlich, so eine mit der Angelegenheit vertraute Person, der Anonymität gewährt wurde, um über sensible Fragen der Treibstoffversorgung zu sprechen. Eine etwaige Freigabe von Reserven in Europa würde unter der Leitung der IEA erfolgen, so die Person.

Die USA sind zunehmend frustriert über EU-Länder, die ihre Zusagen zu der 400-Millionen-Barrel-Freigabe Anfang des Jahres nicht eingehalten haben. Diese hatte die Internationale Energieagentur (IEA) nach Ausbruch des Krieges im Iran und der Schließung der Straße von Hormus koordiniert. Bei der Sitzung der hochrangigen Energy Union Taskforce am Freitag kritisierten einige EU-Länder laut einer der informierten Personen auch Frankreich und Deutschland dafür, dass sie keine nennenswerten Ölreserven auf den Markt gebracht hätten.

POLITICO berichtete am Donnerstag, dass führende EU-Länder und Großbritannien auf den Druck der USA mit einer „entschlossenen“ Haltung reagieren wollten, gleichzeitig aber eine Deeskalation anstrebten.

Nicolas Camut und Charlie Cooper haben zu diesem Bericht beigetragen. Der Text erschien zuerst auf Englisch bei POLITICO.

World.title: Feijóo: In Ceuta, it’s up to Europe to clean up the Spanish government’s mess
World.content:
The response of the current Spanish government, incapable of acknowledging the true nature of the problem and implementing the correct solution, obliges me to reiterate, first and foremost, the obvious, as the President of Ceuta did last week during his visit to Brussels. We are not witnessing a conventional migration crisis, but rather the consequences of an invasion originating from Morocco, which must therefore be held responsible for having condoned or instigated it.

Normality has disappeared from Ceuta for more than six weeks, and the scenes of chaos, overcrowding and insecurity should both shame us and compel us to act. To think that the prolongation of this situation will have no consequences is a mistake we cannot afford to make: it affects our sovereignty, our collective capacity to defend the rule of law, the safety of our citizens, and the credibility of the European project in ensuring its own stability.

Undoubtedly, the national authorities are the first to bear the responsibility for resolving this crisis, in accordance with a non-negotiable principle shared by all EU member states under the Pact on Migration and Asylum: those who have entered irregularly must be returned. All of them. The Spanish government’s obligation is not to find accommodation for them, but to expedite their departure.

That said, given the time that has elapsed and the escalation of violent incidents in Ceuta, Europe as a whole must recognize the failure of the Spanish government and exert the necessary pressure to prevent this crisis from becoming entrenched, spreading, or happening again. Just as Europe has responded when faced with other hybrid threats — on energy, trade or disinformation — the attack on our southern border now demands the same determination.

Firstly, the European Union must ensure that Spain implements, with due rigor and efficiency, all the European instruments available to facilitate returns. Secondly, it must clarify why the Kingdom of Morocco itself has reiterated in an official statement its willingness to take back all those who entered on July 30, while Spanish ministers maintain that no such cooperation exists.

Thirdly, it must make full use of all its diplomatic resources to ensure that the relationship with Morocco, a strategic partner for Spain and for the rest of Europe, continues to develop on the basis of transparency and mutual respect. While I advocate the need to establish a loyal and stable relationship with our neighboring country, I believe it is in the interests of the entire European Union to ensure that this relationship is not undermined by the exploitation of migration flows or by the questioning of the Spanish identity of Ceuta and Melilla, territories that are just as European as Berlin, Paris or Brussels.

World.title: Tories warn Burnham’s EU ‘pandering’ will shred post-Brexit trade deals
World.content:
Customs union membership — a popular option among some members of Burnham’s Cabinet — would ease trade between the U.K. and its largest trading partner, but require Britain to sacrifice the trade deals it has struck since leaving the bloc six years ago.

Greg Hands, who served as trade minister four times between 2016 to 2024 under Conservative governments, said that all options presented “grave consequences for Britain's independent trade policy.”

“Depending exactly on what is agreed, it is likely to invalidate or make very difficult most — if not all — of those existing trade agreements, or many of those existing trade agreements,” he said.

Since Brexit, the U.K. has negotiated free trade deals with nations including Australia, New Zealand, Japan and — more recently — the Asia Pacific trading bloc CPTPP, India, the Gulf states, as well as upgraded deals with South Korea and Switzerland.

Although the U.K. could technically copy-and paste EU versions of trade deals, Hands warned that the terms might not be so favorable, highlighting that the U.K.-Japan deal he had helped to negotiate “has got much more liberal rules on data” than the EU equivalent.

As a non-EU member, the U.K. would also surrender its ability to negotiate the terms of any new trade deals, Hands argued. “Why would the EU prioritize the U.K., which is not a paying member of the EU, over paying full members of the EU when it does trade agreements?”

World.title: Diesel : sous la pression des Etats-Unis, l’exécutif envisage de libérer une part importante de ses réserves
World.content:
L’Elysée a indiqué ce matin qu’Emmanuel Macron avait échangé pendant la nuit avec Donald Trump “pour évoquer la situation énergétique mondiale”, et notamment pour “garantir la disponibilité des produits raffinés au niveau mondial”. La France, qui assure la présidence tournante du G7 “entend réunir dans les meilleurs délais une visioconférence des dirigeants du G7 pour assurer la coordination des mesures à prendre afin de contribuer à desserrer l’étau des prix”.

Lors de l’échange ce vendredi matin, le gouvernement allemand s’est montré réticent à débloquer le moindre baril, selon ces sources. “L'Allemagne et d'autres pays ne veulent pas servir de pions ; ils souhaitent ne libérer leurs stocks que pour de véritables raisons de sécurité d'approvisionnement”, a déclaré l'une d'entre elles à POLITICO, s'exprimant sous couvert d'anonymat afin de pouvoir s'exprimer en toute franchise. L'Allemagne et la France disposent des plus importantes réserves de pétrole et de produits pétroliers en Europe, selon les statistiques officielles de l'UE.

“La France tient à participer et à répondre à cette demande [...] Il est clair que l’UE agira, dans la mesure où ses membres parviendront à s’entendre”, a déclaré une deuxième source. Elle a ajouté qu'il était difficile de savoir si cette libération serait coordonnée conjointement par l’UE ou menée sur une base bilatérale, compte tenu de l’approche “désordonnée” des Etats-Unis, qui ont adressé des demandes différentes à différents pays. “C’est une méthode typiquement américaine : ils ne passent pas par les voies officielles habituelles.”

Le cabinet du ministre Roland Lescure, présent à la réunion vendredi matin, a balayé auprès de POLITICO des “rumeurs” et ne souhaite pas commenter davantage.

Les Etats-Unis montrent une frustration croissante à l’égard des pays de l’UE qui n’ont pas tenu leurs engagements de contribuer à la mise sur le marché de 400 millions de barils, opération coordonnée en début d’année par l’Agence internationale de l’énergie à la suite du déclenchement de la guerre en Iran et de la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz.

Lors de la réunion qui s'est tenue vendredi à Bruxelles, certains représentants européens ont également critiqué la France et l'Allemagne pour ne pas avoir mis sur le marché des réserves pétrolières substantielles, selon l'une des personnes présentes.

POLITICO a rapporté jeudi que les principaux pays de l'UE et le Royaume-Uni souhaitaient répondre aux pressions américaines d'une voix « ferme », tout en cherchant à apaiser les tensions.

Nicolas Camut a contribué à cet article. Il a été initialement publié par POLITICO en anglais et adapté par Alexandre Léchenet.

World.title: The solar system will fall apart far sooner than anyone thought, scientists say
World.content:
The outer planets of the solar system will be thrown into chaos roughly a billion years after the Sun dies, a new study has found, cutting their expected life span a billion-fold.

 

Previous estimates put the stability of the giant planets' orbits at around a quintillion years, far longer than the current age of the universe.

Researchers at California’s Institute of Technology (Caltech) were investigating how the sun’s slow death would impact the outer planets including Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

It was also previously believed by many scientists, including Isaac Newton, that the sun would shed its mass smoothly as it slowly died, transitioning first into a Red Giant and later a White Dwarf.

Earth, Venus and Mercury would be the first to go, consumed by the Sun as it expanded into a Red Giant, with Mars the lone survivor, sitting far enough away to escape the engulfment.

Earlier studies found the outer planets would survive this process, with their orbits widening to about twice their current size as the Sun lost mass. Their eventual break-up was expected to come only from passing stars, over 30 to 100 billion years.

The new findings suggest this picture is wrong. Instead, the outer planets will be thrown into disorder roughly one billion years after the Sun becomes a white dwarf, which is still billions of years away.

When the Sun becomes a white dwarf, it rapidly cools and shrinks to half its current size, but this will not be a smooth process and previously thought.

The research argues the star will lose its mass in violent, random ejections known as “stochastic kicks,” rather than a calm, consistent release.

The new findings suggest this picture is wrong. Instead, the outer planets will be thrown into disorder roughly one billion years after the Sun becomes a white dwarf, which is still billions of years away.

The solar system is 4.57 billion years old, and the Sun has around five billion years left before it swells into a red giant. Scientists had long assumed the giant planets would outlast it by an almost unimaginable stretch of time.

The research was carried out using high-performance supercomputers and hundreds of advanced N-body numeral simulations, with no AI tools involved whatsoever.

The researchers programmed a virtual model of the solar system containing the Sun, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, which the supercomputers then calculated and simulated the velocity and position over billions of years.

What made this year analysis different from previous research was the scripting of the sun losing its mass as it died via random, violent, episodic bursts, with hundreds of different model iterations tested in order to come to a consensus conclusion.

The findings were reported in a study called ‘Terminal Instability of the Solar System Triggered by Stochastic Solar Mass Loss’, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

World.title: G7 agrees 100 million-barrel emergency oil release amid US pressure over diesel
World.content:
G7 countries have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves over four months in a coordinated effort to bring down soaring energy prices, with a particular focus on diesel.

 

The release will be coordinated by the International Energy Agency (IEA), with a substantial amount of diesel to be made available within the first 20 days, according to a G7 statement.

French President Emmanuel Macron, who currently holds the G7 presidency, said the countries had agreed to act together to ease pressure on energy prices.

"We will implement our commitments with a coordinated release through the IEA of 100 million barrels to begin immediately over four months," the statement said.

The move comes after growing pressure from Washington for countries to release strategic reserves as diesel prices rise and supplies tighten.

Earlier on Friday, the European Commission pushed back against what it described as US "threats" to force European countries to act.

Related France weighs emergency oil release as US pressure mounts ahead of G7 call

But an overnight call between Macron and US President Donald Trump appears to have helped push Paris towards action, amid concerns over the impact of a possible US diesel export ban.

The G7 package also includes measures to increase refinery output and a pledge not to restrict trade in energy and oil products between partner countries.

The 100 million barrels would amount to roughly 830,000 barrels a day if released evenly over four months.

But the impact will depend on how quickly countries release their stocks and how much of the oil can ultimately be turned into diesel.

Strategic crude releases do not immediately translate into extra diesel supplies. Refineries must first process the crude, with capacity, logistics and the type of crude available all affecting how much fuel reaches consumers.

The release could provide some relief ahead of winter, when demand for diesel and other refined products typically increases.
