World.title: US posts weak job growth data in September
World.content:
Washington – Employment in the United States grew by 29,000 jobs in September, missing analysts’ expectations significantly, with the unemployment rate rising slightly to 4.2 percent, government data showed on Friday.

Adding to the weak data, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) also revised down job figures for July and August by a combined 60,000 jobs, the department said in a statement.

The revision to July’s data showed that the world’s largest economy lost jobs that month, as opposed to posting a gain of 21,000 as previously reported.

The data comes ahead of key midterm elections in November where President Donald Trump’s Republican Party is facing a stern test over his handling of the economy.

Analysts polled by Dow Jones Newswires and the Wall Street Journal had expected the US economy to add 84,000 jobs in September.

– Health care leads –

Employment in most major sectors was largely unchanged, the BLS reported, with health care posting notable gains of 17,000.

The sector has propped up the labor market in the United States in the last year, as an aging population requires more care both in hospitals and at home.

Still, September’s gains in the sector were slower than its average monthly gain of 33,000 over the last year.

The financial sector continued its downward slide, losing 7,000 jobs in September and bringing its overall slump from a recent peak in May 2025 to 129,000.

Most of the losses in that sector have been among insurance companies.

– Fed implications –

Average hourly earnings for all employees were up 3.0 percent, the BLS said, with wages continuing to lag behind stubbornly high inflation — meaning most workers are seeing real wage losses.

Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren seized on the data to criticize Trump’s performance since taking office last year.

“Paychecks are growing at their slowest rate in nearly seven years, outside of the Covid-19 pandemic,” she said in a statement.

“Since the start of Trump’s war, real wages have fallen 0.7 percent as his failed agenda keeps pushing prices up,” she said, referring to the US war against Iran launched in late February.

The conflict has plunged the Middle East into violence and sent global energy prices skyrocketing, as Tehran’s retaliatory action has targeted Washington’s regional allies and choked a key trading route.

The data comes after the US Federal Reserve — which has a dual mandate to maintain inflation at a long-term two-percent target while ensuring maximum employment — raised interest rates last month to address high prices.

The US labor market has been largely in balance this year, with modest job gains and a relatively steady unemployment rate.

That steadiness has allowed the Fed to focus on the inflation side of its mandate, but any weakness in the labor market may give policy makers pause.

Raising interest rates tends to cool inflation but can also limit economic activity, which can affect the job market.

This week, two key Fed policymakers indicated that the central bank may not raise rates again at its October meeting, although markets continue to expect a further hike before the end of the year.

Friday’s jobs data “lends support to the less hawkish Fed officials that indicate no need to rush and deliver the next rate hike at the end of this month,” said Kathy Bostjancic, chief economist at Nationwide, in a note.

She added that this could release some pressure on bond yields — which have been spiralling in part due to expectations of interest rate hikes.

Nancy Vanden Houten at Oxford Economics, however, disagreed, expecting upside risks to inflation to continue to dominate Fed policymakers’ thinking.

“We think the upside risks to inflation are still a bigger concern for the Federal Reserve and expect they will raise rates at the end of the month,” she said.

World.title: Ethiopia’s conflict: the regional dimension
World.content:
Addis Ababa – Renewed fighting between the Ethiopian government and Tigrayan rebels has worsened regional tensions, with Ethiopia and Eritrea breaking diplomatic ties on Thursday.

Heavy fighting resumed between federal forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) last week, and fighting has been ongoing across several fronts in northern Ethiopia.

The geopolitics of the Horn of Africa are fiendishly complex, with shifting alliances and the involvement of many outside actors with conflicting interests.

Here is what is at stake for the countries concerned:

– Eritrea –

Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the TPLF, including with troops, which it has denied.

On Thursday, they expelled each other’s diplomats and shut down their respective embassies.

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and the two sides fought a brutal border war between 1998 and 2000.

Relations improved markedly with the rise of Ethiopia’s Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in 2018, and Eritrea even fought alongside Ethiopia during the last civil war against the TPLF in 2020-2022.

But relations have since cratered, with Eritrea fearing landlocked Ethiopia plans to invade and seize access to the Red Sea.

“The TPLF is silently allied with its former foe, Eritrea, with supply lines chiefly secured through Tigray’s northern border,” the Chatham House think tank said in a report.

Eritrea’s “priority is to keep war away from its own territory”, it added, before cautioning the country’s actions increase the risk of regional escalation.

– Sudan –

The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have close ties with the TPLF and Eritrea. Tigrayan fighters have reportedly fought with the SAF in Sudan’s civil war.

Ethiopia is accused of assisting the United Arab Emirates in supplying the SAF’s opponent, the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which it has denied.

Sudan was accused of funnelling weapons and supplies to the TPLF during the last war. There were clashes along the shared border in August, suggesting it remains an active concern for the Ethiopian government.

– Egypt –

Egypt is strongly opposed to Ethiopia’s new Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which it says will affect downstream Nile waters. It has forged closer ties with Eritrea and Somalia in an apparent anti-Ethiopia front.

Ethiopia expelled an Egyptian diplomat on Thursday, without giving a reason. Cairo responded by expelling an Ethiopian diplomat.

– United Arab Emirates –

The UAE has invested deeply across east Africa as it seeks security partnerships to counter rivals and control the Red Sea, as well as agricultural land, and investments.

It has been one of Abiy’s principal backers, giving him a $3 billion loan and investment package when he came to power in 2018, and building his giant new palace in Addis Ababa, as well as providing military drones and logistical support during the last civil war.

In return, it is alleged that Ethiopia has helped funnel arms to the UAE’s allies in Sudan, though that is denied by both countries.

– United States –

Washington was closely involved in the peace deal that ended the last civil war in 2022.

Its focus has lately been on the Red Sea — and its efforts to contain Iran and its proxies. As a result, it allowed sanctions on Ethiopia and Eritrea to end, with the ill-timed claim that the “national emergency… has expired”.

– Somalia –

Ethiopia’s relations with Somalia were ruptured in January 2024 when Addis Ababa signed a sea-access deal with the breakaway region of Somaliland.

Relations were ultimately restored with Turkish mediation and the deal with Somaliland seemingly put on the back burner.

World.title: Swiss president to quit government
World.content:
Geneva – Swiss President Guy Parmelin announced Friday that he will quit the government at the end of the year, in a sudden move after more than a decade of ministerial service.

Switzerland’s presidency rotates annually among the seven members of the government, called the Federal Council, of which Parmelin, 66, was the longest-serving minister.

Parmelin told a press conference in Bern that he had informed ministerial colleagues of his decision to step down on December 31.

“By then, it will have been 11 years since I was elected to this role, and the time has come for me to make way for new energy in these times of great uncertainty,” he said, admitting to feeling “a certain weariness”, while insisting he was not stepping down for medical reasons.

– Tariff tussle with Trump –

A pragmatist, Parmelin seemed to make more headway with US President Donald Trump than his predecessor Karin Keller-Sutter.

Trump shocked Switzerland in August 2025 when he announced 39-percent duties on imports of Swiss goods, among the highest in his global tariff blitz.

Parmelin, the economy minister, went to Washington three times in a bid to reduce the rate.

Eventually, Switzerland and the United States announced a declaration of intent to cut tariffs to 15 percent, with the Swiss vowing to invest $200 billion in the United States.

A winegrower by trade, Parmelin is from the French-speaking western canton of Vaud. He is from the hard-right Swiss People’s Party (SVP), which is the biggest in the country,

Parmelin was previously president in 2021 and took centre-stage as Switzerland hosted a summit in Geneva between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Joe Biden.

The president of the Swiss Confederation is first among equals on the Federal Council, chairs its meetings and typically represents the country in major domestic and international matters.

The position goes to whoever has had the longest run on the council without being president.

Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis will become president in 2027.

Parmelin joined the Federal Council in 2016 as defence minister and has held the economy brief since 2019.

The Federal Council seven seats are shared 2-2-2-1 among the four main political parties under a decades-old tacit agreement known as “the magic formula”.

Parmelin’s successor will come from the SVP. Candidates have until October 23 to come forward, and parliament will choose on December 9.

Parmelin will visit India for a three-day state visit from Monday.

World.title: Pilot in flydubai attack says could not let ‘all those people die’
World.content:
Dubai – An Indian pilot attacked by his co-pilot aboard a flight from the UAE to Israel said Friday that he “could not let all those people die”, in his first public remarks after he helped stop the plane from crashing.

His actions on Wednesday helped avert disaster when he managed to open the cockpit door despite suffering injuries, allowing passengers and crew to take control of the plane and make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

The co-pilot has been returned to the United Arab Emirates, where the incident is under investigation to determine any “terrorist activity or intent”.

The mostly Israeli passengers on the flight have been flown back to Israel on a replacement plane.

Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a call from his hospital bed that he knew he had to act quickly, saying his opening the cockpit door was a “last push” to get help.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said.

“I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience — 11 as a captain — described the moment he realised the plane was going down while he was lying injured.

He told Modi that during the ordeal, he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer dedicated to the deity Hanuman.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said.

He said years of aviation experience allowed him to understand what was happening even while he was wounded.

– ‘Kill me, kill me’ –

The circumstances of the confrontation are under investigation, but the co-pilot allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him wounded and triggering a struggle for control of the aircraft.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.

Modi said Machchhar’s actions helped save many lives and avert “a great tragedy”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier also credited Machchhar, as well as the flight’s passengers, with averting catastrophe.

US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that if Iran was found to be linked to the attack the country would be “hit very hard”.

Netanyahu has said the suspect had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination”.

“The attacker, he calls out to the aircrew, ‘Kill me, kill me’,” Netanyahu told US media, adding it was “clear he was suicidal”.

The Israeli leader identified the co-pilot as an Omani national and said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.

“We have constraints that say that you can’t have pilots from countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that,” Netanyahu told Fox News.

Flydubai has suspended flights to and from Israel since the attack, leaving some Israelis stranded in the UAE.

Israel’s flag carrier El Al is planning replacement flights to bring them home but was forced to cancel them Friday, saying Emirati authorities had not given landing permission.

“As soon as approval is received from the authorities, we are prepared to carry out the special flights to Dubai and return the Israelis home as soon as possible,” El Al said in an online notice.

World.title: Disney president says layoffs ‘extremely painful’ but necessary
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Walt Disney Company’s President Dana Walden said on Thursday that the company’s layoffs were “extremely painful” but necessary for its survival.

Disney has carried out several rounds of cost cutting measures in recent years to combat intense competition in streaming, while advances in AI tools have also become a cheaper production alternative for the billion-dollar company.

“We’ve exited colleagues who I’ve worked with for most of my career… It is in many ways a harsh reality,” Walden said during the Bloomberg Screentime conference in Los Angeles.

“It is extremely painful,” she added.

More than 300 people were laid off from Disney on Tuesday, most of whom work in human resources and information technology, according to US media reports.

It comes after Disney eliminated around 1,000 positions in April, primarily across the company’s marketing group, following the arrival of new chief executive Josh D’Amaro, trade media reported.

Walden said the company had also offered a group of executives “the opportunity to make their own decision around whether the timing was right to leave or to stay” as part of a voluntary retirement plan. It remains unclear if the latest wave of layoffs made use of the initiative.

“There is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Walden said about Disney and its competitors in the technology industry.

“Technology set their sights on our business, and we must survive and thrive and grow. And that’s what we’re going to do,” she said.

The Walt Disney company did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

World.title: Indian flydubai pilot opened cockpit door to save passengers
World.content:
New Delhi – Indian flydubai captain Smit Machchhar knew he had to act quickly after an alleged in-flight attack by his co-pilot, opening the cockpit door in a “last push” to get help and avert disaster, he said Friday.

“I was trying to save my own life, but I knew I could not let all those people die,” Machchhar said during a call from his hospital bed to Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, according to a video posted by the leader on social media.

The Boeing 737 flight to Tel Aviv, operated by Dubai-based flydubai, was carrying 174 passengers when the altercation took place on Wednesday.

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience — 11 as a captain — described the moment he realised the plane was going down while he was lying injured.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down. I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said.

“I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar told Modi that during the ordeal, he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer dedicated to the deity Hanuman.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said.

Machchhar said years of aviation experience allowed him to understand what was happening even while he was injured.

The circumstances of the confrontation are under investigation.

– ‘Very proud’ –

The co-pilot allegedly attacked Machchhar, leaving him wounded and triggering a struggle for control of the aircraft.

Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted — losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website — before eventually making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Modi said Machchhar’s actions helped save many lives and avert “a great tragedy”.

“You have done such a great thing that people across the country and around the world are eager to see you and speak to you,” Modi told him.

“You have truly made the whole country proud.”

Machchhar became emotional during the conversation, telling Modi that he felt proud of himself for the first time since the incident.

“I am feeling very proud right now. I had not felt proud of myself until now,” he said.

The pilot, his head wrapped in bandages, and with a breathing tube in his nose, said the path to recovery was long.

“I am not thinking of it as a wound, I am thinking of it as a journey,” he said.

“And it will take time, but I am very, very confident that I will recover.”

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier credited Machchhar, as well as the flight’s passengers, with averting catastrophe.

World.title: Iraq Football Association signs Hudl Wyscout deal to boost global scouting
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq Football Association (IFA) has secured an exclusive multi-year arrangement with Hudl to introduce Iraqi football on the Wyscout scouting platform for the first time, providing clubs and scouts across the globe more access to Iraqi players.

The agreement will apply to the Iraq Stars League, Iraqi Premier Division League, Iraq FA Cup, and Super Cup, as well as the Iraqi men’s, women’s, and junior national teams.

The agreement will make video and statistics from Iraqi tournaments accessible on Hudl Wyscout, a popular professional football platform for scouting, player recruiting, match analysis, and transfer market research.

The partnership might considerably improve Iraqi players’ international profile by enabling scouts and recruiting departments outside the country to analyze potential using the same platform used to evaluate players in football markets throughout the globe.

Iraqi clubs and coaches would now have access to analytic tools for evaluating matches and player performance, giving new resources for coaching and player development.

The deal is another step in the IFA’s attempts to modernize Iraqi football infrastructure and gain international exposure for local events.

For young Iraqi players in particular, participation on Wyscout may make it simpler for abroad teams and scouts to find and monitor rising potential without depending entirely on international competitions or national-team performances.

The partnership also connects Iraq’s local divisions to a larger digital scouting ecosystem, at a time when data and video analysis are becoming more essential in football recruiting.

For Iraqi football, the agreement opens up new avenues for homegrown talent to be noticed abroad, while also providing teams with access to professional scouting and analytical technologies used around the world game.

World.title: Iraq’s 80s smash burger restaurant expands to Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The popular Iraqi smash burger restaurant 80s has moved from Erbil to Baghdad, launching a new branch in Al-Yarmouk as the worldwide smash burger fad gains traction in Iraq.

The local eatery originally opened in Erbil’s Dream City before expanding to Baghdad’s Al-Yarmouk neighborhood, near the Four Streets area, this year.

80s is noted for its retro-inspired decor and Western-style smashed burgers, including the famous Oklahoma Burger and Truffle Mushroom Burger.

Smash burgers are created by pushing small slices of beef straight onto a hot heating surface, resulting in a browned and crispy skin.

The style has grown in popularity in large cities such as London, Dubai, and Los Angeles, fueling a surge of specialized independent burger eateries.

The concept’s introduction in Iraq reflects shifting preferences among younger Iraqi customers as well as a restaurant sector that is more impacted by global cuisine trends.

The growth of 80s is especially remarkable since it is a locally built restaurant rather than an international franchise, providing Iraqi customers with an alternative to the country’s worldwide fast-food corporations.

Baghdad has experienced an increase in the number of independent restaurants, cafés, and foreign dining concepts in recent years, thanks to increased security and new commercial projects that have reshaped the capital’s leisure and hospitality industry.

For 80s, the shift from Erbil to Baghdad provides the restaurant access to Iraq’s biggest metropolitan market while also introducing a cuisine trend that is already popular abroad to a larger Iraqi audience.

World.title: From papads to pitches: NCERT brings startup lessons to Class IX
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Seven women, Rs 80 in borrowed capital and a Mumbai terrace. That was how Lijjat Papad began in 1959. More than six decades later, the story will be used to teach Class IX students how an idea, however small, can grow into an enterprise.

NCERTâs new social science textbook has introduced a dedicated chapter on startups and entrepreneurship, taking students through the basics of identifying business opportunities, understanding markets and preparing a workable business plan.

The chapter is built around three broad questions â how entrepreneurship affects society and the economy, what the main functional areas of a business are, and how an effective business plan is prepared.

It also places these lessons in the context of Indiaâs startup journey. The book says the country had only around 350-400 startups about a decade ago, while the ecosystem has now expanded to nearly 2.3 lakh enterprises, making India the worldâs third-largest startup ecosystem. The broader policy push, it says, is to bring research, industry, startups and entrepreneurship onto a common platform.

Students are introduced to the building blocks of running a business â understanding market activity, spotting opportunities, assessing performance and planning before committing resources.





The chapter also brings artificial intelligence into the discussion, explaining how AI can assist in market analysis and business decision-making.

Alongside contemporary startup concepts, the book uses stories of Indian entrepreneurs to make the subject relatable.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

One of them is Mohan Singh Oberoi, who began his working life on a salary of Rs 50 and went on to become a pioneering figure in Indiaâs hospitality industry.

Born in Punjab in 1898, Oberoi mortgaged his wifeâs jewellery to buy his first hotel and later built a major hotel business.

The Lijjat Papad story, meanwhile, illustrates entrepreneurship at the other end of the scale. Seven homemakers living in a Mumbai chawl started making papads with borrowed supplies and a traditional recipe. With no factory, each woman took dough home in the morning, rolled papads while managing household work and returned the finished product by evening.

The lesson highlights how quality, organisation and persistence helped turn the modest venture into a widely recognised brand.

World.title: 2 Jharkhand yoga instructors killed in Vietnam road accident; bodies to be brought back on Oct 3
World.content:
The bodies of two yoga instructors from Jharkhand, who lost their lives in a road accident in Vietnam are likely to reach their home state on Saturday, officials told news agency PTI.

Sikha Lakra, who heads the Jharkhand Migration Cell under the Labour Department, said the bodies are expected to reach Kolkata by Friday evening. From there, they will be taken to Jharkhand by ambulance.

"The bodies are expected to arrive in Jharkhand on Saturday morning," Lakra told PTI.

According to PTI, the deceased have been identified as 24-year-old Raja Kumar of Ranchi and 25-year-old Vinay Kumar Rai of Jamshedpur.

Both were working as yoga instructors at Adi Yoga Academy in Da Lat city, Vietnam. The two died on September 25, after their two-wheeler collided with a car.

The families had earlier said they were unable to afford the cost of bringing the bodies back to India. Friends of the deceased and members of the Indian community living in Vietnam contributed money to cover the repatriation expenses, family members said.

World.title: 'Exceptional courage': Pilots body writes to PM Modi, requests bravery award for Smit Machchhar

NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) wrote to

on Friday seeking an appropriate national bravery award for flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, citing his âexceptional courageâ and professional conduct during the mid-air emergency on September 30.

The pilots' body said Machchhar, the pilot-in-command of flydubai flight FZ1073, was reportedly attacked by the first officer with a crash axe and sustained serious injuries during the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.

Despite being injured, Machchhar continued to discharge his responsibilities as pilot-in-command, maintained control of the aircraft and ultimately diverted it safely to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, FIP said.

"The Federation of Indian Pilots respectfully submits that acts of exceptional courage such as this deserve recognition at the highest appropriate level. We therefore request the Hon'ble Prime Minister's Office to kindly consider Capt. Smit for an appropriate National Bravery Award / national civilian recognition, in accordance with the applicable Government of India provisions and after due verification of the facts by the competent authorities," it said in a letter.





"Capt. Smit's actions demonstrate that, even when confronted with grave personal danger and serious injury, the responsibility of a true professional pilot remains firmly centred on the safety of those entrusted to his care," the pilots body said.

The organisation noted that 174 passengers and eight crew members were onboard the flight and said Machchhar's actions under extreme personal danger contributed to bringing the aircraft safely to an alternate airport.

FIP's appeal comes after Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora also wrote to PM Modi, urging the government to consider Machchhar for the Ashoka Chakra. Deora said the Mumbai-born pilot's actions demonstrated âcourage, selflessness and dutyâ in an extreme situation.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has busted an alleged India-Dubai extortion network linked to the Goldy Brar gang and arrested three operatives, foiling a plan to open fire at the residence of a Delhi businessman, news agency PTI reported citing officials said on Friday.The accused allegedly contacted businessman Praveen Jain through a UAE-based number on September 16 and demanded Rs 1 crore, while threatening his family with dire consequences. The caller allegedly claimed to be associated with gangster Goldy Brar.Jain received three missed calls around 8.15pm, following which his son Ayush received a call from the UAE number at around 9.27pm. A case was registered at Roop Nagar police station on September 17.Police said analysis of the communication trail showed that the calls were routed through virtual private server and data-centre infrastructure linked to the UAE.The investigation led police to Aarif alias Pistol, 32, who allegedly acted as a link between the Dubai-based callers and their associates in India. He was arrested from Ahmedabad's Vejalpur on September 24 with Gujarat Police's assistance.According to police, Aarif allegedly paid a Dubai-based associate, Aarish, to make the extortion call and instructed him to speak in Haryanvi to make it appear that the threat came from a local criminal.Police subsequently arrested Mubarik alias Gullu from Delhi on September 25. He allegedly helped plan the extortion attempt and arranged accommodation in Kirari for shooters who were to carry out the threat if the demand was not met.Police said intelligence inputs later indicated that the accused planned to fire multiple rounds at Jain's Roop Nagar residence and then repeat the extortion demand. Preventive arrangements were made at the house, foiling the alleged attack.During the probe, police found that the same UAE number was allegedly used to target another Delhi businessman in Rohini. On September 19, the younger brother of a construction businessman received two WhatsApp calls and a 37-second audio message from the number.The caller allegedly identified himself as Vikrant from Mahendergarh, claimed affiliation with the Goldy Brar gang and demanded Rs 1 crore within 48 hours, threatening firing and other consequences. A separate case was registered at Vijay Vihar police station on September 24.Police said four suspected shooters, two from Panipat and two from Khalapar in Muzaffarnagar, had allegedly been engaged to execute the threats. One of them, Nawab Ali alias Sonij, was apprehended on October 1 from a moving train near Rewari with the assistance of the Railway Protection Force, police said.Police said Aarif has been named in 12 cases registered between 2016 and 2026 at Kairana police station in Shamli, including cases related to attempt to murder, extortion, criminal intimidation, rioting and Arms Act offences.Police are now looking for the remaining accused and the Dubai-based caller. Investigators are examining communication records, digital evidence and financial transactions to establish the wider network and determine whether the group was involved in other extortion cases.

World.title: Asian Games silver medallist Sreeshankar targets gold in 2028
World.content:
Asian Games silver medallist long jumper M. Sreeshankar on Friday expressed confidence that his fourth career silver medal would eventually pave the way for a major gold, saying he hoped to achieve the feat in 2028.

Mr. Sreeshankar won the silver medal at the Asian Games in Japan despite suffering an injury during his fourth attempt.

Speaking to reporters at his residence after returning from Japan, Mr. Sreeshankar said his physical condition and preparation were good enough for an 8.20 m-plus jump, but a slip while attempting the distance affected his performance.

“My body condition was good. I had all the conditions required to jump 8.20 m-plus. So, during the jump aimed at reaching 8.20 m, my leg went a bit forward, and I suddenly slipped and fell like Superman,” he said.

Narrow margins

Mr. Sreeshankar said he had missed gold by very narrow margins on previous occasions but believed those experiences were leading him towards a major triumph.

“If I get a gold in 2028, then everything will be compensated, for sure,” he said.

Asked whether winning the medal was a stroke of luck, Mr. Sreeshankar said the difficult weather conditions had made the competition unpredictable. “Definitely. Because in these weather conditions, the performance could go either way. It was raining heavily, but alongside the rain, it was also humid. So, jumping above 8 metres gave me good confidence,” he said.

He said he had expected jumps in the range of 8.10 m or 8.15 m but felt his 8.07 m effort was satisfactory under the circumstances.

The heat, humidity and rain had caused cramps among several athletes, making the ability to adapt to the conditions crucial to winning a medal, he said. “In these major competitions, whoever can overcome and adapt to that particular situation gets the medal,” he said.

Mr. Sreeshankar noted that all five athletes in the competition had previously recorded jumps of around 8.30 m or 8.40 m, making it a closely contested event.

He said the athletes finishing behind him had recorded jumps of 8.05 m and 8.06 m, with the second, third and fourth positions separated by just one centimetre.

To avoid aggravating injury

Mr. Sreeshankar said his muscles began cramping from his third attempt, forcing him to approach the jump cautiously to avoid aggravating the injury.

“I only had the intention of just completing that jump. If I applied too much force, those cramped muscles might have led to further injury. So, I had to take that attempt very easily,” he said.

Palakkad MP V.K. Sreekandan and Palakkad MLA Ramesh Pisharody also visited Mr. Sreeshankar’s residence to congratulate him on his feat.

Narasipura Ring Road Junction, T. Narasipura, Suttur, Varuna and Hoshahalli.

From there, the route will proceed via Doctors’ Community Hall, Lalitha Mahal Road, Sangolli Rayanna Circle, MRC Signal and Karanji Lake Tank Bund Road before the race concludes on F.K. Irani Road.

The public has been requested to plan their journeys in advance, use alternative routes wherever possible, and follow instructions issued by traffic police and diversion signboards during the event.

Traffic advisory

In a separate advisory, the Mysuru City Police have asked the public to avoid the roads along the cycling route and connecting roads during the event.

The roads identified for avoidance by the City police are Devaraj Urs Road, JLB Road, Chamaraja Double Road, Nanjangud Road, Chamappaji Road, Chamundi Hill Road, Alanahalli Road, Lalitha Mahal Road and Karanji Lake Tank Bund Road.

“Traffic congestion is likely on roads connecting to and along the race route. To manage the movement of vehicles, the police have advised the public to use alternative roads during the event,” the statement said.

The public has also been requested to plan their journeys in advance and comply with the instructions of traffic police and traffic diversion arrangements during the cycling race.

Meanwhile, a statement from the organisers said Tourism Minister K.J. George would flag off the cycling series.

The 100-km Elite Men’s Race, the competitive category, will begin at 6 a.m., while the 100-km Open Race for men and women will be flagged off at 6.10 a.m. This will be followed by the 50-km Open Race at 6.45 a.m.

The 20-km Family Fun Ride will be flagged off at 7 a.m., while the 1-km Kids & Community Ride will begin at 9 a.m.

“Participants are being advised to arrive well in advance of their respective flag-off times to allow for check-in, preparation and access to the start area,” the organisers said.

The organisers said the event had attracted interest from both domestic and international riders, with entries received from riders from five countries — the United States, Australia, Mexico, Sri Lanka and France — besides participants from more than 12 Indian States.

The organisers expect the inaugural edition of L’Étape Mysuru to draw around 2,500 riders.

World.title: Semicon design firm Spintronics, CEERI ink pact for GaN tech
World.content:
Hyderabad-based Spintronics AI Semiconductors and CSIR-Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-CEERI) have signed an MoU to collaborate in the area of Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology.

A strategic technology and design transfer partnership focused on the technology has been signed, as part of the MoU, said Spintronics, announcing it is the first company in the country to enter into such a partnership with CSIR-CEERI.

Spintronics and CSIR-CEERI will assess feasibility of establishing an indigenous GaN technology development and fabrication facility in India. It will explore technology and infrastructure requirements, fabrication capabilities and potential pathways to strengthen domestic GaN semiconductor capabilities.

The collaboration will focus on transferring advanced GaN technology and design knowhow from research and development into an industry-led semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem, the company said in a release.

“India’s GaN semiconductor market is projected to grow from $224 million in 2026 to nearly $1.88 billion by 2033. This initiative can help India capture more of that value domestically,” said Spintronics founder and CEO Raghu Varma.

GaN is a next-generation semiconductor technology with applications across defence and aerospace, space systems, satellite communications, RF communications, advanced telecommunications, power electronics, electric mobility and other high-frequency uses.

“This collaboration will strengthen India’s indigenous GaN technology ecosystem,” said Manish Mathew, Scientist F, Head, Diamond Research Group, CSIR-CEERI, Pilani.

World.title: Where pens are passion, craft and collector’s pride
World.content:
The faint smell of fountain pen ink, the rustle of pen cases being opened and the animated chatter of collectors comparing nibs and finishes set the tone at a gathering in Hyderabad on Friday. Across two rooms, pens in an array of shapes, sizes and materials drew stylophiles into conversations about the craft, precision and pleasure of writing.

Pen sellers and manufacturers from across the country, including Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata, gathered at the Federation of Telangana Chambers of Commerce and Industry facility in Lakdi ka Pul here for the three-day Hyderabad Fountain Pen Show.

“These pens are expensive because they are made with a material called Urushi, a natural lacquer, that is secreted by the Urushi tree in Japan. It is rare as only 200 milliliters is secreted in a year and I use it to make the pens in Pune,” said Vivek Kulkarni, an attendee who showcased dozens of pens, while keeping three in a messenger bag.

“Each pen costs ₹7 lakh,” said a pen lover who had come for the event.

Hyderabad was represented by Poona Laxmi Pathi and his son, Poona Satish Kumar, who showcased their products under the PLP Pens brand.

“If a pen writes too smoothly, you have no control,” says Faheem Mohammed philosophically. Shaping the nibs to ensure smoother writing or repairing a vintage pen is his passion. “I worked with bikes. But when I wanted to get some of my Pelican pen nibs repaired, nobody understood. I took it up as a challenge and now I help others out. Very few people understand the geometry of the nib of a fountain pen,” he says, making a point about the shape of a pointed surface.

“Every pen we manufacture is unique. Store-bought pens may feel comfortable to hold or remain uncomfortable. Too thin or too fat. What we offer is customised grip where the buyer can choose pattern, material and even the shape of the grip,” said Amol Wankhede, who had brought his pen wares from Pune for sale.

Another pen seller from Tiruvallur near Chennai had pens crafted from Buffalo horn, acrylic, ebonite and a range of metals and bespoke styles.

Diya Vadodariya from Mumbai, who has been working and creating pens for the past eight years, showed the efficiency of titanium as a material for pen. “I have succeeded in making unique stacked nibs. They give a different line variation from different angles of writing and also allow a smoother flow of ink,” she said about the craft and ingenuity of her work.

Apart from Vadodariya of Acriv, craftspeople such as Chandru of Wonder of Writing and Amol Wankhede of Elica are reshaping the writing-instrument market by combining traditional craftsmanship with social media outreach. Their work is also tapping into a renewed appreciation for the tactile pleasure of writing with a carefully crafted pen.

World.title: A trip down memory lane for Australian grandson of Pudukottai’s former Diwan
World.content:
A chance query on Facebook brought Australian national Ian Kendall this week to Pudukottai, where his grandfather Sir Alexander Robert Loftus Tottenham served as the erstwhile princely state’s Administrator and Diwan from 1934 until his demise in 1946.

“We were overwhelmed by the friendly manner in which we were received in Pudukottai, and to find out about the work of Sir Alexander. We were not aware that he was so warmly appreciated by the people here,” Mr. Kendall told The Hindu over phone on Friday.

Over the past few days, Mr. Kendall, 73, and his wife Helen, visited Sir Alexander’s grave in Machuvadi and the Collectorate premises in Pudukottai.

The couple attended the birth anniversary programme of Rani Rama Devi Tondaiman, the erstwhile ‘Rajmatha’ of the then Pudukottai Samasthanam, hosted by her son Vijaykumar Tondaiman on October 1.

Among Mr. Kendall’s cherished memories of the Pudukottai visit is being photographed with the portrait of Sir Alexander at the Collector’s Bungalow.

An obituary of Sir Alexander Tottenham published by The Hindu on December 14, 1946, records that he joined the Indian Civil Service (ICS) in Madras Presidency in 1897 and remained there until 1923. He served as a member of the Central Board of Revenue and took an active interest in the archaeology of the Pudukottai state. After retiring from the Indian Civil Service, he became an Administrator of the Pudukottai during the minority of Rajagopala Tondaiman. When the ruler assumed full powers in 1944, he was assigned as the Diwan and continued in administration until 1946.

Paying tribute to Sir Alexander in a press communique, in 1946, the then Pudukottah Durbar said, “But for a spell of 10 months in England during these 13 years, he was always in Pudukottah and he had such love and affection for the people of Pudukottah that he was often saying that he would lay his bones only here.”

He was known for his work to reclaim lands affected by soil erosion, and the maintenance of irrigation systems in Pudukottai. The Tottenham filing system of official correspondence that he introduced is still in use in government offices in India, with an upgraded computerised version.

Family links

The Kendalls came to know of Sir Alexander Tottenham while trying to gather details about Mr. Ian’s father Robert, who migrated to Australia in the 1940s, and formalise the family tree.

While official records state that Sir Alexander was a bachelor, other biographical accounts of British administrators in India suggest that he had an Anglo-Indian spouse and two sons, Robert and Ginger.

“Vijaykumar [Tondaiman] replied to my niece Simone’s query about Sir Alexander on Facebook, and sent her a book that had some of his history related to my father and his brother. That’s when we decided to visit Pudukottai. We feel quite humbled that we got so much attention in the short time that we were here,” said Mr. Kendall.

“Alexander Tottenham had left an endowment of ₹10,000 that he had wished to be used for charitable work after his demise. This has been administered by our family over several years. We observe December 13 as ‘Tottenham Day’ in Pudukottai with a special prayer service in his memory and by rendering assistance to people in need,” Mr. Tondaiman added.

World.title: Spiritual guru Kalki Bhagavan laid to rest in Andhra Pradesh
World.content:
The mortal remains of spiritual guru Kalki Bhagavan were laid to rest on the premises of ‘Ekam – The Oneness Temple’, at Bathalavallam village of Varadaiahpalem mandal in Tirupati district on Friday.

Kalki Bhagavan, formerly known as Vijay Kumar Naidu, breathed his last in Chennai on September 29. The government decided to accord him a funeral with State honours.

Minister for Endowments Anam Ramanarayana Reddy, as State representative, placed a wreath on the mortal remains of Kalki Bhagavan and paid tributes. He also conveyed his condolences to the bereaved family members.

District Collector S. Venkateswar, Superintendent of Police L. Subbarayudu, Sullurpeta MLA Nelavala Vijayasri and MLC B. Kalyan Chakravarthy were among those present.

World.title: Inquiry by Coop Dept officer finds Shivamogga Brahmin Mahasabha spent funds violating by-laws
World.content:
The inquiry officer of the Department of Cooperation, who probed allegations against the Shivamogga District Brahmin Mahasabha, has submitted a report stating that the Sabha’s office-bearers spent funds in violation of its by-law, and that the amount can be recovered from members of the executive committee.

Following complaints by S.S. Srikanth of Shivamogga and Vinay S.V. of Sogane village near Shivamogga, Deputy Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Shivamogga, Nagabhushan C. Kalmane, ordered an inquiry into the Mahasabha’s activities on January 22 this year, under the Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960. Manjunath S., superintendent at the office of the Assistant Registrar of Cooperative Societies, Shivamogga sub-division, was appointed inquiry officer.

The complainants had alleged that the Mahasabha had taken up the management of Surabha Goshala at Mandenakoppa near Shivamogga, an activity not covered by the organisation’s registered objectives. They also alleged that the cow shelter had been established on government land without any formal lease or grant from the Revenue Department, and that the Mahasabha had collected substantial sums from members and the public and spent them on the goshala, in violation of its by-laws.

The inquiry officer submitted his report on September 21, after verifying the documents furnished by the complainants and seeking explanations from the Mahasabha’s office-bearers.

The report stated that the executive committee for 2016-21 violated the by-law by signing a memorandum of understanding with the Go Rakshana Nyasa Samiti of Mattur-Hosahalli to manage the goshala, without confirming the ownership of the land on which the goshala stands. The land, it noted, belongs to the government. The Mahasabha paid an annual rent of ₹72,000 to the Samiti although the land’s khata was not in the Samiti’s name. This amount can be recovered from the office-bearers of the executive committee, the report said.

The report further noted that the committee in office between 2016 and 2021 spent ₹50.36 lakh on constructing buildings at the go-shala, while the committee for 2021-26 spent another ₹64.14 lakh, raised from the public and other organisations. Terming the expenditure a misuse of funds, the inquiry officer held that the office-bearers had caused loss to the Mahasabha.

The inquiry officer observed that, though managing a goshala deserved appreciation, it was inappropriate to spend money raised from the public on land that did not belong to the organisation. The Mahasabha received ₹24.13 lakh as aid from the government to run the goshala and raised ₹1.62 crore from the public and organisations for the activity, the report mentioned.

Mr. Vinay, one of the complainants, told The Hindu that he was happy with the findings. “The report has confirmed our allegations. It has been submitted to the Deputy Registrar, who can initiate recovery proceedings and the appointment of an administrator. We will soon approach the officer to seek a recommendation for appointing an administrator, which has to be decided by the State Cabinet,” he said.

World.title: Dar says Makkah defence pact committee to meet next week on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that a meeting of Makkah Defence Alliance’s Strategic Political Defence Committee (SPDC) would take place in Riyadh next week, adding that it would focus on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

He made the remarks while addressing a press briefing detailing the Pakistan delegation’s engagements at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York in September, as well as high-level meetings that took place on its sidelines.

“We made a plan because all three of us countries were present [in New York],” Dar said, referring to himself, Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud.

He said the SPDC, established under the trilateral “Makkah Accord”, comprises three members from each country — the foreign ministers, defence ministers and chiefs of army staff.

On Sept 25, a special meeting took place of the three army chiefs in Riyadh, he said, adding that the foreign ministers had met prior to this in New York in the wake of increased Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

“Very soon, a meeting of the whole SPDC … has been agreed to in principle, to take place in Riyadh,” the deputy premier said, noting that the current situation and “ground reality” would be examined during the meeting, particularly vis-a-vis Saudi Arabia.

Responding to a question, Dar said that this upcoming meeting was an emergency one, and the committee would meet again as planned after “the end of October or beginning of November”, when its work was expected to be completed.

He said that the meeting would focus on the Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, as the previous meeting of foreign ministers in New York had done. Later, he said that the meeting would take place “next week”.

Regarding yesterday’s airstrike on a power plant in Madina, which was attributed to the Houthis, he highlighted that Pakistan had already condemned it and said it was “not acceptable”.

The deputy prime minister also noted that he had spoken to Iran in detail regarding the Houthi attacks, reminding them that Pakistan had its trilateral agreement to honour. Iran, he said, denied association “both with the Houthis and with the Iraqi militia”.

Iran also advised that the Houthis be “engaged politically”, rather than using “kinetic action”, he said, although he clarified that this was simply a “brainstorming between two foreign ministers, and in all good faith, a suggestion”.

He added that the decision would be taken between the three countries of the SPDC after the upcoming meeting.

Dar also stated, responding to a question about the potential expansion of the Makkah defence pact, that while he would not name them, “at least six countries” were keen to join the accord.

He added that this would not be possible until after the agreement was made “fully operational”, which would take at least a year, but stressed that the document of the accord itself stated that it would be open to other countries if they agreed to the principles laid down by the existing members.

Dar’s remarks come amid fresh fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis. The Houthis have declared a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeted its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

Meanwhile, the defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The first meeting of the SPDC was held in Istanbul on Aug 31, during which it was decided that the alliance’s secretariat will be initially headed by Pakistan for three years. Retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood has been appointed as the first secretary general of the alliance.

UN chief to visit Pakistan before end of tenure

During the briefing, the foreign minister also said that UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres would visit Pakistan “soon”, likely before the end of his tenure.

He said that the UN chief held a meeting with the Pakistan delegation at the UNGA session, adding: “We have invited him to Pakistan and the UN secretary general has accepted.”

Calling Guterres a great supporter of Pakistan, the deputy premier recalled the “unforgettable” role he played in aiding the country through calamities.

He added that the UN chief’s term will end on Dec 31 of this year, and said that the visit would “likely” take place before this.

He noted that the programme for the visit would be released by the government and would take place “very soon” on the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

“I think it will be a memorable visit,” Dar added.

During the premier’s meeting with Guterres on the sidelines of the UNGA last week, the two exchanged views on major regional and international developments. The UN chief also commended Pakistan’s role in the Middle East peace process, according to the Prime Minister’s Office.

World.title: 2 civilians martyred in firing by Indian forces near Kasur border: state media
World.content:
State-run Radio Pakistan reported on Friday that two unarmed Pakistani civilians were martyred and another was injured in firing by India’s Border Security Force (BSF) near the border in Kasur.

Citing security sources, the report said that three residents of Ladhar village went a few steps ahead of a border pillar when the BSF “opened fire on them without warning”.

“The sources said two civilians were martyred while another sustained injuries in the firing. All three individuals were unarmed,” the report said.

It identified the deceased as Azmat Rasool and Mohsin Jutt, both residents of Jattan Wali Haveli, Ladhar.

“The security sources further said that none of the three individuals had attempted to cross the border fence. They said the incident constitutes a violation of the border agreement and the standard operating procedures governing the Pakistan-India international border,” the report added.

“Indian media, while continuing its tradition of a false-flag narrative, labelled the innocent civilians as alleged infiltrators,” the report said.

The development comes a day after Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry lampooned India’s claims of “neutralising” a “terrorist” allegedly linked to the Pakistani military, presenting the individual during a press conference.

Asked whether the recent allegations could trigger another armed conflict between the neighbours during the press briefing, he affirmed that Pakistan’s armed forces were always ready for any such move and warned of “very harsh” retribution.

World.title: Army's top brass warns of 'decisive force' against any 'May 9-like situation'
World.content:
The army’s top brass on Friday warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”, according to the military’s media wing.

The warning came during the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference in Rawalpindi, which was presided over by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.

“[The] forum underscored the importance of internal stability and resolved that any attempt to cause agitation or create [a] May 9-like situation, on any pretext whatsoever, will be dealt with decisive force and rule of law, without hesitation and discrimination,” a statement from Inter-Services Public Relations said.

The warning comes as the PTI is gearing up for a long march to Islamabad, to demand the release of former prime minister and party founder Imran Khan. The protest was originally scheduled for Sept 27 but was postponed to Oct 4.

The party is currently in talks with the government over its long march, with the first round of dialogue taking place earlier in the day.

It is worth mentioning that Imran’s arrest on May 9, 2023, had triggered widespread riots across Pakistan, during which government buildings and military installations — including the GHQ in Rawalpindi — were stormed and vandalised. Following the unrest, a crackdown was launched against the PTI, with dozens of terrorism cases lodged against its leaders and supporters.

Need for ‘targeted action’ against Afghanistan stressed

According to ISPR, the forum also reviewed the security landscape and resolved to maintain a “high state of readiness”. It hailed successful counter-terrorism operations, but stressed the need to blend kinetic and non-kinetic measures.

These included “people-centric governance at [the] grassroot level, strategic engagement with [the] public, dismantling of [the] terror-crime nexus operating under patronage of vested interests and police capacity building, in line with the National Action Plan and Vision Azm-i-Istehkam”.

Affirming Pakistan’s right to self-defence, the forum noted the need for “targeted action” against terrorism emanating from Afghanistan, stressing that “only the Taliban’s delusional leadership, facilitating terrorism on behalf of India, bears responsibility for its consequences”.

Since Sep 21, in the aftermath of terror incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan has carried out three strikes in Afghanistan, targeting terrorist hideouts.

A day earlier, ISPR Director General Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan had the right to self-defence and “everything that is necessary will be done” in response to terrorism emanating from Afghanistan .

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia condemned

The army huddle on Friday also welcomed the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye and its contribution to “longstanding strategic and collective defence ties”, the statement read.

“It (the forum) strongly resented Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, expressed solidarity with the kingdom and affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to the security and sanctity of the Haramain Sharifain,” ISPR added.

The defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Fresh fighting between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea. Both sides have claimed strikes on each other as tensions remain high.

The Corps Commander Conference on Friday also reiterated Pakistan’s position on Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir and expressed support for resolving the Kashmir dispute, in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

In his concluding remarks, CDF Munir commended the formations for their operational preparedness and professionalism, directing the commanders to bolster intelligence-based operations and enhance combat capabilities through the adoption of modern technology, training and multi-domain integration.

“He expressed confidence that the armed forces, with unwavering support of the nation, remain fully prepared to safeguard Pakistan’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national security,” ISPR said.

The forum also offered prayers for the martyrs of the armed forces, law enforcement agencies and civil society and paid tribute to their sacrifices.

World.title: First round of talks between govt, opposition end as PTI’s Oct 4 protest looms over Islamabad
World.content:
The first round of talks between the PTI-led opposition and the ruling coalition over the party’s proposed Oct 4 long march concluded on Friday, with both sides agreeing to resume the dialogue on Saturday.

The meeting between government and opposition representatives, chaired by National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq, was aimed at defusing the country’s ongoing political crisis. It comes ahead of the the PTI’s planned Oct 4 protest march demanding the release of party founder Imran Khan, which has emerged as the latest point of contention between the party and the federal government.

According to a statement issued by the NA Secretariat, the participants held detailed discussions “on the prevailing political situation and exchanged views on various matters of national importance”.

“The government, PPP and opposition representatives apprised each other of their respective positions and held a detailed exchange of views in a constructive and cordial manner. The participants emphasised the need to resolve national issues through dialogue and negotiations,” it said.

The statement added that the second round of talks would be held on Saturday at 2pm in the NA speaker’s chamber.

“NA Speaker Sadiq played a key role in facilitating dialogue among the government, PPP and opposition,” the statement said.

The delegations were welcomed by Speaker Sadiq upon their arrival. “I am only playing the role of a mediator,” he said.

Sadiq said his office was “always open” to resolving issues through negotiations and that he had consistently invited the opposition to engage in dialogue. He maintained that negotiations were the only way to resolve differences and issues, adding that positions and offices were temporary.

“Parliament is the only forum where solutions to issues can be found,” he said.

In an earlier post on X, the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan said the opposition side was being led by the leader of the opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas.

Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry attended the meeting, along with PPP Senator Sherry Rehman and National Assembly members Syed Naveed Qamar and Ejaz Hussain Jakhrani.

The opposition was represented by PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Khan, Abbas, Amir Dogar, former NA speaker Asad Qaiser and PTI General Secretary Salman Akram Raja.

As the PTI remains resolute to go ahead with the march, federal ministers have warned that the Centre would have no other option but to impose governor’s rule or emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in light of the security situation in the province and the PTI’s protest call.

For its part, the opposition party has warned the government of dire consequences if such a decision is imposed.

‘PTI will have to call off its march’

Speaking to the media after the meeting, PPP’s Rehman said the party believed in resolving issues through negotiations.

She said that PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had stated the party’s stance on the long march and that the PTI had to call it off “unconditionally”.

“They will have to call it off rather than postponing or deferring,” she said.

“Both parties have time; we will meet tomorrow. We will try to conclude this by tomorrow,” she stated.

Talking about the opposition’s reported demand of facilitating a meeting with incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, she said she could not answer the question. However, she said the opposition had asked for time and “we should respect it”.

“A political and democratic attitude requires sitting at the negotiation table and resolving the issues through dialogue,” she stated.

Later, Bilawal welcomed the government’s decision to work with his party and jointly engage with the opposition “to find political solutions to political problems”.

“The challenge of terrorism has become an existential threat to Pakistan, particularly given the active support these groups receive from neighbouring countries,” he wrote on X.

The PPP chief expressed hope that the talks would conclude with the opposition unconditionally calling off the long march, which would allow the country to come together to address the threat of terrorism and those from neighbouring countries.

“The PPP has been, and will always remain, committed to combating terrorism through any and all constitutional means,” he added.

‘Govt should engage with integrity’

The Senate opposition leader, speaking to the media at his office during a break in talks with the government, said the government should engage with the opposition “with integrity” and take steps towards resolving the issues.

“If the government cares about the political crisis, then it should sit with the opposition with integrity and step forward to find a solution,” Abbas said.

Regarding PTI’s long march, he said the call would remain “intact” until a solution was found.

“Negotiating is the way of political leaders; negotiations could resolve gigantic issues and war,” he said, adding that “it, however, depends on the government’s intention”.

He questioned whether the government, as the other party to the negotiations, genuinely wanted to resolve the issues.

“They are in government and it is their responsibility to maintain peace, resolve crises, and ensure economic stability,” he said.

Abbas reiterated that the outcome depended on how “autonomous” the government was and whether it had the “intent” to pursue negotiations.

Speaking to the media after the talks, PTI Chairman Gohar said that both parties had shared their stances on “all the issues”.

Regarding negotiations with the government, he added that “Abbas and Mehmood Khan Achakzai have the mandate for these things”.

During an opposition alliance meeting yesterday, he said, the party had decided to attend the talks with the government and give their stance if it called on the opposition.

“The positive aspect of this talk is that it is still continuing and we’ll meet again tomorrow,” he said, adding that tomorrow’s talks would be held by the same opposition committee that held them today.

Asked what the party would do if the PTI were to gain access to Imran and he were to once again call for a long march, he said: “We always act upon the directions given by Khan sahab.”

A day earlier, it emerged that a joint delegation of the PPP and the government would hold a meeting with the PTI leadership on Friday, during which the “current political situation” in the country would be discussed with the opposition.

The decision came after a meeting at President House attended by President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and other party leaders.

Sanaullah also said on Thursday that the federal government and PTI were engaged in “off-the-record talks” regarding PTI’s planned protest.

Sanaullah said that the decision on the proposed march rested with PTI’s senior leadership, “with whom off-the-record consultation is ongoing”.

“So let us see, even if they do not postpone it, we have arrangements in place to stop them,” he warned.

World.title: Mexico to prohibit presidents from holding dual citizenship
World.content:
A Mexican constitutional reform to require presidential candidates to renounce any dual citizenship is fast-tracking toward final approval, despite criticism that the measure backed by the ruling party infringes on political rights and aims to block opposition rivals.

President Claudia Sheinbaum has defended the initiative, which would also apply to state governors and the Mexico City mayor as a safeguard against foreign interference.

“Presidents of Mexico can only have one flag, one homeland, one people to defend,” Sheinbaum said during her daily news conference on Wednesday.

Its critics, however, say it erects hurdles for dual-national politicians and could hamper generational succession within Sheinbaum’s ruling Morena party and those of its allies, where several figures hold foreign passports.

The constitutional changes were swiftly approved this week by a majority of Mexico’s 32 state legislatures, backed by Morena lawmakers and their coalition after passing both chambers of the national Congress. Lawmakers must now issue a formal “declaration of constitutionality” before publishing the text in the official gazette.

Mexico’s current constitution does not explicitly bar presidents and governors from holding dual citizenship. In Latin America, only two countries have such bans: Cuba and Venezuela.

The United States allows dual citizens to become president, but the issue has proven politically sensitive. Ted Cruz renounced his Canadian citizenship in 2014 ahead of his 2016 presidential run.

Patriotism or political subterfuge?

Sheinbaum and her administration say that the citizenship proposal is part of the party’s broader emphasis on defending national sovereignty amid mounting pressure from the administration of US President Donald Trump.

But its critics have questioned both the speed of its passage and its political intentions ahead of the 2030 presidential election. The requirement would take effect for prospective candidates in 2028, meaning it would not affect current state governors or candidates competing in the 2027 midterms.

Sheinbaum’s office did not respond to requests for comment.

Mexican billionaire Ricardo Salinas, a prominent tycoon and fierce critic of the administration who has repeatedly hinted at political ambitions, has railed against the bill and suggested that it was designed specifically to thwart his possible run.

“Are they willing to screw over millions of Mexicans who migrated north… solely out of a sick desire to block a Mexican whom they fear and hate from the presidency?” Salinas wrote in a social media post in August.

On Monday, Salinas appeared to reverse course, writing on social media that he did not hold dual citizenship; Reuters could not confirm whether he holds a second citizenship.

A spokesperson for Grupo Salinas declined to comment, describing his citizenship status as a private matter.

A source within the Morena party, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters the reform was aimed at hampering a possible run by Salinas.

Larry Rubin, president of the American Society of Mexico, who holds dual US and Mexican citizenship, has also condemned the measure.

“Having two nationalities does not make anyone less Mexican,” Rubin said. “Do not turn your back on millions of dual nationals, migrants, and binational families.”

Mexican ambassador to the United States, Roberto Lazzeri, however, said the measure is not a referendum on dual citizenship, but rather a specific tightening of the requirements for the highest political offices.

“Holding dual nationality does not make anyone less Mexican,” he wrote on social media on Tuesday, though he added, “the greater the public responsibility, the greater the obligations toward the country.”

World.title: World Bank calls on govt to implement policy actions under $20bn reform partnership
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The World Bank on Friday called upon the government to expedite implementation of policy actions under its $20 billion economic reform partnership for harmonisation of sales tax, provincial agriculture and property taxes and removing regulatory constraints to achieve higher growth, revenue mobilisation and trade and investment facilitation.

The World Bank group launched the 10-year country partnership framework 2025-35 in January last year, with a total blended financing of about $20bn, involving concessionary and commercial lending facilities. It is now pursuing the implementation phase of the agreed reform agenda.

A bank delegation, led by its country director Bolormaa Amgaabazar, had a meeting with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb on Friday to review progress under the ongoing economic reform partnership, said a statement issued by the Ministry of Finance.

The delegation discussed implementation priorities across growth, jobs, fiscal management, revenue mobilisation, capital-market development, trade and investment, and institutional reforms.

According to the ministry, the meeting reviewed the World Bank’s support for Pakistan’s broader economic reform agenda, with particular emphasis on translating reform priorities into targeted, implementable actions and strengthening coordination among relevant ministries, provincial governments and implementing agencies.

The two sides agreed on moving from reform design to effective implementation, with a focus on practical measures capable of delivering measurable improvements in economic activity, investment, jobs and the overall business environment, the statement said.

The meeting discussed the proposed World Bank growth and jobs operation, including interventions aimed at improving the investment climate, access to finance, sectoral productivity and labour-market outcomes.

During the meeting, the World Bank outlined proposed measures relating to the investment framework, reduction of regulatory and business constraints, access to finance for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and development of export-finance products for the EXIM Bank of Pakistan to support incremental trade flows, the statement said.

The ministry said that the discussion also covered reforms to strengthen the Prime Minister’s Access to Finance initiative, including a unified insolvency framework, factoring legislation and regulations to support SME financing, as well as measures to expand commercial financing and greater private-sector participation.

On sectoral reforms, the World Bank highlighted proposed interventions in pharmaceuticals and medical products, and agriculture, including improvements in seed registration, deregulation of selected commodities and strengthening of international accreditations to facilitate participation in international procurement and markets.

“The meeting also reviewed initiatives to strengthen skills development and labour-market alignment, including improvements in the national vocational qualifications framework, greater international recognition of skills and development of formal overseas migration pathways supported by digital platforms,” it said.

According to the statement, the finance minister and the World Bank delegation reviewed implementation of the National Tariff Policy and ongoing analytical support for tariff reforms, including work relating to the automotive sector and future tariff reforms.

“The discussion emphasised the importance of supporting competitiveness, productivity, investment, exports and Pakistan’s greater integration into global value chains.”

On fiscal and revenue reforms, the meeting reviewed World Bank technical assistance to strengthen tax-policy capacity, including support for the medium-term revenue strategy and revenue-policy modelling, the statement said. It added that discussions also covered general sales tax harmonisation, including greater alignment of rules, definitions and classifications for services, improved federal-provincial coordination and stronger data-sharing arrangements.

The ministry said that the meeting between two sides also reviewed progress on agricultural income tax reforms, including implementation of amended provincial laws and rules and digital systems for registration, filing and payment.

“The importance of strengthening compliance and federal-provincial data sharing was also discussed.”

It added that the discussion further covered provincial property-tax reforms, including efforts to improve and harmonise property-valuation approaches, strengthen digital systems and progressively move towards more market-based valuation frameworks.

On domestic capital markets, the meeting discussed World Bank’s support for developing a roadmap for capital-market reforms through the Capital Markets Development Council, aimed at deepening domestic capital markets, broadening financing avenues and strengthening the ecosystem for investment and capital formation, the ministry said.

“The meeting also reviewed World Bank support for public-sector efficiency and the government’s rightsizing agenda, including technical assistance to strengthen institutional effectiveness and improve the efficiency of public resources,” it stated.

During the meeting, the finance minister highlighted the importance of strengthening debt-management capacity and domestic bond markets.

“Discussions covered ongoing technical cooperation on financial instruments for managing market risks, domestic bond-market development and strengthening investor-relations capacity.”

Meanwhile, the meeting also discussed the World Bank’s analytical support on Pakistan’s sovereign credit profile and the pathway towards further rating improvements.

Per the statement, the finance minister said the government would work diligently to strengthen both the quantitative and qualitative drivers of sovereign ratings, including fiscal and debt sustainability, external buffers, sustainable growth, institutional effectiveness and continued structural reforms, while deepening engagement with relevant stakeholders to support further improvement in Pakistan’s sovereign credit standing.

The World Bank delegation also briefed the finance minister on analytical work on governance and institutional effectiveness, with discussions focused on practical and measurable reforms to strengthen government effectiveness, regulatory quality, transparency, accountability and the overall business environment.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to continued cooperation under the economic reform partnership, with a shared focus on implementation, institutional strengthening, private-sector-led growth, improved public-resource management, stronger investment and enhanced economic opportunities,” the statement concluded.

World.title: Fighting Pakistan go down to Vietnam in final ASEAN Cup match
World.content:
Pakistan ended their FIFA ASEAN Cup campaign with a fighting 4-2 defeat against Vietnam at the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta on Friday.

Nolberto Solano’s side, ranked 99 places below Vietnam in the FIFA rankings, took the lead through a superb first-half goal from Mohibullah but could not withstand a second-half onslaught from their opponents.

Long Hai Nguyen, Duc Hoang Nguyen and Bac Dinh Nguyen scored to put Vietnam 3-1 ahead before veteran Kaleemullah Khan pulled one back for Pakistan in the 88th minute. Hoang Minh Williams restored Vietnam’s two-goal advantage in stoppage time.

The result left Vietnam second in Division I Group ‘B’ behind Thailand, with the Philippines third and Pakistan finishing with one point from their three matches in their maiden FIFA competition.

Pakistan had come from two goals down to draw 2-2 with the Philippines in their previous match and needed a victory against Vietnam to have any chance of reaching the bronze-medal match.

They dominated the opening half and deservedly went into the break ahead.

Ali Akbar Khan combined with Abdul Samad Shahzad in the opening minutes before his effort inside the box was blocked. Shayek Dost then headed wide in the fifth minute after another promising move through midfield.

Vietnam gradually settled into the game and Yousuf Butt was forced to make a save from a deflected effort, but Pakistan continued to threaten through Ali Akbar and Abdul Samad, who operated down the flanks.

Abdul Samad saw his effort saved before Pakistan took the lead in the 31st minute.

Mohibullah pressed a Vietnam centre-back into a mistake, won possession and kept his composure to slot the ball under goalkeeper Patrik Giang Le.

Vietnam nearly equalised before the break when Hoang Minh Williams fired into the side-netting.

Solano introduced Alamgir Ghazi and Umer Nawaz at the start of the second half, replacing Ali Agha and Shayek, but Vietnam quickly turned the game around.

Long Hai Nguyen levelled in the 50th minute, receiving a through ball down the left, cutting inside and firing past Yousuf.

Seven minutes later, Duc Hoang Nguyen completed another attacking move by striking a cutback first time to put Vietnam ahead.

Pakistan responded as Abdul Samad Shahzad saw his effort blocked before being replaced by Abdul Samad Khan. The substitute then delivered a cross from which Umar headed over.

Vietnam extended their lead in the 80th minute when Bac Dinh Nguyen raced onto a long ball and fired past Yousuf.
